mkncGn42Ir.one_liner: Distills diffusion and flow models by predicting several denoising steps per network evaluation with a single regression loss.
mkncGn42Ir.problem: Few-step distillation of video diffusion models relies on VSD and adversarial losses that are hard to optimize, suffer mode collapse, and reduce video diversity and motion.
mkncGn42Ir.method: Parallel Decoding Distillation (PDD) is a trajectory-based distillation with block designs and a student predictor head that predicts multiple denoising steps per evaluation. It learns a representation of the mean velocity without regressing its derivative via JVPs or finite differences and supports variable NFE.
mkncGn42Ir.key_idea: Predict mean velocities for multiple denoising steps in parallel with an on-policy regression objective, avoiding JVPs, finite differences, VSD, and adversarial losses.
mkncGn42Ir.evidence: LTX-2.3 text-to-video/audio, Wan 14B text-to-video, and Qwen-Image text-to-image, evaluated with automated metrics and an AI-based judge per reviews.
mkncGn42Ir.claimed_gains: Reports leading results at 4-8 NFE on LTX-2.3, Wan 14B, and Qwen-Image, plus a significant improvement in generated video diversity.
mkncGn42Ir.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple (one regression objective, no JVP, VSD, or adversarial training), supports flexible NFE, and shows strong, broad results with preserved diversity on large image, video, and audio-video models.
mkncGn42Ir.main_concern: Methodological novelty over Pi-Flow is insufficiently justified, and perceptual evaluation (no human study) and the extreme low-NFE regime are limited.

zlF4nBSJba.one_liner: Pipeline that generates verifiable multi-agent conflict tasks for computer use, with graders compiled from executed reference trajectories.
zlF4nBSJba.problem: Existing computer-use benchmarks assume consistent, cooperative environments, while real peers report outdated states or contradictory instructions, and unconstrained LLM task generation causes narrative drift, answer leakage, and unsatisfiable grading rubrics.
zlF4nBSJba.method: CLASHarness combines hierarchical scenario planning with an eight-step verified micro-pipeline that pre-commits decisive visual facts before rendering and compiles hybrid code and semantic graders directly from executed reference trajectories, so every task is solvable by construction. It yields a benchmark of 600 multi-round tasks used to evaluate 15 VLMs.
zlF4nBSJba.key_idea: Commit the decisive visual facts before rendering a scenario and compile graders from an executed reference trajectory so the task is solvable by construction.
zlF4nBSJba.evidence: A 600-round benchmark evaluated on 15 VLMs, with analyses of failure modes, resolving versus investigating conflicts, inference cost, and step budgets.
zlF4nBSJba.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the setting of conflicting peer information is timely and missing from current computer-use benchmarks, and that the generation pipeline addresses known failure modes of LLM-generated benchmarks in a principled way.
zlF4nBSJba.main_concern: The 'solvable by construction' guarantee is not fully supported, since some checks are unreachable or unfair, no task was checked by a human, and the model comparison mixes step budgets (40 versus 20 steps).

sRFfu07zKr.one_liner: Characterizes minimax excess abstention risk for binary classification under class-conditional error constraints and gives a surrogate-loss algorithm.
sRFfu07zKr.problem: Minimizing abstention while keeping both class-conditional errors below prescribed thresholds lacks a distribution-free minimax rate and a computable formulation for models such as neural networks.
sRFfu07zKr.method: They characterize the distribution-free minimax rate of excess abstention risk, up to logarithmic factors, in terms of hypothesis class complexity and sample size, then introduce surrogate-loss formulations with finite-sample guarantees on excess surrogate ambiguity risk. The learning task is posed as a constrained optimization problem whose computational complexity is characterized in the convex setting.
sRFfu07zKr.key_idea: Replace the 0-1 abstention objective with a surrogate-loss constrained optimization problem on ambiguity risk, subject to constraints on both class-conditional errors.
sRFfu07zKr.evidence: Minimax bounds for the 0-1 loss, finite-sample surrogate guarantees, and experiments on various datasets against a competing method (the Lei 2014 approach, per reviewers).
sRFfu07zKr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and gives a complete, sound story from 0-1 loss generalization and a lower bound to a surrogate loss and optimization, as a natural extension of Lei (2014).
sRFfu07zKr.main_concern: The baseline comparison does not isolate the benefit of the proposed method because the Lei (2014) baseline is underspecified, and the techniques follow standard Rademacher and VC-style analysis with limited new ideas.

faABsoUN7r.one_liner: Asynchronous Restoration Attribution scores attention-head importance in diffusion LLMs by averaging over paths restoring heads on independent schedules.
faABsoUN7r.problem: Head importance in diffusion LLMs changes with available context across denoising stages, so a single global ranking and synchronized restoration can miss interaction-dependent contributions.
faABsoUN7r.method: Uses masking rate as a proxy for denoising stage and averages head contributions over paths that gradually restore suppressed head outputs under independently sampled schedules, then applies the scores to dynamic pruning and adaptive sparse attention.
faABsoUN7r.key_idea: Restore each head's output on independently sampled schedules so every head is evaluated while others sit at different restoration levels, capturing head interactions.
faABsoUN7r.evidence: Experiments on two DLLM families (LLaDA and Dream per reviews) across eight tasks, using removal of top-ranked heads and keep-only-top-heads tests, with comparisons such as CoKV.
faABsoUN7r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation and the asynchronous versus synchronized illustration are clear and the method is validated across two models and eight benchmarks.
faABsoUN7r.main_concern: Uniform masking rate may not match real denoising trajectories, and the method looks generic to attention models rather than specific to diffusion language models.

OUMKQPvct3.one_liner: ConstraintGS attenuates opacity of weakly constrained Gaussians using a cross-view descriptor of rendering support and viewing-direction coverage.
OUMKQPvct3.problem: Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting overfits, and supervision is unevenly distributed so individual Gaussian primitives receive different amounts and directional distributions of rendering support.
OUMKQPvct3.method: Builds a self-opacity-normalized cross-view descriptor combining support magnitude and directional coverage, which allocates opacity attenuation under a mean budget and per-primitive bounds, and plugs into existing pipelines without changing inference.
OUMKQPvct3.key_idea: Score each Gaussian by a self-opacity-normalized descriptor of support magnitude and directional coverage, then allocate bounded opacity attenuation, strongest for weakly constrained primitives.
OUMKQPvct3.evidence: Experiments on three widely used benchmarks across multiple Gaussian splatting host methods (FSGS, CoR-GS, DropGaussian and others per reviews), with an ablation of each design choice.
OUMKQPvct3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is principled and analysis-motivated, needs no extra learned model, and applies easily to existing pipelines with strong results.
OUMKQPvct3.main_concern: Empirical gains are inconsistent across metrics and datasets, with SSIM or LPIPS worsening for several host methods even when PSNR improves.

ZD2jXlzQ4b.one_liner: CurvSpread adds the exponential-map Jacobian to a spacing-entropy surrogate and sets confinement from curvature for hyperbolic graph self-supervision.
ZD2jXlzQ4b.problem: Dispersion prevents collapse in self-supervised learning, but hyperbolic space has no finite radius at which spreading naturally stops.
ZD2jXlzQ4b.method: Contrasts wrapped and intrinsic spreading laws, shows an intrinsic law has a finite equilibrium exactly when the confinement coefficient exceeds the volume-growth rate (d-1)sqrt(kappa), and builds CurvSpread by adding the exponential-map Jacobian to a local-spacing entropy surrogate with confinement calibrated to that rate.
ZD2jXlzQ4b.key_idea: Calibrate radial confinement to the hyperbolic volume-growth rate (d-1)sqrt(kappa), so the finite-equilibrium threshold is set by geometry rather than tuned per dataset.
ZD2jXlzQ4b.evidence: A proof of the threshold for the finite-sample objective, 25 dimension-curvature settings, and a single calibration selected on three development graphs and evaluated on ten graph datasets (abstract truncated).
ZD2jXlzQ4b.claimed_gains: Across 25 dimension-curvature settings the operational midpoints of the trained-encoder response are centered on the predicted boundary (median 1.00), and one calibration selected on three development graphs is competitive on ten (abstract truncated).
ZD2jXlzQ4b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the contribution is clear and theory-guided, with a meaningful link between the derived threshold and the implemented regularizer.
ZD2jXlzQ4b.main_concern: Empirical evidence is thin: weak results on larger datasets such as arxiv, possibly non-tree-like datasets, and no same-stack comparison against the HyperGCL isotropy regularizer or tuned wrapped and pairwise alternatives.

c2068LEaJe.one_liner: 4DCodeBench: agents write executable graphics programs that reconstruct dynamic 3D scenes from video, scored on geometry and dynamics.
c2068LEaJe.problem: Whether coding agents can recover scene structure and complex dynamics from video as executable programs is untested.
c2068LEaJe.method: Agents reconstruct dynamic scenes from video as executable graphics programs, implementing abstractions such as physical simulation, on curated real-world videos and synthetic scenes spanning deformation, fluid flow and fracture, without access to the reference video during regeneration.
c2068LEaJe.key_idea: Agents must output executable code that exposes explicit geometry and correspondence per frame, enabling ground-truth 3D evaluation on synthetic scenes while leaving the dynamics representation open.
c2068LEaJe.evidence: Benchmarking of frontier models (17 per a reviewer) on real and synthetic scenes with multiple metrics, a VQA metric and human evaluation, plus a census of the dynamics representations models choose.
c2068LEaJe.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports that strong static reconstruction does not yet translate into reliable reconstruction of complex dynamics.
c2068LEaJe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task design is strong, the benchmark covers many models on real and synthetic scenes, and requiring code and frame-level geometry enables useful analysis.
c2068LEaJe.main_concern: Each model is run once per scene with no run-variance estimate, the VQA metric has a high always-Yes baseline (87.4%), and 71% analytic solutions raise doubt that scores reflect physical understanding.

Nw2Ay81op4.one_liner: A forecaster that samples predictions from a Dirichlet of past class counts achieves optimal multiclass pseudo-U-calibration regret.
Nw2Ay81op4.problem: Recent work gave a simultaneous U-calibration and smooth-loss guarantee only with extra dimension-dependent factors (roughly K^{5/4} sqrt(T) in the worst case), leaving open whether one forecaster can reach the optimal rates.
Nw2Ay81op4.method: After observing class counts, it draws the next prediction from a Dirichlet with those counts on the face of classes seen so far (a fresh Bayesian bootstrap), and the analysis uses an identity that averaging a bounded proper loss under a Dirichlet equals a discrete derivative of its Dirichlet-averaged Bayes risk.
Nw2Ay81op4.key_idea: Sampling each prediction from a Dirichlet of observed class counts makes the be-the-perturbed-leader term telescope to a nonpositive Jensen gap, with a one-count likelihood ratio bounding stability.
Nw2Ay81op4.evidence: Theoretical proofs of regret bounds, plus a numerical table on binary problems illustrating the growth rates.
Nw2Ay81op4.claimed_gains: Regret over all bounded proper losses is at most 4 sqrt(S_T T), which is at most 4 sqrt(min{K,T} T), with logarithmic regret for every bounded Euclidean-smooth proper loss (the abstract is cut off on the smooth-loss bound).
Nw2Ay81op4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the algorithm is simple and natural, removes the dimension factors of prior work, and greatly simplifies the multiclass proof.
Nw2Ay81op4.main_concern: The paper is dense and hard to read, the guarantee is for pseudo-U-calibration and Euclidean-smooth losses (excluding log-barrier-smooth settings), and numerical results are binary only.

OCyBrCgtPE.one_liner: Computer-use agents interact with generated applications to judge them, improving preference prediction, requirement verification and generation.
OCyBrCgtPE.problem: LLM judges of coding-agent outputs focus on code analysis and unit tests, missing failures in interactive applications that are obvious to human users.
OCyBrCgtPE.method: Computer-use agents directly interact with an application and produce traces used for pairwise preference judging, requirement verification, inference-time repair and reward modeling for RL, and the paper releases 6,858 application pairs with human preferences and agent traces plus 222 applications with human-verified requirement labels.
OCyBrCgtPE.key_idea: Interaction traces from computer-use agents, rather than code or static screenshots alone, serve as evidence for judging and as feedback for repair and RL.
OCyBrCgtPE.evidence: Two released datasets and experiments on preference prediction, requirement verification, inference-time repair, reward model training and DAPO-based RL, with analyses of interaction strategy, model capability and trace components.
OCyBrCgtPE.claimed_gains: Predicting human preferences improves from 65.6% to 69.1% and requirement verification from 77.0% to 81.6%, and at inference time it repairs 75.5% of broken applications (the abstract is cut off after this).
OCyBrCgtPE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the released datasets pairing human preferences with agent traces are valuable and the experiments cover evaluation, inference-time repair and RL training.
OCyBrCgtPE.main_concern: Gains over a single-screenshot baseline are small (67.6% versus 69.1%) at much higher compute, and interaction-based judging has substantial prior work (such as AppEvalPilot and WebGen-Agent), so its originality claims are overstated.

UhYyoOBHrq.one_liner: SHA-PF searches LLM-generated problem formulations scored by search hardness, favoring rare samples with greater progress potential.
UhYyoOBHrq.problem: LLM-based problem formulation methods focus on design-intent alignment and overlook whether a formulation induces an efficient search process in expensive simulation-driven design.
UhYyoOBHrq.method: SHA-PF scores each candidate formulation by a search-hardness-based priority that favors rare samples with greater progress potential, then searches the formulation space through LLM-based generation, repair and evolutionary refinement.
UhYyoOBHrq.key_idea: Score candidate formulations by how strongly they prioritize rare, high-progress-potential samples, then evolve them with LLM generation and repair.
UhYyoOBHrq.evidence: A real-world multi-objective benchmark and five expensive antenna design benchmarks, with reviews noting HFSS simulations and tests across optimizers and LLM backbones.
UhYyoOBHrq.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says discovered formulations need significantly fewer evaluations to reach design requirements, without numbers.
UhYyoOBHrq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that making search efficiency the formulation objective is a well-motivated, practically significant idea with strong results on expensive real simulators.
UhYyoOBHrq.main_concern: Results lack repeated runs or variance, and the cost of searching for the formulation (25 generations, population of 5) is excluded from the comparison.

7kbo1DjUvJ.one_liner: Embedding model aligning text with per-object video trajectories via slow-fast trajectory encoding and mask-guided contrastive learning.
7kbo1DjUvJ.problem: Global video embeddings entangle multiple objects and their spatiotemporal dynamics, which limits object-level grounding between text and video.
7kbo1DjUvJ.method: VTrajEmbed decomposes a video into object trajectories and aligns each trajectory embedding with text through retrieval. Slow-Fast Trajectory Encoding densely samples low-resolution frames for motion cues and sparsely selects high-resolution frames for scene context, aggregated by a shared LLM backbone.
7kbo1DjUvJ.key_idea: Encode each trajectory with a dual-branch dense-low-resolution and sparse-high-resolution LLM-aggregated encoder, trained with a relation-masked contrastive loss that avoids false negatives.
7kbo1DjUvJ.evidence: Text2Traj-Bench, a trajectory-level benchmark with model-assisted construction and human-verified query-trajectory relations, plus transfer to global video retrieval.
7kbo1DjUvJ.claimed_gains: Reports that VTrajEmbed-5B improves text-to-trajectory and trajectory-to-text R@1 over baselines; the numbers are cut off in the abstract.
7kbo1DjUvJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree object-level video-text alignment through trajectory embeddings is a meaningful formulation, and that the Slow-Fast design and Text2Traj-Bench are useful contributions with substantial gains over baselines.
7kbo1DjUvJ.main_concern: The main evaluation uses pre-generated, curated trajectory candidates rather than an end-to-end pipeline, and the benchmark's model-generated queries may introduce selection bias.

WJmxx7weU2.one_liner: Represents molecular orbitals as optimized Gaussian clouds, like Gaussian splatting with quantum mechanics as renderer, to scale DFT.
WJmxx7weU2.problem: Fixed atom-centered basis sets in DFT dictate how accuracy and cost scale with system size.
WJmxx7weU2.method: GS-DFT jointly optimizes Gaussian positions, shapes and mixing coefficients by gradient descent to minimize the energy without training data, using adaptive density fitting with screening for two-electron integrals and a regularized differentiable orthogonalization of orbitals.
WJmxx7weU2.key_idea: Learn the basis itself by optimizing positions, shapes and mixing coefficients of a Gaussian cloud directly against the DFT energy, as in 3D Gaussian splatting.
WJmxx7weU2.evidence: Accuracy in energy, density and nuclear forces against conventional basis sets, stretched-bond and anion cases, and memory scaling to thousands of atoms with a multi-GPU implementation.
WJmxx7weU2.claimed_gains: The optimized basis reaches the accuracy of the largest conventional basis sets with a fraction of the parameters, has quadratic peak memory scaling, and simulates up to 2,742 atoms (10,406 electrons).
WJmxx7weU2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that connecting DFT with Gaussian splatting is a new, promising direction and that the method is clearly presented with accuracy and complexity experiments.
WJmxx7weU2.main_concern: Scalability and efficiency claims are broader than the evidence (the 2.3x scaling claim rests on three systems, and fewer basis functions appear only past a crossover), and wall-clock time is much slower than conventional SCF.

BReqQMFlJb.one_liner: Plan-derived control- and data-flow constraints on branches and parameters defend computer-use agents against branch steering prompt injection.
BReqQMFlJb.problem: In Dual-LLM designs, committed plans can branch on runtime observations, so adversaries can steer a computer-use agent down a hazardous pre-approved branch with crafted untrusted data.
BReqQMFlJb.method: They introduce STEER-Bench (101 tasks across 9 domains) and COBRA, which pairs trusted branching plans with ahead-of-time capability constraints enforced at HTTP and MCP boundaries, bounding the parameters and destinations each branch may execute.
BReqQMFlJb.key_idea: Fix branch-specific capability constraints on destinations and parameters ahead of time from the trusted plan and enforce them at HTTP and MCP calls.
BReqQMFlJb.evidence: STEER-Bench with 101 tasks over 9 domains, compared with ReAct and CaMeL-NOVA on 74 shared attack configurations, plus validation on external benchmarks per reviews.
BReqQMFlJb.claimed_gains: Attack success is 90.5% against ReAct and 87.8% against CaMeL-NOVA on 74 shared configurations, and COBRA reduces it to 0% while retaining 97% benign utility.
BReqQMFlJb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the branch steering gap in Dual-LLM defenses is real and well demonstrated, and that a system-level defense with data-flow constraints is practical.
BReqQMFlJb.main_concern: The data-flow integrity definition is stronger than what the system guarantees, since attacker-supplied values can still select a branch when they satisfy the plan's constraints.

jln57MIkop.one_liner: Token-level negative preference optimization weighted by FutureKL, with modality-specific unlearning and retention objectives adaptively allocated.
jln57MIkop.problem: MLLM unlearning must suppress target knowledge while keeping utility, but sequence-level objectives ignore unequal token influence (sequence coupling) and a target suppressed under one modality view can stay accessible through another (modality imbalance).
jln57MIkop.method: MT-NPO uses bounded FutureKL-guided suffix scores to focus unlearning on influential tokens, and modality-specific unlearning and retention objectives that adaptively allocate optimization by residual target accessibility and utility degradation.
jln57MIkop.key_idea: Weight NPO's per-token loss by a bounded FutureKL estimate of each token's influence on future generation, and rebalance per-modality unlearning by remaining target accessibility.
jln57MIkop.evidence: Multiple benchmarks (including CLEAR) and MLLM backbones (including LLaVA), compared against GA, GD, NPO, PO and MANU, with ablations such as Token-NPO and Future-only.
jln57MIkop.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two limitations (sequence coupling, modality imbalance) are clearly identified and the method is clearly defined and evaluated across classification, cloze and generation tasks.
jln57MIkop.main_concern: Conditions for baselines and ablations are under-specified so gains cannot be attributed to adaptive allocation, and the baseline set omits some token-wise and MLLM-specific unlearning methods.

PWAAPtzrmu.one_liner: ScaleSplit-NO predicts 3D turbulence with a Parent operator for the coarse field and a Child operator for full-resolution local patches.
PWAAPtzrmu.problem: Training neural surrogates for 3D turbulence at high resolution is memory-limited because full-field memory grows with resolution, and full-resolution training data are scarce and expensive.
PWAAPtzrmu.method: A Parent operator predicts the global coarse field at the next time step and a Child operator predicts full-resolution local patches conditioned on it; the Child is pretrained alone and attached to the Parent's coarse prediction through zero-initialized connections, so neither model sees the full-resolution field.
PWAAPtzrmu.key_idea: Exploit turbulence's scale structure: split prediction into a coarse global Parent and a patch-wise Child conditioned on it, joined by zero-initialized connections after separate pretraining.
PWAAPtzrmu.evidence: Two high-resolution turbulence benchmarks including JHTDB256 (256^3) and urban wind prediction for a Montreal district on a 500x150x500 grid, against competing baselines.
PWAAPtzrmu.claimed_gains: On JHTDB256 the NMSE is 53% lower than the strongest baseline and training memory is 79% lower than the most memory-efficient baseline; one-step NMSE falls by 65.8% on the Montreal urban wind task.
PWAAPtzrmu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the scale-separation design principled and well motivated by turbulence memory scaling, with predictions stronger than baselines and a well-documented, reproducible setup.
PWAAPtzrmu.main_concern: Baselines do not isolate the value of the coarse-resolution correction, and a closely related scale-separated JHTDB approach (Pixel-Resolved Long-Context Learning for Turbulence at Exascale) is neither compared nor ablated.

M8J1WmXMo5.one_liner: ImpasseBench injects environment blockers into repair tasks and scores agent actions relative to when evidence becomes sufficient.
M8J1WmXMo5.problem: Coding agents keep trying when the environment makes completion impossible, over-persisting, attempting undesired workarounds, and claiming unsupported success despite early evidence that only outside help can restore progress.
M8J1WmXMo5.method: ImpasseBench injects twelve realistic environment blockers into otherwise solvable repair tasks and marks, in each trajectory, the step at which collected evidence becomes sufficient. Actions are scored relative to that step, and an escalation tool or an external monitor is tested as mitigation.
M8J1WmXMo5.key_idea: Mark per trajectory the step at which evidence suffices that only outside help can restore progress, then score effort and unsafe requests before versus after it.
M8J1WmXMo5.evidence: Eight frontier models and 19,371 trajectories, with escalation-tool and external-monitor interventions.
M8J1WmXMo5.claimed_gains: The escalation tool cuts budget exhaustion from 34.0% to 6.7%, and the monitor nearly triples task success after environment restoration.
M8J1WmXMo5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses an important, timely, under-measured failure mode with a clean benchmark whose labels come from blocker cards and explicit rules rather than an LLM judge.
M8J1WmXMo5.main_concern: The sufficient-evidence point is defined by rules without human validation, the escalation-tool gain is confounded with its instructions (no prompt-only baseline), and novelty over recent abstention work needs sharper delineation.

fRpPJorScJ.one_liner: Anchor-based multi-view clustering with view-specific prior-correction matrices and a discrete factorization term that outputs labels without spectral post-processing.
fRpPJorScJ.problem: Anchor-based methods use a shared semantic prior across views even though views have view-specific noise, distortions, and outliers, and separate representation and clustering stages leave representations not optimized for the final clustering.
fRpPJorScJ.method: PCAL reconstructs each view through a shared anchor representation, aligns each view's anchor matrix with the shared prior by orthogonal projection, and adds regularized view-specific correction matrices so the prior adapts to view discrepancies. A discrete factorization term links anchor representation learning directly to cluster label assignment.
fRpPJorScJ.key_idea: Correct the shared anchor prior per view with regularized correction matrices and tie anchor representations directly to discrete cluster assignments in one optimization.
fRpPJorScJ.evidence: Comparison with other multi-view clustering methods on clustering metrics and computation time per reviewers; the visible abstract is cut off before results.
fRpPJorScJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified framework with per-view prior correction and discrete assignment is reasonable and reduces computation time while staying competitive on clustering metrics.
fRpPJorScJ.main_concern: Novelty and motivation are not clearly delineated from related work, and explanations of how reconstruction, prior correction, and discrete assignment coordinate (Figure 1) are insufficient.

AThTIpgAtR.one_liner: Geometric reductions (Morse-theoretic and double-point intersection) determine minimum width for W^{1,p} universal approximation, separating it from L^p.
AThTIpgAtR.problem: It is unknown whether the minimum width for universal approximation in W^{1,p} with finite p differs from that for L^p and W^{1,infinity}, since no other non-trivial separation between norms is known beyond L^p versus L^infinity.
AThTIpgAtR.method: For leaky-ReLU-like activations the authors show the minimum width is d_out when d_out exceeds 3/2 times d_in and p is at most d_out minus d_in. They then characterize the minimum width for all p in the case d_out = 2 d_in - 1 with d_in at least 3, via a reduction to a geometric problem.
AThTIpgAtR.key_idea: Reduce W^{1,p} width questions to topological problems (Morse-theoretic and double-point intersection) about embedding-like maps, so the minimum width depends on p and on the parity of d_in.
AThTIpgAtR.evidence: Theory only: proofs of minimum-width characterizations, with no experiments.
AThTIpgAtR.claimed_gains: For d_out above 3/2 d_in and p at most d_out - d_in the minimum width equals d_out (same as L^p, and strictly below W^{1,infinity} when d_out is at most 2 d_in); at d_out = 2 d_in - 1 with d_in at least 3 it equals the L^p value if p is at most d_in - 1 and increases by one when p exceeds d_in - 1.
AThTIpgAtR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the results are new and solid, showing for the first time that the W^{1,p} width differs from both L^p and W^{1,infinity}, with a surprising dependence on p.
AThTIpgAtR.main_concern: Results exclude ReLU (they need C^1 leaky-ReLU-like activations), require output dimension large relative to input, and the related Sobolev-approximation literature is not discussed.

PlTvk9ITIw.one_liner: Chained, grounded questions with guideline decision tables supervise intermediate radiology reasoning over 122,127 abdominal CT questions.
PlTvk9ITIw.problem: Vision-language models are trained on image-answer pairs and judged by the answer alone, leaving the intermediate clinical representation (size, enhancement, change) unchecked.
PlTvk9ITIw.method: RadThinking turns each step of reading a scan into a question with a reference answer grounded in a 3D bounding box, links questions into chains, and encodes five clinical guidelines as decision tables, so the intermediate representation is both grounded and explicit.
PlTvk9ITIw.key_idea: Supervise the representation a radiologist builds (grounded findings, comparisons, guideline rules) as intermediate answers scored at their 3D boxes, not only the final answer.
PlTvk9ITIw.evidence: 122,127 questions over 5,365 abdominal CT scans of 2,679 patients from two countries, evaluated on eleven models with analysis of open-weight models and fine-tuning comparisons.
PlTvk9ITIw.claimed_gains: Benchmark difficulty result: the best of eleven models gets every answer right in only 23% of chains (numerical errors aside), and turning thinking on brings no consistent gain.
PlTvk9ITIw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the large, grounded, dependency-linked dataset is a useful resource for evaluating and supervising step-wise medical reasoning.
PlTvk9ITIw.main_concern: The key comparison isolating intermediate supervision (final-only versus intermediate-plus-final) is described but not reported, and LLM-assisted rationale construction lacks fully documented audit statistics.

rz9XM7LCkv.one_liner: Short task-specific warm-ups give task vectors whose shared and private subspaces project and rescale gradients during multi-task RL.
rz9XM7LCkv.problem: Mixed RL risks interference across heterogeneous tasks, while independent training plus post-hoc merging leaves specialized updates to be reconciled afterward.
rz9XM7LCkv.method: TVG-RL extracts task vectors from short task-specific warm-ups, decomposes them into shared and task-private subspaces plus a complementary component, and trains a single policy from the original base while projecting and rescaling subsequent RL gradients. It needs neither fully trained experts nor a final merging stage.
rz9XM7LCkv.key_idea: Use task-vector geometry, normally a post-hoc merging tool, as an online prior that projects and rescales RL gradients differently for shared, private, and complementary directions.
rz9XM7LCkv.evidence: Eight heterogeneous benchmarks, a second backbone, held-out GPQA-D, and a measured online overhead of 3.1-3.8% per reviews, with baselines re-evaluated in one pipeline.
rz9XM7LCkv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that turning task vectors from post-hoc merging tools into online optimization priors is a natural, useful idea with consistent baselines and low overhead.
rz9XM7LCkv.main_concern: Ablations and controls (random subspace, shared-only, private-only, norm restoration) and multi-task optimization baselines are missing, so it is unclear whether the geometry causes the gains.

q8pW2J584L.one_liner: Single-head softmax transformer construction that runs preconditioned Richardson iteration to approximate in-context Gaussian kernel ridge regression.
q8pW2J584L.problem: It was unclear whether a standard softmax-attention transformer can implement a convergent solver with an end-to-end prediction-error guarantee for nonlinear in-context learning.
q8pW2J584L.method: They construct a single-head transformer whose forward pass approximately implements preconditioned Richardson iteration on the Gaussian-kernel ridge regression system under bounded-data assumptions. Softmax attention supplies the row-normalized Gaussian-kernel operator, and MLP layers approximate the intra-token scalar arithmetic of each update.
q8pW2J584L.key_idea: Softmax attention forms a row-normalized Gaussian kernel operator while MLPs approximate scalar arithmetic, so each block performs one preconditioned Richardson update on the kernel system.
q8pW2J584L.evidence: Theory with an error-propagation analysis, plus experiments training transformers (reviews mention 12-layer models compared against five solvers, run in a single input dimension).
q8pW2J584L.claimed_gains: O(log(1/epsilon)) blocks and MLP width O(sqrt(N/epsilon)) achieve epsilon-accurate prediction for prompts of length N.
q8pW2J584L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theorem rigorous and well written, with a construction that handles softmax normalization and cleanly separates the roles of attention and MLP layers.
q8pW2J584L.main_concern: Experiments show trained transformers approximate KRR but do not show they implement Richardson iteration, and the bounds are not tied quantitatively to the 12-layer models used.

wdZxGtKvh6.one_liner: Adversarial perturbations make commercial image editors' safety moderation classifiers flag protected images as policy-violating, triggering refusals.
wdZxGtKvh6.problem: Prior image immunization needs model weights and the editing prompt, so it fails against closed-source commercial image editors.
wdZxGtKvh6.method: MIRAGE adds adversarial perturbations that align the image with policy-violating concepts in representation space, so the pre-generation moderation classifier flags it and the editor refuses. Reviews describe surrogate-model ensembles, feature alignment, PGD, and global-local optimization.
wdZxGtKvh6.key_idea: Perturb the image so moderation classifiers see policy-violating concepts, making the editor's pre-generation safety check refuse the edit instead of attacking the editing model itself.
wdZxGtKvh6.evidence: Evaluated on multiple closed-source image editing APIs; reviews add a social-media evaluation and adaptive-attacker tests, and note a single editing prompt and one policy category.
wdZxGtKvh6.claimed_gains: Immunization success rate rises from less than 15% for the best prior technique to more than 88% on multiple closed-source image editing APIs at the same perturbation level.
wdZxGtKvh6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value targeting the shared moderation filter of commercial editors as a practically relevant, simple, prompt-agnostic idea evaluated on closed-source APIs.
wdZxGtKvh6.main_concern: Adaptive attackers can remove the protection and transfer from open-source classifiers to commercial safety checkers is unexplained, with limited novelty over prior refusal-inducing attacks.

dUI1uFVvNt.one_liner: Generator proposes universal-Turing-machine programs whose byte outputs train a learner from scratch, with RL rewarding frontier sequences.
dUI1uFVvNt.problem: Pretraining relies on curated natural data, and it is unclear whether a model can generate its own useful training data from random initialization.
dUI1uFVvNt.method: Two autoregressive transformers train together from random initialization: a generator proposes programs run by a universal Turing machine to produce byte sequences, and a learner predicts them with cross-entropy. The generator is trained with RL to produce sequences at the frontier of the learner's capability, giving an adaptive curriculum.
dUI1uFVvNt.key_idea: A generator trained with a gradient-alignment reward writes UTM programs at the learner's capability frontier, producing an adaptive synthetic curriculum without natural data.
dUI1uFVvNt.evidence: Zero-shot loss on text, image, and audio datasets as compute scales, with ablations of the RL reward; per reviews, natural data (e.g., DCLM and DNA signals) is used to select configurations and models.
dUI1uFVvNt.claimed_gains: not stated; the TL;DR only claims zero-shot loss on text, image, and audio datasets decreases predictably with compute.
dUI1uFVvNt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the closed-loop self-play design and the gradient-based generator reward, with ablations and transfer across text, image, and audio.
dUI1uFVvNt.main_concern: Reviewers say the claim of general capability without natural data is overstated because natural data selects configurations and checkpoints, and compute accounting appears to omit generator cost.

a9wKPp7xvR.one_liner: Den2MoEE converts dense LLM embedding models into expert-specialized MoE models using domain-aware neuron grouping, diversity-driven conversion, and router-signal embeddings.
a9wKPp7xvR.problem: Training MoE embedding models from scratch is too costly, and existing dense-to-MoE conversions ignore embedding-specific expert specialization and routing, yielding homogeneous experts and poor performance recovery.
a9wKPp7xvR.method: Den2MoEE applies TokenScore-weighted neuron domain modeling, expert-diversity-driven dense-to-MoE conversion, and a two-phase recovery strategy. MoE router signals are also used as complementary embedding representations without increasing activated parameters.
a9wKPp7xvR.key_idea: Group FFN neurons into experts by similarity of domain-conditioned, TokenScore-weighted activation profiles, then recover quality with routing-aware two-phase training and router-signal embeddings.
a9wKPp7xvR.evidence: Code and multilingual embedding benchmarks against a LLaMA-MoE reconstruction baseline, with clustering, routing, backbone (up to 4B per reviews), and additional-domain analyses and throughput measurements.
a9wKPp7xvR.claimed_gains: Reduces the number of activated parameters by 33%-55% compared with the original dense LLM embedding models (the rest of the performance claim is truncated in the abstract).
a9wKPp7xvR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method addresses a practical inference-cost problem and preserves more of the dense model's performance than the LLaMA-MoE reconstruction at comparable activated parameters, with extensive evaluation.
a9wKPp7xvR.main_concern: Justification and baselines are limited: the premise that similar domain activation profiles belong in one expert is supported only empirically, LLaMA-MoE is the only direct conversion baseline, and noticeable degradation remains versus the dense backbones at 4B.

7TlYUWak6o.one_liner: Isospectral RLVR optimization: fix the base model's weight spectra and train only the input and output singular frames.
7TlYUWak6o.problem: The optimization layer that converts reward feedback into weight-space updates in RLVR remains poorly understood.
7TlYUWak6o.method: ISO-Merger composes shared-base specialists in fixed-spectrum frame coordinates without post-merge data, rollouts, or distillation. ISO-Optimizer applies AdamW or Muon directly to the frame variables under fixed base spectra.
7TlYUWak6o.key_idea: RLVR reuses the base weight spectra and learns new behavior by adapting the input and output singular frames, so optimize the frames while holding the spectra fixed.
7TlYUWak6o.evidence: Spectrum restoration and fixed-spectrum training analyses, plus math and coding RLVR experiments with AdamW and Muon baselines under learning-rate sweeps, including Qwen3-4B-Base.
7TlYUWak6o.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-4B-Base, ISO-AdamW reaches AdamW's 400-update accuracy in 280 updates (1.5 X fewer updates, 27% less wall-clock time) and exceeds AdamW by 2.2 points at update 400; ISO-Merger achieves the highest aggregate scores among data-free merging methods.
7TlYUWak6o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the spectral analysis is well supported by controlled interventions and that the two derived methods show consistent gains over AdamW and Muon in thorough experiments.
7TlYUWak6o.main_concern: Spectrum-preserving optimization already exists in POET and Pion, and the modest gains are not clearly attributed, with no ablation of the fixed spectrum in ISO-Merger.

zn3bDEHdtr.one_liner: Unifies robot demonstrations from 37 sources as camera-centric actions in a 20k-hour corpus and trains a video-action model on it.
zn3bDEHdtr.problem: Public robot demonstrations already total tens of thousands of hours, but heterogeneous data from different robot platforms is hard to reuse across embodiments.
zn3bDEHdtr.method: Proposes a camera-centric action representation as a unified interface, builds CamX (20k hours from 37 sources converted to it), and trains CamUVA, a unified video-action model that identifies every camera view and action stream by its camera pose.
zn3bDEHdtr.key_idea: Express actions as camera trajectories and tag each camera view and action stream with its camera pose, abstracting away embodiment-specific kinematics.
zn3bDEHdtr.evidence: Per the reviews, design studies and scaling experiments on a 120-task RoboLab simulation benchmark and several real-world platforms, with generalization to unseen embodiments.
zn3bDEHdtr.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims zero-shot generalization to unseen robot embodiments without giving numbers.
zn3bDEHdtr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the integration effort and empirical scale are substantial, and that the corpus and camera-pose-based design give broad, useful evidence about cross-embodiment training.
zn3bDEHdtr.main_concern: Conceptual novelty is limited relative to the engineering breadth, and the evidence does not separate the benefit of canonicalizing action conventions from using the camera frame itself.

9s26jh2HRS.one_liner: Co-trains robot policies on egocentric human recovery demonstrations aligned to a shared corrective-intent space with robot data.
9s26jh2HRS.problem: Robot teleoperation data for failure recovery is hard to scale because inducing diverse failures, correcting them and resetting is slow, and recovery needs more data than success demonstrations.
9s26jh2HRS.method: Human operators arrange task-level failure configurations and record short recovery segments. EgoRecovery co-trains by aligning human recovery demonstrations to a compact corrective-intent space shared with robot data, capturing timing and magnitude of correction, with a small number of robot recovery demonstrations connecting intent to robot actions.
9s26jh2HRS.key_idea: Map human and robot recovery demonstrations into a compact corrective-intent space of correction timing and magnitude, with few robot demonstrations grounding that intent in executable actions.
9s26jh2HRS.evidence: Compares recovery-demonstration yield per operator hour for human versus robot teleoperation and evaluates the co-training framework; experimental details are cut off in the available abstract.
9s26jh2HRS.claimed_gains: Human operators generate about 10x as many recovery demonstrations per operator hour as robot teleoperation under their protocol.
9s26jh2HRS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see the recovery-data problem as well identified and egocentric human data as a plausible way to scale recovery supervision.
9s26jh2HRS.main_concern: The evaluation is narrow, with no transfer across failure types or tasks, and the data-efficiency figure is measured only under the authors' own protocol.

knpNnJ4JPS.one_liner: Benchmark of pathology foundation models built on a new mouse lung-cancer dataset pairing H&E images with in vivo genetic perturbations.
knpNnJ4JPS.problem: Pathology foundation models are evaluated on small cohorts whose clinical labels are noisy and confounded.
knpNnJ4JPS.method: They used Perturb-map to generate genetically diverse tumors in a mouse lung cancer model with paired H&E and multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) imaging, and built a benchmark suite covering perturbation-label retrieval and tumor microenvironment prediction.
knpNnJ4JPS.key_idea: Use in vivo Perturb-map knockouts with biological replicates and paired mIF readouts as controlled labels for evaluating H&E foundation-model embeddings.
knpNnJ4JPS.evidence: 84 knockout perturbations across 32 mice with 19,018 tumors and 116,383 H&E patches; eleven public pathology foundation models and three ImageNet baselines evaluated.
knpNnJ4JPS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled in vivo perturbation design, the curated dataset with mIF readouts, and the large number of benchmarked models.
knpNnJ4JPS.main_concern: It is unclear whether perturbation signals can be separated from batch and mouse effects (two libraries, residual mouse-specific signal, reliance on F8-control normalization).

mrFYMSBdgo.one_liner: FuseAlign: transformer forced aligner trained on pseudo-labeled speech with online EMA label correction, plus AlignBench benchmark and new metrics.
mrFYMSBdgo.problem: Forced-alignment evaluations rely on short clean speech, perfect transcripts and metrics that hide consequential errors, while real use involves long diverse recordings and error-prone ASR transcripts.
mrFYMSBdgo.method: The paper adds improved metrics, a scoring protocol for real ASR transcripts and the AlignBench benchmark. FuseAlign jointly contextualizes audio and text to localize coarse words, refines boundaries at millisecond resolution, and detects missing transcript words without lexicon-based or Viterbi decoding.
mrFYMSBdgo.key_idea: Jointly contextualize audio and text in a transformer to localize words, then refine boundaries at millisecond resolution, training on pseudo-labels corrected online by EMA snapshots.
mrFYMSBdgo.evidence: Evaluated on AlignBench against baseline aligners, including with real ASR transcripts, with ablations; reviewers also cite TIMIT and Buckeye results.
mrFYMSBdgo.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract says FuseAlign substantially outperforms all baselines on AlignBench and remains robust under real ASR transcripts.
mrFYMSBdgo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation gap is well motivated and that FuseAlign substantially reduces mean, moderate and catastrophic alignment errors against established aligners on the new benchmark.
mrFYMSBdgo.main_concern: The claim of consistent superiority is overstated: other datasets and the chunked MMS-FA configuration show competing aligners doing better, and the test set is small and English-only.

Jr784qYi8d.one_liner: RecallWAM adds a recall objective to world-action learning, recovering which areas were explored from historical observations to guide object navigation.
Jr784qYi8d.problem: Foresight-based world-action models predict future observations, but identical scene appearances can correspond to different exploration states that need different search decisions.
Jr784qYi8d.method: RecallWAM augments foresight-based world-action learning with a Recall capability that recovers exploration state from historical observations, and trains on balanced exploration trajectories that trade off shortest-path guidance with randomized branch exploration.
Jr784qYi8d.key_idea: Supervise the model to reconstruct a coverage-based exploration state from past views and feed that state to the policy alongside foresight prediction of future observations.
Jr784qYi8d.evidence: Benchmarks HM3D, MP3D and OVON with controlled ablations of Recall and Foresight, history composition and explicit state input.
Jr784qYi8d.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract claims leading performance on HM3D, MP3D and OVON and joint Recall and Foresight gains exceeding the sum of their individual gains.
Jr784qYi8d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that making previously explored coverage explicit is a well-motivated extension of foresight-based world-action models, backed by clean ablations and consistent results across three benchmarks.
Jr784qYi8d.main_concern: Attribution is unclear: leading-performance comparisons mix perception and policy (frozen SAM3 masks), no baseline is retrained under matched conditions, and the super-additivity claim rests on single runs without seeds.

YfO0BmTcOl.one_liner: Few-step crystal generation by learning average velocity (MeanFlow) in a frozen autoencoder's per-atom latent space with a diffusion transformer.
YfO0BmTcOl.problem: Generative models for materials discovery need dozens to thousands of network evaluations per structure, creating a sampling bottleneck for large-scale screening.
YfO0BmTcOl.method: MeanFlux is a diffusion transformer that learns the average velocity across trajectory intervals in the per-atom latent space of a frozen autoencoder, generating crystals in 1 to 16 steps. It is further fine-tuned with negative-aware fine-tuning (NFT) on a crystal reward.
YfO0BmTcOl.key_idea: Learn interval-averaged velocity (mean flow) in a frozen per-atom latent space so a crystal is sampled in 1 to 16 network evaluations, which also makes reward fine-tuning cheap.
YfO0BmTcOl.evidence: MP-20 de novo generation, crystal structure prediction, LeMat-GenBench, model-size scaling, and NFT reward fine-tuning, with baselines re-scored under one protocol.
YfO0BmTcOl.claimed_gains: A 130M model matches the best mSUN yield (metastable, unique, new candidates) on MP-20 using one-sixth the inference compute; NFT reaches 41.2% relaxed LeMat-GenBench mSUN, 3.7 times the conditional base model, at the same sampling cost.
YfO0BmTcOl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the sampling efficiency is strong, with MP-20 mSUN comparable to Chemeleon2 at roughly one-sixth of the compute, and the evaluation is broad and fairly controlled.
YfO0BmTcOl.main_concern: Technical novelty is limited because every component (latent VAE with DiT, MeanFlow, guidance distillation, NFT) comes from prior work, and some compute comparisons are estimated and LLM-based generators are missing.

Cn55vMRDRL.one_liner: Exact solver computing the full circular partial optimal transport cost profile for arbitrary convex radial costs and repeated support points.
Cn55vMRDRL.problem: Partial optimal transport between periodic signals needs a circle-aware solver, and the existing PAWC profile algorithm covers only the W1 cost on distinct support.
Cn55vMRDRL.method: COPT extends PAWC's local augmentation and simultaneous-cut arguments to convex costs and uses a rank refinement for repeated support and flat cost regions. It extends to spherical measures via great-circle slicing and to repeated comparisons via a linear embedding.
Cn55vMRDRL.key_idea: Extend PAWC's local-augmentation and simultaneous-cut arguments from W1 to arbitrary convex radial costs, with rank refinement to handle repeated support points.
Cn55vMRDRL.evidence: Complexity proofs and metric properties, plus experiments on correspondence recovery, partial shape matching, foreground retrieval and directional data, validated against exact solvers with runtime and memory comparisons to PAWC.
Cn55vMRDRL.claimed_gains: Returns the complete profile in O(N log N + K^2) time and O(N) memory (K the largest transported cardinality), and in O(pN log^2 N) time for integer power costs.
Cn55vMRDRL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper meaningfully extends circular partial transport to general convex costs and repeated locations, with theoretical guarantees and validation against exact solvers.
Cn55vMRDRL.main_concern: The contribution is incremental over PAWC and PAWL, supports only equal point weights, and the presentation is not self-contained (key details and experiments sit in the supplement).

ReKwy0w1f1.one_liner: Open-source library and benchmark unifying 17 robust online, offline and safe RL algorithms, evaluated over 279 perturbation configurations.
ReKwy0w1f1.problem: Robust RL methods live in separate codebases with limited reusability, and their empirical capability boundary under diverse shifts is unclear.
ReKwy0w1f1.method: RobustRLlib integrates 17 representative robust online, offline and safe RL methods behind one interface, with an evaluation platform covering diverse real-world shifts and humanoid and vision-language-action tasks.
ReKwy0w1f1.key_idea: Separate robustness mechanisms from base algorithms under a unified interface and perturbation specification so algorithms can be reused and compared on a common shift grid.
ReKwy0w1f1.evidence: Systematic evaluation over 279 perturbation configurations with normalized scores, predefined severity grids and per-task results.
ReKwy0w1f1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying fragmented robust RL implementations under one interface with a standardized evaluation protocol addresses a real and practically valuable problem.
ReKwy0w1f1.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate robustness mechanisms: training budgets (about 5M steps for ATLA versus 2M for PPO), base algorithms and attack sets differ across methods, and baselines are not validated against published results.

UREguflpCe.one_liner: Training-free audio token pruning that recursively refines time intervals whose representations deviate from anchors, then regulates sparse gaps.
UREguflpCe.problem: Dense audio tokens make Audio LLMs expensive, and existing compression methods do not check how faithfully retained tokens preserve the underlying temporal representation trajectory.
UREguflpCe.method: TimePrune applies Time-Aware RDP to encoder outputs, recursively refining intervals whose intermediate representations are poorly described by their temporal anchors under a token budget, plus Temporal Coverage Refinement to limit overly sparse intervals.
UREguflpCe.key_idea: Choose which audio tokens to keep by recursively splitting intervals where intermediate representations deviate from their temporal anchors, giving denser anchors where the trajectory changes more.
UREguflpCe.evidence: Four ALLMs and five audio understanding benchmarks against nine baselines at 75% to 95% pruning, plus a long-form efficiency analysis with Qwen3-Omni.
UREguflpCe.claimed_gains: On long-form audio with Qwen3-Omni, TimePrune retains only 15% of audio tokens while preserving 94.2% of the Vanilla score (further reduction figure truncated in the abstract).
UREguflpCe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free and general, and that evaluation across four models, several benchmarks and budgets shows it works.
UREguflpCe.main_concern: Novelty and justification are questioned (an incremental heuristic that could apply to other modalities), gains over baselines are marginal on individual benchmarks, and temporal-structure preservation is not verified on timing-sensitive tasks.

3rkw0BZlYN.one_liner: Shows theoretically and empirically that better approximation of the power distribution can lower reasoning accuracy, for example through immediate stopping.
3rkw0BZlYN.problem: Power sampling lets base models match RL-post-trained reasoning, but how the error of approximating the power distribution affects task performance is underexplored.
3rkw0BZlYN.method: The paper analyzes sampling importance resampling (SIR) with a Markov graph task, a theorem that more candidates strictly improve sampling fidelity while, under stated conditions, raising failure probability, and experiments with practical LLM power samplers.
3rkw0BZlYN.key_idea: Increasing SIR candidates monotonically improves fidelity to the power distribution, yet when likelihood and task success are misaligned this raises failure probability, for example by favoring immediate stopping.
3rkw0BZlYN.evidence: A Markov-graph illustration, SIR theory, and experiments with LLM power samplers on reasoning and instruction-following tasks across several models (LLaMA, Phi and Qwen per reviews).
3rkw0BZlYN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of whether more faithful sampling helps task performance is important and that the SIR fidelity-versus-failure-probability analysis is a solid theoretical contribution.
3rkw0BZlYN.main_concern: Empirical evidence is narrower than the title suggests: immediate stopping appears mainly in two Qwen models, other models improve with more candidates, and the conceptual finding overlaps known likelihood-quality mismatch.

ckZROrrI4T.one_liner: Re-entering each intermediate result through the shared grid input interface lets learned visual operations compose on unseen pairs
ckZROrrI4T.problem: Learned operations on grid states execute accurately in isolation but fail when composed into visual programs.
ckZROrrI4T.method: Compares a grid-state executor, which re-enters each intermediate result through the shared spatial color interface, with a latent-handoff executor that passes hidden states, under matched parameters, data, supervision and update budget.
ckZROrrI4T.key_idea: Each intermediate result is returned through the same grid representation the next operation consumes, instead of passing unadapted hidden states between operations.
ckZROrrI4T.evidence: Matched-training comparisons on unseen primitive pairs and longer programs, a frozen-weight handoff test, position-wise probes of intermediate grids, and transfer to grounded-object operations and programs recovered from demonstrations.
ckZROrrI4T.claimed_gains: Exact accuracy on unseen primitive pairs rises from 43.5% to 88.2% under matched training, and from 29.2% to 87.6% with every learned weight fixed.
ckZROrrI4T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the comparison of state interfaces is tightly controlled (matched model size, data, supervision, seeds) and the accuracy gap is large and consistent.
ckZROrrI4T.main_concern: The result may simply reflect out-of-distribution hidden-state inputs in the latent baseline, and input alignment is not cleanly separated from the low-dimensional bottleneck or shown to matter beyond closed grid tasks.

8pdy1JMoLS.one_liner: Steers rollout generation with Langevin steps in logit space at branch points to diversify RLVR rollout groups
8pdy1JMoLS.problem: RLVR can only reinforce what it samples, so rollout groups with little reward spread limit progress, and existing exploration methods widen sampling blindly in every direction.
8pdy1JMoLS.method: DRIFT applies a Langevin step to steer generation at branch points. Because the optimal drift (the gradient of expected reward in logit space) cannot be evaluated before a rollout ends, it estimates a direction online from prior steering feedback, using remaining entropy at branch points as the signal, and composes with GRPO and DAPO.
8pdy1JMoLS.key_idea: A Langevin step in logit space follows an online-estimated drift direction learned from earlier steering feedback, using entropy remaining at branch points as the signal.
8pdy1JMoLS.evidence: Training Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base under GRPO and DAPO; reviewers also cite five seeds, random-steering and matched-KL temperature controls, and a fixed-checkpoint analysis.
8pdy1JMoLS.claimed_gains: Raises the benchmark average by 1.5 to 3.1 points in every pairing and AIME accuracy by up to 4.6 points.
8pdy1JMoLS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree DRIFT targets a real rollout-quality bottleneck and composes with GRPO and DAPO without a value model or search tree, with consistent empirical gains.
8pdy1JMoLS.main_concern: Entropy feedback is not shown to track correctness or continuation value, and carrying the drift across branches by token-probability rank is unjustified and unablated.

F2MNniBNZf.one_liner: Diffusion on a shift-covariant wavelet representation with dense learned phase conditioning restores corrupted physiological time series
F2MNniBNZf.problem: Existing diffusion approaches to physiological signal restoration condition only on the corrupted observation and must learn cyclic (cyclostationary) structure implicitly.
F2MNniBNZf.method: Trains diffusion on a shift-covariant wavelet representation and conditions it on dense per-sample phase inferred from the corrupted input. Adds a training-free cyclostationarity index that predicts when phase conditioning helps, and antithetic coupling of reverse trajectories to reduce sampling variance.
F2MNniBNZf.key_idea: Encode cyclostationarity through shift-covariant wavelet diffusion plus dense phase conditioning inferred from the corrupted input, with antithetic coupling of reverse trajectories to cut variance.
F2MNniBNZf.evidence: Restoration experiments across four physiological modalities (ECG, PPG, EMG, EEG per reviews), plus downstream MIT-BIH and held-out cardiac dataset evaluations cited by reviewers.
F2MNniBNZf.claimed_gains: Comparable performance with fivefold fewer network evaluations via antithetic coupling; no other numbers are stated in the abstract (a review cites ECG deltaSNR of 15.87 dB vs 13.85 dB for DeScoD).
F2MNniBNZf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clear and well motivated and that experiments show clear gains over competing methods, including downstream and cross-dataset evaluation.
F2MNniBNZf.main_concern: It is not shown that the benefit comes from physiological phase rather than extra conditioning capacity, since the PPG, EMG and EEG phase encoders are trained only through the restoration loss.

0AI7eJ8UZi.one_liner: Selects test-time interventions for histopathology LVLM agents only when estimated description adequacy is low
0AI7eJ8UZi.problem: Whole-slide LVLM agents rely on regional descriptions that can be inadequate or irrelevant, and it is unclear when a frozen LVLM perceptor should be corrected and which correction to use.
0AI7eJ8UZi.method: Defines "adequate descriptions" (relevant, sufficiently complete, consistent with ground-truth evidence) and studies how they relate to downstream answer accuracy. Builds a simple controller that selects an intervention for descriptions with low estimated adequacy and accepts its output.
0AI7eJ8UZi.key_idea: An adequacy estimate for each regional description gates whether a corrective intervention is applied, instead of applying one uniformly to every description.
0AI7eJ8UZi.evidence: Four pathology LVLMs, three interventions and two WSI agents on whole-slide visual question answering; reviewers add three WSI datasets, patch-level and end-to-end results, and a probe on LVLM hidden states.
0AI7eJ8UZi.claimed_gains: The abstract states no numbers (it is cut off before the controller's results); a reviewer cites gains of 0.66 to 1.67 points over the strongest fixed-intervention baseline.
0AI7eJ8UZi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a real system-level problem of description errors propagating through WSI agents, with evaluation across multiple LVLMs, interventions, agents and datasets showing consistent positive trends.
0AI7eJ8UZi.main_concern: The adequacy signal is not validated as reflecting visual grounding (the LLM judge sees only reference text and its rubric is under-specified), and the routing margins are small and lack error bars.

hcYNKtB6ZH.one_liner: Whitens frozen vision-model features with mean and covariance from unlabeled images before cosine similarity in zero-shot evaluation
hcYNKtB6ZH.problem: Cosine similarity ignores how variance is distributed across feature directions, so when a few directions carry most variance, wrong candidates can score almost as high as correct matches.
hcYNKtB6ZH.method: Measures variance concentration with the effective dimension d_eff = (Tr Sigma)^2 / Tr(Sigma^2) of the feature covariance, then whitens features using a mean and covariance estimated on unlabeled images before computing cosine similarity. No labels or training are needed.
hcYNKtB6ZH.key_idea: Whiten features by mean and covariance before cosine similarity, because cosine variance between unrelated features is about 1/d_eff, which is large when effective dimension is small.
hcYNKtB6ZH.evidence: 36 models and 46 extraction points on semantic and geometric correspondence, point tracking and nearest-neighbour classification; reviewers cite dense evaluations such as SPair-71k and diffusion-transformer features.
hcYNKtB6ZH.claimed_gains: The abstract states d_eff ranges from 1.7 to 374 across 36 models and 46 extraction points despite feature dimensions of 768 to 6144; accuracy gains are not stated there (a review cites mean dense gains of +14.0 points for raw DiTs and +3.6 for vision encoders).
hcYNKtB6ZH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad and carefully controlled across many models and benchmarks, and that the explanation of cosine failure under concentrated variance is clear.
hcYNKtB6ZH.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited because whitening and per-channel standardization are established, and much of the gain may come from simple per-channel rescaling.

d3K1zxnxo2.one_liner: Single flow-matching velocity field jointly generates force/torque traces, trajectories and post-contact vision latents from pre-contact observations
d3K1zxnxo2.problem: Most world models do not ground predictions in plausible force/torque traces alongside robot trajectories, although forces drive contact dynamics in contact-rich manipulation.
d3K1zxnxo2.method: The Bin Dynamics Model (BDM) for robotic bin stowing is conditioned on an RGB-D image, item segmentation and the planned blade sweep. One flow-matching velocity field jointly generates a physics latent (decoded to the F/T trace and end-effector trajectory) and a vision latent predicting post-contact DINO embeddings.
d3K1zxnxo2.key_idea: One flow-matching velocity field jointly generates a physics latent (force/torque and trajectory) and a vision latent (post-contact DINO embedding) conditioned only on pre-contact information.
d3K1zxnxo2.evidence: Real-robot bin-stowing cycles (reviewers cite about 248K synchronized cycles) compared with generative action-model and regression baselines, plus ablations and downstream heads predicting space created by a sweep.
d3K1zxnxo2.claimed_gains: Reduces trajectory CRPS by about 75% (0.009 vs. 0.036) over the strongest generative action-model baseline and trajectory RMSE by about 26% (0.025 vs. 0.034 m) over the strongest baseline overall, with sub-centimeter accuracy on space-created prediction.
d3K1zxnxo2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically relevant and that the unusually large real-robot dataset with synchronized force/torque, RGB-D and trajectories is a strong testbed.
d3K1zxnxo2.main_concern: The evaluation does not establish generalization (random cycle-level split, under-defined headline metrics, anomalous ablation results), and the "world model" framing lacks multi-step state prediction.

AGaK3dDne6.one_liner: Calibrates prediction, confidence and path of pretrained diffusion models to cut reverse-channel-coding communication cost
AGaK3dDne6.problem: When pretrained diffusion and flow models are used for reverse-channel-coding image compression, mismatch between the deployed receiver and the source-marginalized ideal receiver raises communication cost.
AGaK3dDne6.method: Decomposes ideal expected RCC cost into required source information and receiver-mismatch excess, then proposes CalRCC, which calibrates prediction (trading coding cost against reconstruction quality), confidence (receiver uncertainty) and path (allocation of model evaluations along the reverse process). No new generative backbone is trained.
AGaK3dDne6.key_idea: Reduce the receiver-mismatch term of RCC cost by calibrating the receiver's prediction, confidence and evaluation path along the reverse process of a pretrained generative model.
AGaK3dDne6.evidence: Experiments with controlled DiffC, plus studies with CoD and Turbo-DDCM showing prediction calibration transfers to other diffusion codecs.
AGaK3dDne6.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract says CalRCC substantially improves practical compression with stronger fidelity and perceptual quality.
AGaK3dDne6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly organized, offers a principled cost decomposition into source information and receiver mismatch, and shows consistent improvements in reconstruction quality and rate-distortion.
AGaK3dDne6.main_concern: Gains are hard to attribute because the method combines existing techniques (LoRA fine-tuning, covariance adjustment, schedule optimization) and lacks a reconstruction-loss-only fine-tuning baseline.

XYhCP2sgxW.one_liner: A Builder model learns reusable meta-skills from Target execution feedback to construct agent harnesses with frozen weights
XYhCP2sgxW.problem: Agent performance depends on the execution environment as well as reasoning ability, and it is unclear how a Builder can learn to construct better environments for a fixed Target at test time.
XYhCP2sgxW.method: The Builder learns meta-skills, which are principles specifying when support is needed and what resources to provide, from the Target's execution feedback on a development set. It then uses the frozen skill bank to construct harnesses for unseen tasks.
XYhCP2sgxW.key_idea: The Builder distills Target execution feedback into a frozen bank of principles on when support is needed and what resources to provide, which guides harness construction on unseen tasks.
XYhCP2sgxW.evidence: Harness-Bench and NewtonBench with ablations (no-skill, direct delivery to the Target, Target-side skills, retrieved vs full bank) and a same-model Builder/Target self-improvement setting.
XYhCP2sgxW.claimed_gains: Full-bank meta-skills improve macro-average performance by 8.95 percentage points over no-skill construction and by 12.02 points over direct delivery of the same bank to the Target.
XYhCP2sgxW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the research question of teaching an environment builder rather than the task solver is clear and valuable, and the ablations and baselines are well matched to the central questions.
XYhCP2sgxW.main_concern: Generalization is shown only on held-out instances within familiar task categories with separate skill banks per benchmark, and cross-benchmark transfer is untested.

ZOYCr0n0lm.one_liner: Task-conditioned generative initializer predicts the full anisotropic RBF state, then physics-based refinement solves each PDE instance
ZOYCr0n0lm.problem: PINNs optimize a new solution model for each PDE instance, so repeated changes in parameters, boundary conditions or forcing terms are costly.
ZOYCr0n0lm.method: A decoupled offline-online framework pairs an explicit anisotropic RBF solver with a task-conditioned generative initializer that predicts coefficients, centers and kernel geometry once per query. The output is then refined under the deployment physics objective using analytic derivatives.
ZOYCr0n0lm.key_idea: A generative model amortizes the search for the complete RBF state (coefficients, centers, kernel geometry), leaving only short physics-loss refinement with analytic derivatives at deployment.
ZOYCr0n0lm.evidence: Four canonical PDE families and a transient (2+1)-dimensional Flow Mixing problem in interpolation and extrapolation regimes, compared with standard RBF initialization; reviewers also cite ablations and baselines such as Hyper-LR-PINN, PINO, P2INN-SVD, FNO and PINN.
ZOYCr0n0lm.claimed_gains: Improved finite-budget adaptation over standard RBF initialization; no numbers stated in the abstract.
ZOYCr0n0lm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and the controlled comparison against standard RBF initialization, with ablations across several PDE families, supports the learned initializer.
ZOYCr0n0lm.main_concern: It is unclear how much of the gain comes from the RBF backbone versus the learned initialization, since backbones are not compared under a matched protocol and baselines omit recent stronger models.

CIck8UfWPp.one_liner: Represents feature distributions as projected quantile displacements from a common reference for fast, small-batch generative model evaluation
CIck8UfWPp.problem: Generative model development needs repeated comparison against a real dataset using only small generated batches per checkpoint, where FID-style metrics rank models less reliably and score more slowly.
CIck8UfWPp.method: QID embeds feature distributions as projected quantile displacements from a common optimal-transport reference, with a derived finite-dimensional representation that lets small generated batches be compared efficiently with the full real dataset. fQID adds a Gaussian approximation for faster scoring.
CIck8UfWPp.key_idea: Embed feature distributions as projected quantile displacements from a common reference, compressing the real dataset into interval-averaged quantiles plus a residual that preserves the sliced Wasserstein score.
CIck8UfWPp.evidence: Over two million images across ImageNet, CIFAR-10, FFHQ, LSUN Bedroom and COCO, using Inception and DINOv2 features, compared with FID, MIND and MMD variants and with published human realism judgments.
CIck8UfWPp.claimed_gains: On small ImageNet batches in Inception space QID has nearly fivefold fewer pairwise ranking errors than FID, reference reuse roughly halves score-difference variance relative to MIND, and speedups reach 95x over full-reference kernel estimation and 43x over optimized FID.
CIck8UfWPp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written with straightforward, sound mathematics, and that precomputing the reference embedding offline gives efficient online scoring with runtime and storage gains.
CIck8UfWPp.main_concern: Fig. 3 uses each metric's own large-sample ranking as ground truth, so it does not show QID tracks true model quality, and MMD baselines reach lower model-selection error.

WNMMzIJwrn.one_liner: Prior-fitted transformer reads a Gaussian-noised release of Chebyshev moments to give differentially private in-context tabular prediction
WNMMzIJwrn.problem: Tabular foundation models such as TabPFN put training rows in context, so every prediction is a deterministic function of the sensitive rows and is incompatible with differential privacy.
WNMMzIJwrn.method: The data holder publishes once the Chebyshev moments of the target along public random projections of the features, plus the Gram matrix of the columns, noised in a single Gaussian mechanism. A transformer pretrained on millions of synthetic and public tables with on-the-fly noised releases reads this release and returns a predictive distribution for any query as post-processing.
WNMMzIJwrn.key_idea: Pretrain a transformer on noised moment releases so it learns a prior over them; every prediction is then post-processing of one DP release and costs no extra privacy budget.
WNMMzIJwrn.evidence: A large suite of tabular datasets (reviewers cite 53 regression and 33 classification tables) across privacy budgets, compared with sufficient-statistics-perturbation ridge regression and per-table DP-SGD networks, with CRPS as a metric.
WNMMzIJwrn.claimed_gains: Beats the strongest one-shot baseline (sufficient statistics perturbation for ridge regression) at every privacy budget in aggregate, and at moderate budgets gives better CRPS than a DP-SGD network trained per table; no numeric values stated.
WNMMzIJwrn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a previously unaddressed problem with a broad evaluation, and that privatizing the data once means later queries use no extra privacy budget and need no retraining.
WNMMzIJwrn.main_concern: Reviewers question the privacy proof's reliance on data-scaling parameters assumed public and the limited novelty of a combination of known DP techniques whose two-phase pretraining is not cleanly ablated.

05fSVlmt8D.one_liner: Proves every uniformly discretization-stable operator is exactly a stable Markov kernel network, unifying transformers, FNO and Flowers
05fSVlmt8D.problem: Operator-learning networks should be stable to changes in input discretization, but the space of architectures with a quantitative Holder stability bound in the Wasserstein distance between input measures has not been characterized.
05fSVlmt8D.method: Defines uniform discretization stability and proves all such operators can be written as a stable Markov kernel network. Shows the read kernels arise as solutions of regularized variational problems whose costs and regularizers recover transformers, FNO, Flowers and hybrids.
05fSVlmt8D.key_idea: Uniformly discretization-stable operators are exactly stable Markov kernel networks, whose read kernels solve regularized variational problems, with the cost and regularizer selecting the architecture.
05fSVlmt8D.evidence: Theory only: a representation theorem and stability results for variationally constructed kernels, with proofs and counterexamples; reviewers note there are no numerical experiments.
05fSVlmt8D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the representation theorem and variational framework are original, mathematically rigorous and clearly stated, and give a unified view of transformers, neural operators and Flowers.
05fSVlmt8D.main_concern: Practical significance is unclear because the existence proof builds the target operator into the kernels, does not show learnability or guide architecture design, and has no numerical experiments.

AFDCW1UrWx.one_liner: Gradient tracking over directed graphs with client-specific gradient frequencies and asymmetric, heterogeneous communication frequencies
AFDCW1UrWx.problem: In decentralized federated learning, push-pull gradient tracking over directed graphs and resource-aware handling of heterogeneous clients have been solved separately, with no algorithm covering both.
AFDCW1UrWx.method: Spod-GT adds client-specific gradient computation indicators and link-specific communication activation indicators to push-pull gradient tracking. Convergence is analyzed for non-convex objectives under a relaxed gradient diversity assumption.
AFDCW1UrWx.key_idea: Per-client gradient-computation indicators and per-link activation indicators, sampled with client- and link-specific probabilities, are folded into the push-pull gradient tracking recursion so gradient work and directed-link use are controlled separately.
AFDCW1UrWx.evidence: A convergence analysis under intermittent client participation and numerical experiments on image classification datasets against well-known gradient-tracking baselines; reviewers cite three datasets, IID and non-IID data, and five runs.
AFDCW1UrWx.claimed_gains: Proves O(1/K) consensus and stationarity guarantees for gradient tracking over directed graphs under intermittent client participation; no numeric empirical gains stated.
AFDCW1UrWx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the heterogeneous computation and communication setup is well motivated and the non-convex convergence analysis under relaxed gradient diversity is rigorous.
