vuvblinoH8.method: Builds 50K puzzles across 20 CAPTCHA types and 5 interaction modes with execution-verified screenshot-action trajectories (46K with step-by-step reasoning) and pixel-mask annotations, then trains CaptchaAgent, a single 9B policy, with supervised fine-tuning followed by RL using the environment verifier as reward.
vuvblinoH8.key_idea: Execution-verified screenshot-action trajectories with reasoning and pixel-mask annotations supervise SFT, and the environment verifier supplies the RL reward.
vuvblinoH8.evidence: Pass@1 on the dataset's 20 CAPTCHA types plus two external benchmarks, with SFT and RL stages compared.
vuvblinoH8.claimed_gains: Supervised fine-tuning reaches 70.5 Pass@1 and reinforcement learning further improves it to 71.7, with gains on two external benchmarks.
vuvblinoH8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the data pipeline is scalable, covers a wide range of CAPTCHA types, and supports SFT, RL, and closed-loop evaluation.
vuvblinoH8.main_concern: Much of the SFT gain reflects learning to submit rather than learning to solve (submission rate 20.5% to 96.8%), and RL adds little (70.5 to 71.7) without explanation.

2Q0VRQhPQp.one_liner: Native 3D material diffusion model improving texture detail via synthesized high-frequency data, multi-level feature fusion, and latent-to-pixel loss transition.
2Q0VRQhPQp.problem: Native 3D generators recover accurate geometry but struggle to reconstruct detailed textures such as text and patterns.
2Q0VRQhPQp.method: A data construction agent creates high-frequency textured 3D assets, a multi-level feature fusion (MLFF) module integrates local and global features of the conditional input, a latent-to-pixel space loss transition offsets VAE reconstruction errors, and learnable viewpoint embeddings extend the model to multi-view inputs.
2Q0VRQhPQp.key_idea: Fuses local and global conditioning features and shifts supervision from latent to pixel space, trained on agent-built high-frequency-texture assets.
2Q0VRQhPQp.evidence: Single- and multi-view experiments; reviews cite component ablations (removing high-frequency data drops PSNR from 25.48 to 22.90) on 30 TexVerse objects.
2Q0VRQhPQp.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims it significantly outperforms existing approaches in preserving texture details in single- and multi-view settings.
2Q0VRQhPQp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis is sound and that texture gains, especially for text and patterns, are visually convincing and supported by ablations.
2Q0VRQhPQp.main_concern: Evaluation is small and narrow (30 objects from TexVerse, synthetic primitive-based training data), and the closest native method NaTex is absent from the quantitative comparison.

gMj1xxF4HO.one_liner: Batched Sinkhorn solver running each OT problem in one GPU thread block that exits on convergence.
gMj1xxF4HO.problem: General GPU solvers launch every Sinkhorn update over the whole batch and run until the slowest problem converges, which is slow for loops of many small OT calls.
gMj1xxF4HO.method: Makes each problem an instance solved start to finish by one thread block when it fits on chip, freeing the slot for a pending instance on convergence; with fixed iteration counts several instances share a block, the forward map and exact gradient take one launch each, and larger instances leave later launches once converged.
gMj1xxF4HO.key_idea: Treats each OT instance as the unit of GPU execution so converged instances release their thread-block slot immediately instead of waiting for the batch's slowest problem.
gMj1xxF4HO.evidence: Tracking and domain-decomposition workloads and training layers (label assignment, point-cloud registration), compared with OTT-JAX, POT, and the Sinkhorn modules of OTA and GeoTransformer; reviews note A100-only timing.
gMj1xxF4HO.claimed_gains: 2.73-10.75x faster than OTT-JAX and 5.3-34x faster than POT on tracking and domain decomposition; 1.05-2.8x faster than OTT-JAX and 9.9-24x faster than OTA and GeoTransformer Sinkhorn modules in training layers, cutting label assignment from 16.3% to 4.7% (rest truncated).
gMj1xxF4HO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a real bottleneck and that the benchmarking is careful, with speedups visible in whole training steps and honest reporting of cases where it loses.
gMj1xxF4HO.main_concern: The ML contribution is limited (standard GPU techniques) and end-to-end impact is modest (1.13x for OTA, 1.18x for GeoTransformer), suggesting a better fit for a systems venue.

8EzC9x2YmS.one_liner: Training-free post-pruning attention recalibration that boosts visual attention in decoder regions found by causal profiling.
8EzC9x2YmS.problem: After visual token pruning, aggregate visual attention drops relative to textual attention and outputs shift toward the no-image distribution, so retained visual tokens are underused by the decoder.
8EzC9x2YmS.method: Causal Attention Profiling uses controlled interventions to find task-specific decoder regions where visual evidence is critical, and Plateau Attention Recalibration adjusts attention logits there; it plugs into existing pruning methods without changing the retained token set or adding parameters.
8EzC9x2YmS.key_idea: Locates decoder regions where visual evidence is causally critical, then recalibrates attention logits toward retained visual tokens only in those regions.
8EzC9x2YmS.evidence: Attention-allocation and output-distribution analyses across token budgets, causal interventions, and experiments on VLMs such as Qwen2.5-VL-7B and LLaVA-1.5-7B with a 500-example profiling set (per reviews).
8EzC9x2YmS.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (a review notes roughly 1% latency overhead and describes gains as modest).
8EzC9x2YmS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of whether the decoder uses retained visual tokens is well motivated and that CAR is training-free, lightweight, and compatible with existing pruning methods.
8EzC9x2YmS.main_concern: The claim that the pruning-induced drop in visual-to-text attention causes degradation is not established, since the drop is partly a mathematical consequence of removing tokens, and gains are modest relative to tuning cost.

vG3R1VKEtX.one_liner: Theory categorizing proxy-reward errors as harmful, benign, or beneficial by their effect on ground-truth reward under policy gradient.
vG3R1VKEtX.problem: Reward-model quality metrics such as ranking accuracy treat every incorrect reward as harmful, although some errors may not hurt or may even help policy-gradient training.
vG3R1VKEtX.method: They analyze which outputs attract probability during policy gradient optimization, categorize reward errors by their effect on the increase in ground-truth reward, and derive reward-model evaluation metrics (such as HAcc) that account for how harmful errors are.
vG3R1VKEtX.key_idea: Track which outputs gain probability under policy gradient to classify each reward error by its effect on ground-truth reward; errors that prevent stalling around mediocre outputs can help.
vG3R1VKEtX.evidence: Theoretical analysis, RLHF experiments with models up to 3B comparing the new metrics against ranking accuracy, and insights for reward design with verifiable rewards.
vG3R1VKEtX.claimed_gains: The new metrics typically correlate better than ranking accuracy with language-model performance after RLHF, though gaps remain; no numbers are stated.
vG3R1VKEtX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper challenges the assumption that reward errors are always harmful and gives clear, rigorous theory, with the beneficial-error result being non-obvious.
vG3R1VKEtX.main_concern: The proposed HAcc metric is a simple expected-reward threshold that may not capture the factors in the theory, and its correlation with downstream RLHF performance remains weak and sometimes negative.

K3baFPpT3v.one_liner: Offline augmentation adds verified short action bridges between observations in robot demonstrations, stitching suboptimal and failed trajectories.
K3baFPpT3v.problem: Robot demonstrations contain useful behavior even in inefficient or failed episodes, but finding and verifying connections between trajectories is hard in high-dimensional data, where prior stitching methods rely on low-dimensional states.
K3baFPpT3v.method: NEEDLE identifies candidate connections and adds short action bridges (generated with an inverse dynamics model per reviews) that pass a feasibility verifier, using only RGB images, proprioception, and episode-level outcomes. A sampling technique adds accepted bridges to policy training without synthesizing intermediate images or discarding the original demonstrations.
K3baFPpT3v.key_idea: Verified local action bridges between recorded observations let policies learn alternative actions, with bridge sampling that keeps original demonstrations and avoids synthesizing intermediate images.
K3baFPpT3v.evidence: Real-robot tasks against baselines, plus simulated manipulation tasks, verifier ablations, and stitching-type ablations according to reviews.
K3baFPpT3v.claimed_gains: On real-robot tasks, improves success rate over the strongest baseline on each task by an average of 21 percentage points.
K3baFPpT3v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method recovers useful supervision from imperfect or failed demonstrations without extra robot interaction, and that the real-robot results and ablations are a strength.
K3baFPpT3v.main_concern: The pipeline is heuristic and heavy, the verifier only checks local reachability so accepted bridges can still add wrong supervision, candidate retrieval is under-described, and real-robot evaluation covers only two tasks and two baselines.

OBWJXhjqTU.one_liner: Training-free MM-DiT grounding: propagates a high-confidence concept anchor as a one-hot seed over a hybrid self-attention graph.
OBWJXhjqTU.problem: Attention-based concept grounding in MM-DiTs yields overlapping activations on visually confusable concepts, a failure mode the authors call concept leakage.
OBWJXhjqTU.method: AnchorDiff selects a high-confidence anchor from the concept-to-image attention map and propagates it as a one-hot seed over a graph from image-to-image self-attention, using output-space similarity for within-object propagation and a row-wise attention gate to suppress cross-object edges. The authors also build the Multi-Concept Confusion Dataset with per-concept masks.
OBWJXhjqTU.key_idea: Separate semantic localization (anchor from cross-attention) from structural refinement (seed diffusion over a gated self-attention graph) to stop activation spilling onto non-target objects.
OBWJXhjqTU.evidence: Experiments on ImageNet-Segmentation, PascalVOC, and the new Multi-Concept Confusion Dataset, with ablations on the attention gate and propagation steps.
OBWJXhjqTU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and training-free, and that the gains on confusable-object settings and the multi-concept benchmark with per-concept masks are useful.
OBWJXhjqTU.main_concern: Related work and novelty are under-covered (DiffSeg, M2N2, iSeg, and SeeDiff use similar self-attention propagation), and the method always selects an anchor, so absent concepts and wrong anchors are not handled.

Pi6m3hGMbz.one_liner: Decouples logical optimizer assignment from physical parameter layout to balance matrix-optimizer work in Megatron-style distributed training.
Pi6m3hGMbz.problem: Matrix-based optimizers like Shampoo, Muon, and SOAP need whole-matrix updates, which conflicts with tensor fragmentation in distributed frameworks such as Megatron, and existing fixes are redundant or break communication overlap.
Pi6m3hGMbz.method: For data parallelism, alpha-Balanced Static Partitioning preserves tensor atomicity and communication overlap while balancing optimizer load. For tensor parallelism, an asynchronous-compute design assigns complete matrix updates to different ranks, and Micro-Group Scheduling balances tasks with fused transfers.
Pi6m3hGMbz.key_idea: Assign each complete matrix update to a single rank and balance tasks with static partitioning and micro-group scheduling, separate from parameter placement.
Pi6m3hGMbz.evidence: Qwen3 models up to 32B parameters on 256 GPUs, with Muon, Shampoo, and SOAP loss-curve comparisons.
Pi6m3hGMbz.claimed_gains: A 1.57x speedup in end-to-end iteration time and a 5.8x reduction in optimizer latency on Qwen3 models up to 32B parameters on 256 GPUs.
Pi6m3hGMbz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets a concrete systems conflict between matrix updates and ZeRO/TP layouts, with clear motivation, a well-organized design, and strong experiments.
Pi6m3hGMbz.main_concern: The approach reuses standard LPT and greedy bin-packing with static planning, evidence for exact optimizer equivalence rests on loss curves, and results are hard to reproduce or apply at smaller scales.

hbRAmIGZ4d.one_liner: Dual conditional flows model dominant arrival-time patterns and high-error residual tails for seismic phase picking, joined by adaptive vector-field routing.
hbRAmIGZ4d.problem: Deep learning seismic phase pickers have heavy-tailed error distributions, where a small fraction of large arrival-time errors compromises phase association and event localization.
hbRAmIGZ4d.method: SeisTailFlow builds parallel Main and Tail Flows, using out-of-sample residuals to find waveform conditions with elevated error risk. It combines residual-based tail supervision, background-referenced spectral enhancement, extreme-value regularization, and adaptive vector-field routing.
hbRAmIGZ4d.key_idea: Identify high-error waveform conditions from out-of-sample residuals, give them a dedicated Tail Flow, and route between Main and Tail vector fields adaptively.
hbRAmIGZ4d.evidence: Synthetic data and the STEAD dataset, with event-level splits and out-of-fold tail labels, measuring overall accuracy, probabilistic quality, and tail-error metrics.
hbRAmIGZ4d.claimed_gains: Improves overall picking accuracy and probabilistic prediction quality while substantially reducing tail errors and large-error events; no numbers stated.
hbRAmIGZ4d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that targeting tail errors is relevant and the synthetic and STEAD experiments show gains in overall accuracy and tail-error reduction, with leakage-aware splits and tail-risk metrics.
hbRAmIGZ4d.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to synthetic data and STEAD, the overall MAE gain is small relative to the added complexity, and tail-metric consistency and Tail Flow training details are under-specified.

0kTSGH9ZPN.one_liner: Derives change-of-measure inequalities from the data processing inequality applied to an event indicator, covering f-divergences, Renyi, and alpha-mutual information.
0kTSGH9ZPN.problem: Existing change of measure inequalities rely on more complex variational arguments and are not unified across divergence families.
0kTSGH9ZPN.method: Applies the data processing inequality to a Bernoulli channel induced by an event to obtain bounds in f-divergence (KL, chi-squared), Renyi divergence, and alpha-mutual information (maximal leakage), then applies them to generalization error, PAC-Bayes, differential privacy, and memorization.
0kTSGH9ZPN.key_idea: Reduce change of measure to the data processing inequality for the Bernoulli channel of an event indicator, yielding exact event-DPI relations.
0kTSGH9ZPN.evidence: Theoretical derivations with applications to generalization error analysis, PAC-Bayesian theory, differential privacy, and data memorization; no experiments are stated.
0kTSGH9ZPN.claimed_gains: Tighter inequalities and stronger guarantees while recovering best-known results through simplified analyses; no numbers stated.
0kTSGH9ZPN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the proof elementary, intuitive, and easy to use, with tighter bounds than the classical strong converse lemma and a notable memorization result.
0kTSGH9ZPN.main_concern: Using an event indicator in the data processing inequality is an established information-theoretic trick, so novelty is limited, and the unification reads like a review that suffers under the page limit.

whbIKUx7kT.one_liner: Cycle-consistency objective that trains diffusion policies on action-free video via inverse and forward dynamics sharing one latent action.
whbIKUx7kT.problem: Action-labeled demonstrations are far scarcer than action-free video, and imitation constrains the policy, forward-dynamics and inverse-dynamics roles only on the labeled demonstrations.
whbIKUx7kT.method: Enforces that latent actions inferred from a transition suffice for forward evolution under the same policy latent space, turning unlabeled video into supervision without fabricating action labels. Slot-wise latent mixup brings out-of-domain transitions in-domain, and a staged schedule with batch-relative weighting addresses gradient conflict with the supervised signal.
whbIKUx7kT.key_idea: Require the latent action inferred from a transition to reproduce that transition under the policy's own forward role, making video a self-supervised cycle target.
whbIKUx7kT.evidence: Three policy architectures, three video sources, two benchmarks (RoboCasa and Libero), and real-robot tasks, with ablations of naive cycle training, mixup and scheduling.
whbIKUx7kT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using action-free video without pseudo-action labels is a relevant problem and that the evaluation across backbones, video sources and a real robot, including honest negative-transfer ablations, is broad.
whbIKUx7kT.main_concern: Gains are not shown to come from the video rather than the added inverse-dynamics auxiliary task, since a matched three-mode supervised baseline is missing.

gJGOnXZUG0.one_liner: Synthesizes maximally permissive shields for tool-calling LLM agents from first-order safety requirements over relational application state.
gJGOnXZUG0.problem: Existing guardrails enforce safety over simplified views of application state, so they may permit unsafe calls or unnecessarily block safe ones.
gJGOnXZUG0.method: From a first-order safety requirement, tool specifications, legal initial states, and uncontrollable environment actions, RelShield gives a safety-game fixed-point characterization of the maximally permissive shield. It proves synthesis undecidable in the relational setting, gives a sound symbolic procedure, and gives a sound and complete method for instances whose reachable safe states have bounded size.
gJGOnXZUG0.key_idea: Compute the largest set of grounded tool calls that keeps the safety requirement maintainable, as the fixed point of a safety game over relational state.
gJGOnXZUG0.evidence: Undecidability, soundness, and bounded-size completeness theorems, plus an implementation of both procedures evaluated on relational instances.
gJGOnXZUG0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that specifying safety over relational application state, with guarantees independent of the agent's behavior, is a well-chosen problem level with a clear fixed-point characterization.
gJGOnXZUG0.main_concern: Empirical support is thin, with the symbolic procedure solving 0 of 9 extension instances, and the advance over related formal-methods work and the modeling effort are not established.

k0wjCXb6ut.one_liner: Benchmark of 100 coding tasks with separate utility and safety verifiers testing whether skill-using agents minimize data access and privileges.
k0wjCXb6ut.problem: Coding-agent benchmarks measure task success but not whether the agent completes the task using only the minimal data and privileges required.
k0wjCXb6ut.method: A Workflow Analyzer identifies privacy and security vulnerabilities in skill-conditioned coding agents and patches existing skill-use tasks through iterative task evolution into 100 synthetic tasks with benign but minimization-relevant requirements. Each task runs in Docker with independent utility and safety verifiers.
k0wjCXb6ut.key_idea: Add minimization requirements to existing skill tasks and verify them with executable tests that check trajectories and deliverables separately from utility checks.
k0wjCXb6ut.evidence: Evaluations of multiple models and harnesses in Docker environments; the abstract is cut off before the results.
k0wjCXb6ut.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a reviewer cites a safety failure rate of approximately 62% among functionally successful runs.
k0wjCXb6ut.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark addresses an important, understudied issue of unintended data and privilege violations during benign skill use, and that separating utility from safety reveals a clear gap.
k0wjCXb6ut.main_concern: The analysis says little about why failures occur or how they split by violation type, and verifier validation is incomplete, so the reported failure rates are hard to interpret.

4UNFty26sh.one_liner: Systematic comparison of summarizing versus per-session prediction and isolated versus comparative prompting for LLM prediction of product conversion rates.
4UNFty26sh.problem: It is unclear how to combine individual behavioral histories in an LLM to predict the fraction of users who take an action, given bias-variance trade-offs in where to aggregate and what to compare within a prompt.
4UNFty26sh.method: The paper predicts product-level conversion rates from browsing sessions without task-specific training, varying whether sessions are summarized before inference or predicted individually and averaged, and whether products are evaluated separately or together in one prompt.
4UNFty26sh.key_idea: Evaluating products together in one prompt lets the model infer what is typical, which helps summaries far more than per-session predictions, trading lower bias for context-dependent noise.
4UNFty26sh.evidence: Five LLMs and two e-commerce datasets, scored by Spearman correlation with observed rates, with matched 80-session controls and standardization and repetition ablations noted by reviewers.
4UNFty26sh.claimed_gains: Comparative summaries achieve the highest Spearman correlation with observed rates in 12 of 15 settings, with no alternative significantly better.
4UNFty26sh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two-axis design is clear and the matched-session controls and ablations give practically useful findings that more behavioral detail is not better and that comparative summaries win.
4UNFty26sh.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the paper combines established techniques and offers no generalizable principle beyond the e-commerce observations, and its uncertainty intervals ignore resampling and reruns.

JhRGP5aOI9.one_liner: Three-stage training for explainable hateful meme detection: background knowledge, then detection, then boundary alignment, built on agentic knowledge construction.
JhRGP5aOI9.problem: Explain-then-detect methods train explanation generation and label prediction together, causing objective interference that yields detection worse than simple SFT baselines.
JhRGP5aOI9.method: ProKDA first builds external background knowledge about each meme with an agentic pipeline, then trains in three stages (background knowledge learning, hatefulness detection learning, hatefulness boundary alignment), each with a single objective. Reviewers describe the stages as using retrieval, SFT, and DPO with GPT-4o-generated supervision.
JhRGP5aOI9.key_idea: Separates knowledge learning from decision learning by training one objective per stage in sequence, so background knowledge is converted into detection decisions without task interference.
JhRGP5aOI9.evidence: Macro-F1 comparisons on HMC, MAMI, and PrideMM with 3B and 7B backbones against direct-detection and explain-then-detect SFT, plus stage ablations (Table 2).
JhRGP5aOI9.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (reviewers report 7B macro-F1 gains of 8.26, 4.71, and 2.56 points over direct-detection SFT on HMC, MAMI, and PrideMM).
JhRGP5aOI9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the progressive, decoupled training is well motivated, with stage ablations showing each stage adds to detection performance.
JhRGP5aOI9.main_concern: Limited novelty, since the method combines established components (retrieval, SFT, DPO, teacher-generated data), and the experiments do not isolate task interference as the cause of the gain.

5FWBc0Cays.one_liner: 4D Point Splatting fits moving oriented points to real mmWave radar captures via differentiable range-Doppler splatting.
5FWBc0Cays.problem: Radar datasets lag vision and language, and existing synthesis methods (forward simulators, learned generators, static-scene inverse renderers) cannot fit a real capture of a moving body, leaving a sim2real gap.
5FWBc0Cays.method: 4DPS represents the scene as oriented points carrying material, normal, and velocity, each splatted into range and Doppler bins to render the raw complex radar return, so standard signal processing yields any representation. The scene is initialized from the capture's camera and fit to the real capture.
5FWBc0Cays.key_idea: Give each splatted point a velocity and render its closed-form Doppler response, so a moving body is fit end to end through the raw radar return.
5FWBc0Cays.evidence: Fits of 235 sequences on HuPR and 100 on RT-Pose, signal-level fidelity metrics, and a downstream RT-Pose pose model trained on renders only (abstract cut off).
5FWBc0Cays.claimed_gains: Median correlations of 0.940 and 0.830 on range-azimuth, 0.829 and 0.695 on range-Doppler, and 0.988 and 0.966 on micro-Doppler (HuPR and RT-Pose); a model trained on renders alone reaches 21.9 cm MPJPE versus 16.7 cm for real training and 127.6 cm for RF-Genesis.
5FWBc0Cays.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is practical, with explicit differentiable velocity and a closed-form Doppler response, and that evaluation across two datasets, signal representations, and ablations is comprehensive with high-fidelity renders.
5FWBc0Cays.main_concern: Downstream value is not shown: renders fitted to existing captures train worse than real data and do not consistently help when added, and RF-Genesis is the only, unequally matched, baseline.

dWYdDrKqaH.one_liner: Contrastive planner conditioned on a scalar preference via FiLM and low-rank modulation to adjust plan conservativeness at inference.
dWYdDrKqaH.problem: Existing contrastive planning learns a single latent geometry, so it cannot trade task efficiency against risk exposure for the same start-goal query.
dWYdDrKqaH.method: MoMo jointly conditions the representation geometry through Feature-Wise Linear Modulation and the latent prediction operator through low-rank neural modulation, so a scalar preference changes plan conservativeness without retraining. They show the formulation preserves the probability density ratio needed for inference-driven contrastive planning.
dWYdDrKqaH.key_idea: Condition both the contrastive encoder (FiLM) and the latent transition operator (low-rank modulation) on a scalar preference while preserving the density-ratio encoding.
dWYdDrKqaH.evidence: Six environments compared with state-augmentation baselines, plus density-ratio and Gaussianity checks in the appendix and limited comparisons with MODULI, CDT, and CCAC on one task per reviews.
dWYdDrKqaH.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says plan safety adapts smoothly to preferences with improved temporal and preferential consistency over state-augmentation baselines, without numbers)
dWYdDrKqaH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that steering plans at query time with a scalar preference is useful, labels come from the data itself, and the density-ratio structure is preserved with consistent results across environments.
dWYdDrKqaH.main_concern: Baselines are narrow (mostly state-augmented variants, other preference-conditioned methods only on the simplest task), and generalization and scalability beyond one high-dimensional task are untested.

xyN5QuM71z.one_liner: Defines Visual Simile Generation and scores text-to-image outputs on subject anchoring, attribute transfer, and non-literal abstraction with CanonScore.
xyN5QuM71z.problem: Text-to-image models given a simile such as 'a moon that looks like a boat' often draw a plain boat, a moon beside a boat, or a moon with masts, failing to transfer only the implicated attribute.
xyN5QuM71z.method: Formalizes a task requiring the subject to dominate, the implicated attribute of the comparison object to transfer, and no concrete features of the comparison object to appear; builds VSG-Bench of 549 prompts across 13 resemblance relations, each annotated with the licensed attribute and forbidden features, and a composite CanonScore.
xyN5QuM71z.key_idea: Annotate per prompt which single attribute may transfer and which concrete features are forbidden, then score subject anchoring, transfer, and literalization separately.
xyN5QuM71z.evidence: VSG-Bench of 549 prompts across 13 resemblance relations and four axes, evaluated on multiple text-to-image models with several judges and prompt rewrites.
xyN5QuM71z.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract reports a 549-prompt benchmark but no performance numbers.
xyN5QuM71z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the decomposition into subject preservation, attribute transfer, and over-literalization a useful diagnostic that goes beyond single-score prompt alignment, with robustness checks across judges.
xyN5QuM71z.main_concern: CanonScore's anchor component mixes subject accuracy with attribute transfer, and the manual annotations lack independent verification or inter-annotator evidence.

3PCKucJRZM.one_liner: Compresses scientific tensors of any dimensionality under pointwise error bounds using a dimension-agnostic GNN predictor pretrained on synthetic fields.
3PCKucJRZM.problem: Learned codecs optimize aggregate distortion rather than user-specified pointwise error bounds, and mostly target fixed field dimensionality or need costly retraining.
3PCKucJRZM.method: An error-bounded codec with a GNN-based, dimension-agnostic learned predictor over axial neighborhoods, pretrained on synthetic 2D and 4D fields and evaluated with and without domain fine-tuning on 13 scientific fields in 3D to 5D.
3PCKucJRZM.key_idea: Use a GNN over axial neighborhoods as a dimension-agnostic predictor inside an error-bounded codec, pretrained on synthetic 2D and 4D fields and transferred to 3D and 5D.
3PCKucJRZM.evidence: Pretraining on synthetic 2D and 4D fields and evaluation on 13 scientific fields in 3D to 5D against SZ3 and other compressors, with and without domain fine-tuning.
3PCKucJRZM.claimed_gains: Consistently competitive with SZ3, achieving an 18.1% average improvement and greater consistency across all domains than other compressors.
3PCKucJRZM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the dimension-agnostic GNN design sound and practically relevant, enabling transfer from 2D/4D pretraining to 3D/5D with promising compression results.
3PCKucJRZM.main_concern: Bitrate gains come with a large throughput penalty (encoding and decoding roughly 10 to 20 times slower than SZ3) and are modest on real 5D data.

QqbW0SAfJR.one_liner: Encodes LLM acquisition-function recommendations as priors updated by Gaussian-UCB bandit inference from BO trajectory statistics.
QqbW0SAfJR.problem: Bayesian optimization performance depends on choices such as the acquisition function that need expertise, and LLMs struggle to track long optimization histories, making their recommendations unreliable.
QqbW0SAfJR.method: LPG-UCB encodes LLM recommendations as priors over acquisition-function preferences and updates them by Bayesian inference using summary statistics from the BO trajectory. It is modeled as a non-stationary rotting bandit with a sublinear expected cumulative regret bound under appropriate conditions.
QqbW0SAfJR.key_idea: Treat acquisition-function selection as a bandit whose arm priors come from the LLM and are corrected by Gaussian updates from observed BO outcomes, reducing reliance on any single recommendation.
QqbW0SAfJR.evidence: A regret bound and experiments on diverse synthetic benchmarks against fixed acquisition functions, adaptive portfolios, and LLM-based baselines (the abstract text is cut off).
QqbW0SAfJR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining LLM priors with principled bandit-based acquisition selection is an interesting approach, backed by a regret analysis and a broad comparison on synthetic benchmarks.
QqbW0SAfJR.main_concern: The LLM prior's contribution is not isolated: the bandit often overrides the LLM, real-world benchmarks and key LLM baselines are missing, and the LLM recommendations themselves are not analyzed.

tK4yRayph8.one_liner: Linear probes on residual-stream activations detect silent wrong CoT steps; probe-direction steering induces or repairs errors causally.
tK4yRayph8.problem: Answer-level verification misses silent restoration, where a model reaches the correct answer while producing a fluent, verifiably wrong intermediate reasoning step that is never corrected.
tK4yRayph8.method: The paper measures silent restoration across twelve model configurations and four domains, trains linear probes to identify wrong steps, builds a probe-plus-distance detector, and tests causality by steering along the probe direction.
tK4yRayph8.key_idea: Wrong steps show a uniform upward shift in linear probe score across interior layers, even before generation; a probe-plus-distance detector exploits this and steering along it is causal.
tK4yRayph8.evidence: Twelve model configurations and four domains for prevalence, probes on nine configurations, an out-of-domain detector comparison against baselines, and steering interventions.
tK4yRayph8.claimed_gains: Silent restoration reaches 32% of answer-correct MedQA traces for Qwen2.5-7B; probes identify wrong steps at 0.73-0.91 AUROC; the detector reaches 0.792 out-of-domain AUROC versus 0.655 for the strongest token-uncertainty signal; steering induces errors in 46% of correct steps.
tK4yRayph8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that probes separating correct from wrong reasoning steps despite correct answers is an interesting finding, supported by comprehensive experiments across domains and models with strong baselines.
tK4yRayph8.main_concern: Novelty and context: several results (mid-layer probing, pre-commitment signal, silent error correction) are expected from or already in prior work, and the 'first' claims misrepresent that literature.

zY2kqg5ofo.one_liner: Closed-loop long-session evaluation of full-duplex speech models, mitigated by privileged-context self-distillation LoRA and two-resolution KV context.
zY2kqg5ofo.problem: How full-duplex spoken dialogue models behave over extended sessions is poorly understood, and responsiveness, spoken content quality, and voice consistency degrade over time.
zY2kqg5ofo.method: The paper introduces a closed-loop long-session evaluation framework, a self-distillation-based LoRA adaptation, and a Two-Resolution Context (TRC) architecture that keeps recent interaction in full detail while compressing older history into key-value representations.
zY2kqg5ofo.key_idea: Use a teacher with compressed memory of earlier turns to supervise on-policy self-distillation, and compress older history into key-value states while keeping recent turns in full detail.
zY2kqg5ofo.evidence: Three publicly available models with distinct architectures evaluated on long-session stability, information retention, and computational efficiency (PersonaPlex, Raon-SpeechChat, and MiniCPM-o per reviews).
zY2kqg5ofo.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says LoRA adaptation mitigates degradation, but the text is cut off before any numbers).
zY2kqg5ofo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree long-session reliability of full-duplex models is an under-explored, valuable problem and that the self-distillation and TRC methods give meaningful gains in several settings.
zY2kqg5ofo.main_concern: Evaluation realism: the cascaded user simulator always waits for the complete model response and never interrupts or backchannels, so the methods are untested under real full-duplex interaction.

t1R6F2fdM0.one_liner: Discrete operation tokens compress reusable reasoning patterns while retaining explicit instance-specific execution text.
t1R6F2fdM0.problem: Long multimodal reasoning traces contain redundancy, while shared latent spaces mix reusable procedures with problem-specific information.
t1R6F2fdM0.method: SLR segments reasoning traces, separates abstract operations from concrete executions, and clusters operations into a discrete codebook. Training replaces operation descriptions with codebook tokens interleaved with explicit execution text.
t1R6F2fdM0.key_idea: Encode recurring reasoning operations as discrete codebook tokens while leaving their instance-specific computations explicit.
t1R6F2fdM0.evidence: Three MLLM configurations undergo multimodal reasoning evaluation, with four-benchmark Qwen3-VL results and token, codebook, and initialization ablations.
t1R6F2fdM0.claimed_gains: SLR reduces mean output length by 10-35% compared with standard SFT while matching or exceeding its accuracy in the reported evaluations.
t1R6F2fdM0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating reusable reasoning operations from instance-specific content and the resulting shorter outputs.
t1R6F2fdM0.main_concern: Missing equally concise natural-language controls leave codebook benefits confounded with teacher-generated trace rewriting.

mOatJUlLCe.one_liner: Predictable inter-chunk GPU kernels and affine latency models guide unequal attention partitions and thread-array scheduling.
mOatJUlLCe.problem: Equal-sized attention chunks can have unequal latency, causing load imbalance and GPU underutilization on heterogeneous requests.
mOatJUlLCe.method: TailorAttention combines inter-chunk pipelining and transposed tensor-core dataflows in Hopper and Blackwell kernels. An affine-latency scheduler jointly selects chunk sizes and CTA assignments while accounting for reduction overhead.
mOatJUlLCe.key_idea: Make chunk latency predictable through kernel design, then jointly schedule unequal chunks and CTA assignments using latency and reduction-cost estimates.
mOatJUlLCe.evidence: Experiments span GPUs, models, query lengths, GQA settings, and workload mixtures against FlashAttention-3/4 and FlashInfer, with a provable additive scheduling bound.
mOatJUlLCe.claimed_gains: TailorAttention improves attention-kernel performance by up to 4.96x and reduces end-to-end latency by 27.1% over FlashAttention-3/4 and FlashInfer.
mOatJUlLCe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value linking kernel latency predictability to scheduling for heterogeneous attention workloads.
mOatJUlLCe.main_concern: Incomplete related-method comparisons and coarse ablations leave the distinct contributions of kernel changes and scheduling unclear.

5bN6X1yQE9.one_liner: Retrieval gains over raw queries and structural preference rewards train less repetitive task decomposition for tool retrieval.
5bN6X1yQE9.problem: Optimizing retrieval metrics directly can reward redundant subtasks and undermine generalization to unseen tools.
5bN6X1yQE9.method: PCTD rewards the retrieval-ranking improvement of a decomposition over the raw query. A preference reward adds supervision for logical coherence and atomicity, and MTDTool benchmarks mobile multi-turn decomposition.
5bN6X1yQE9.key_idea: Combine a reward for retrieval improvement over the undecomposed query with preferences for coherent, atomic subtasks.
5bN6X1yQE9.evidence: Experiments and ablations evaluate retrieval, decomposition quality, and unseen-tool generalization, including the MTDTool benchmark.
5bN6X1yQE9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the motivation for controlling repetitive decompositions and measuring improvement over direct-query retrieval.
5bN6X1yQE9.main_concern: The causal explanation for reward hacking remains weakly established because the cited baseline failure is not directly tested and the counterfactual reward is heuristic.

aJqai0DsRG.one_liner: Coupling-aware flow matching combines doubly robust training with score-corrected stochastic sampling for counterfactual outcome generation.
aJqai0DsRG.problem: Counterfactual generation needs finite-step error guarantees that account for learned source-target couplings and nuisance models.
aJqai0DsRG.method: The approach learns a source-target coupling and trains flow and score fields with a sample-split, doubly robust objective. A score-corrected stochastic sampler follows a Gaussian-smoothed interpolation.
aJqai0DsRG.key_idea: Control Euler sampling error through source-target displacement moments under the learned coupling.
aJqai0DsRG.evidence: Coupling-sensitive KL bounds and finite-sample guarantees accompany experiments on synthetic data and semi-synthetic MNIST images.
aJqai0DsRG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical motivation, counterexamples, and coupling-sensitive sampling guarantees.
aJqai0DsRG.main_concern: The experiments provide limited evidence for realistic, high-dimensional generation and different sampling budgets.

cLuhZLRLNf.one_liner: A denoising-process critic supplies intermediate coordination guidance to decentralized diffusion policies in offline multi-agent reinforcement learning.
cLuhZLRLNf.problem: Supervision focused on final joint actions can leave decentralized diffusion denoising poorly coordinated.
cLuhZLRLNf.method: DiMAC evaluates intermediate denoising states through their expected final joint-action value. Coalition value decomposition supplies agent-wise and pairwise guidance, weighted by denoising-step reliability.
cLuhZLRLNf.key_idea: Decompose centralized denoising-prefix values into decentralized singleton and pairwise guidance signals.
cLuhZLRLNf.evidence: Experiments on MPE and SMAC compare offline MARL and diffusion baselines, with ablations and gradient analyses examining process supervision.
cLuhZLRLNf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find explicit intermediate denoising supervision meaningful and the ablations supportive of its effectiveness.
cLuhZLRLNf.main_concern: Out-of-distribution final actions and mixed coalition prefixes may make critic-derived process supervision unreliable.

KhDznFL1nO.one_liner: A shared low-rank residual adapter modifies expert inputs while keeping local MoE routing frozen.
KhDznFL1nO.problem: Mixture-of-Experts language models share the same token representation for routing and expert computation, coupling router updates with expert input adaptation during downstream tuning.
KhDznFL1nO.method: Low-Rank Expert Adaptation (LREA/LoREAL) keeps each MoE layer's router and experts frozen while passing the layer input through a parallel shared low-rank residual adapter (2dr parameters per layer plus optional N per-expert scalars) before feeding selected experts. This alters what frozen experts receive locally without changing the representation used by that layer's router.
KhDznFL1nO.key_idea: Keep local MoE routers and experts frozen while passing expert inputs through a shared parallel low-rank residual adapter.
KhDznFL1nO.evidence: Experiments on OLMoE-1B-7B evaluate continued pretraining and supervised fine-tuning against router tuning and expert LoRA across parameter budgets, paired with nonlinearity, placement, and router-capacity ablations.
KhDznFL1nO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared expert-input adapter architecture is simple, clearly presented, avoids scaling parameters with expert count, and reduces forgetting compared to router tuning.
KhDznFL1nO.main_concern: Reviewers point out conceptual overlap with LatentMoE and representation fine-tuning methods such as ReFT and (IA)3, negligible perplexity gains over parameter-matched expert LoRA, and a matrix mismatch in Appendix B.

nwpLjtMBqS.one_liner: Reasoning-graph extraction and type-constrained entity replacement synthesize low-leakage RAG evaluation benchmarks from seed datasets.
nwpLjtMBqS.problem: Existing RAG benchmarks contain questions that LLMs can already answer from parametric memory due to pretraining contamination and benchmark aging, confounding retrieval evaluation.
nwpLjtMBqS.method: SeedRG extracts reasoning graphs from seed question-context pairs and synthesizes structurally matched new instances through type-constrained entity replacement. It then applies a reasoning-graph consistency check to preserve task difficulty and a knowledge-leakage filter to remove items solvable without retrieval.
nwpLjtMBqS.key_idea: Extract reasoning graphs from seed question-context pairs, substitute entities under type constraints, and filter instances failing graph consistency or solvable without retrieval.
nwpLjtMBqS.evidence: Experiments quantify knowledge leakage across three existing RAG benchmark datasets and evaluate the low-leakage benchmarks generated by SeedRG.
nwpLjtMBqS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper provides systematic evidence of knowledge leakage in existing RAG datasets and presents a clear graph-constrained pipeline to preserve reasoning structure during regeneration.
nwpLjtMBqS.main_concern: Reviewers question whether SeedRG offers clear advantages over simply filtering out questions solvable without retrieved context or using dynamic real-time benchmarks, and note missing comparisons to AnonyRAG.

f2VXKzKbm0.one_liner: Nash decoding treats token positions as players and iteratively revises tokens using full-context conditional probabilities.
f2VXKzKbm0.problem: Text revision lacks an explicit token-level equilibrium criterion for deciding when further local edits cease to help.
f2VXKzKbm0.method: The paper defines a game where each token position chooses a vocabulary item to maximize its log conditional probability. Nash decoding iteratively revises tokens toward approximate equilibrium, with convergence guarantees for conditionals compatible with a joint distribution.
f2VXKzKbm0.key_idea: Token-wise best-response revision seeks a sequence in which no single position can substantially increase its full-context log probability.
f2VXKzKbm0.evidence: Potential-game analysis and convergence theory accompany masked-model evaluations on CLAPNQ, PubMedQA, and CoQA.
f2VXKzKbm0.claimed_gains: Masked-model Nash equilibria achieve higher F1 and ROUGE scores than autoregressive models up to 18× larger without fine-tuning or retraining.
f2VXKzKbm0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the game-theoretic formulation and explicit equilibrium-based account of iterative text revision.
f2VXKzKbm0.main_concern: Reviewers agree that comparisons against existing iterative-refinement, edit-based, and remasking decoding methods are insufficient.

Z5FryQMBSS.one_liner: An ordinal hidden-state router selects location-disclosure granularity, then route-specific activation steering controls VLM responses.
Z5FryQMBSS.problem: VLMs can disclose location details beyond the granularity warranted by an image's visual privacy context.
Z5FryQMBSS.method: The method fits an ordinal granularity router to pre-generation privacy representations. During decoding, disclosure-level-conditioned interventions steer hidden states according to the selected route.
Z5FryQMBSS.key_idea: Routing along an ordered hidden-state disclosure direction selects the target granularity for route-conditioned decoding interventions.
Z5FryQMBSS.evidence: Experiments cover four VLM backbones, routing and steering diagnostics, general capability benchmarks, and transfer to a dataset with a different privacy taxonomy.
Z5FryQMBSS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating contextual disclosure-policy selection from control of the generated response.
Z5FryQMBSS.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the observed alignment gains establish reliable disclosure control, given unsteered intermediate routes and failures under adversarial prompting.

1UIq0cjyZB.one_liner: SWAGES scores task-VM assignments with system-wide graph attention and guides evolutionary search using critic-derived gradient subspaces.
1UIq0cjyZB.problem: Dynamic workflow schedulers miss interactions across workflows, while larger globally aware policies make reinforcement learning and evolutionary search costly.
1UIq0cjyZB.method: SWAN models active workflows, ready tasks, VMs, and compatibility in a shared graph context. GUIDES reuses rollout transitions to train twin critics whose surrogate gradients define a low-dimensional subspace for fitness-based evolutionary search.
1UIq0cjyZB.key_idea: Global graph attention scores assignments while critic-derived gradient directions restrict evolutionary policy search to a low-dimensional subspace.
1UIq0cjyZB.evidence: Experiments compare scheduling methods across workflow settings and include four continuous-control settings noted in the reviews.
1UIq0cjyZB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate joint task prioritization and VM allocation under a global context and report encouraging scheduling results.
1UIq0cjyZB.main_concern: Reviewers flag inconsistent total-cost values across apparently identical experimental settings, weakening confidence in the reported results.

8VfxiMg64h.one_liner: AR-Retrofit adds gated cross-depth residual corrections to frozen decoders and reuses routing signals for selective layer execution.
8VfxiMg64h.problem: Adding attention residuals to pretrained models can require costly backbone retraining and add inference overhead.
8VfxiMg64h.method: AR-Retrofit introduces gated depth aggregation while preserving the pretrained forward function at initialization, with token- and depth-dependent residual strength modulation. ReSkip uses the learned routing signals to skip residual computation without an additional controller.
8VfxiMg64h.key_idea: Zero-initialized gated corrections aggregate historical depth representations, whose routing signals also guide selective layer execution.
8VfxiMg64h.evidence: Experiments span language, multimodal, and robotic tasks, including six VLM benchmarks and measured runtime evaluations.
8VfxiMg64h.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-VL-2B, AR-Retrofit adds less than 0.4% trainable parameters and trains in 12.6 minutes on one H100, while average VLM scores improve by 2.08 and 1.44 points for the 2B and 4B models.
8VfxiMg64h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value lightweight cross-depth adaptation of frozen backbones and preservation of the original function at initialization.
8VfxiMg64h.main_concern: Reviewers find that baselines and ablations do not isolate adaptive routing benefits from ordinary parameter-efficient tuning, training objectives, or simpler fixed mixtures.

6LQD9MHjku.one_liner: CaptureChart renders paired chart captures with controlled degradations and probes intermediate visual evidence needed for reasoning answers.
6LQD9MHjku.problem: Real-photo chart benchmarks are costly to expand and confound multiple capture degradations, making individual failure causes difficult to isolate.
6LQD9MHjku.method: A Blender pipeline varies surfaces, scenes, lighting, and camera imaging while preserving chart questions and answers. Additional evidence questions test whether models recover facts used in checked reasoning solutions.
6LQD9MHjku.key_idea: Aligned rendered views isolate capture factors, while parent-linked evidence probes distinguish missing visual facts from final-answer failures.
6LQD9MHjku.evidence: The benchmark renders 32,000 views from 1,000 CharXiv charts, adds 1,151 evidence questions linked to 173 reasoning questions, and evaluates 14 VLMs across 30 capture variations.
6LQD9MHjku.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value controlled paired captures, reusable rendering, and diagnostic evidence questions across a broad model evaluation.
6LQD9MHjku.main_concern: Reviewers agree that simulated degradation severity lacks validation against real photographs and human answerability.

mHPHL5MNTJ.one_liner: Procedural Graphs guide agents from local procedure subgraphs and refine graph structure using contrasting execution outcomes.
mHPHL5MNTJ.problem: Long-running agents lose procedural knowledge in accumulated histories, causing missed prerequisites, repeated mistakes, and out-of-order tool use.
mHPHL5MNTJ.method: The framework localizes an active procedure node and translates its surrounding subgraph into situational guidance. An LLM refiner contrasts successful and failed trajectories, retaining edits that preserve or improve held-out validation performance and recording rejected edits.
mHPHL5MNTJ.key_idea: Editable procedure-relation-procedure graphs provide local execution guidance and evolve through validation-filtered feedback from contrasting trajectories.
mHPHL5MNTJ.evidence: Evaluations cover multiple benchmarks and models, including ALFWorld, with graph-construction and guidance ablations and repair of flawed expert priors.
mHPHL5MNTJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value explicit procedural memory, step-level guidance, and feedback-driven refinement supported by multi-benchmark experiments.
mHPHL5MNTJ.main_concern: Reviewers question whether comparisons isolate the graph representation's contribution from additional guidance calls and feedback-driven refinement.

REQNchgjAK.one_liner: SPARK anchors symbolic behavior-tree actions to current 3D observations and uses local recovery before requesting a new plan.
REQNchgjAK.problem: Robotic manipulation systems can confuse changed object positions with a changed task and unnecessarily replan.
REQNchgjAK.method: SPARK represents tasks as symbolic behavior trees and grounds each action in current 3D observations. Runtime verification triggers local recovery and re-anchoring, with replanning only when these steps fail.
REQNchgjAK.key_idea: Separating symbolic plans from action-time spatial grounding permits re-localization and local recovery without replacing the plan.
REQNchgjAK.evidence: Evaluations include fixed-plan displacement tests, LIBERO-PRO with a 27B 4-bit planner, and 11 real-world tasks across three robot platforms.
REQNchgjAK.claimed_gains: SPARK completes 60.0% of trials after 10cm mid-episode displacements without changing the plan and reaches 74.4% mean LIBERO-PRO success across 6 settings, or 77.8% with an additional success check.
REQNchgjAK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate separating task plans from spatial grounding and the displacement experiments that directly test this distinction.
REQNchgjAK.main_concern: Reviewers question the contribution beyond integrating existing planning, grounding, verification, and recovery modules with a heavily engineered skill library.

OcrPih5Lrw.one_liner: A causal student predicts distributions over annual geospatial embeddings from partial satellite time series for in-season monitoring.
OcrPih5Lrw.problem: Annual retrospective foundation-model embeddings are poorly suited to monitoring within a growing season and costly to recompute frequently.
OcrPih5Lrw.method: The framework distills annual embeddings using partial observations with a frame encoder and causal transformer. Embedding and uncertainty heads predict an annual-embedding distribution, supported by an auxiliary seasonal-dynamics head.
OcrPih5Lrw.key_idea: Condition a distribution over annual teacher embeddings on the satellite observations available at each date.
OcrPih5Lrw.evidence: Monthly Sentinel-2 observations support embedding reconstruction and agricultural evaluations including cropland classification, field-boundary segmentation, and crop change detection.
OcrPih5Lrw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a practical need for inexpensive in-season representations and acknowledge encouraging downstream results.
OcrPih5Lrw.main_concern: The evaluation insufficiently isolates the value of annual-teacher distillation for timely in-season prediction from simpler temporal encoders or generic performance gains.

u9h01NvzTL.one_liner: FROST uses real-data gradient feedback to trigger batch-level routing and sample-level filtering of synthetic training data.
u9h01NvzTL.problem: Synthetic-data fidelity and diversity scores do not account for a learner's changing needs or distribution mismatch during training.
u9h01NvzTL.method: FROST estimates synthetic utility through gradient alignment with real training data and compares batch utility against recent history. It filters individual samples only in out-of-band batches without an external verifier or held-out validation set.
u9h01NvzTL.key_idea: Use real-training gradient alignment to score synthetic batches, then filter samples only when batch utility deviates from its recent history.
u9h01NvzTL.evidence: Experiments cover public image-classification and text-to-SQL benchmarks plus an industrial ads re-ranking system, with component ablations and overhead analysis.
u9h01NvzTL.claimed_gains: FROST filters out around 20--30% of synthetic data while improving real-task performance relative to training on the full synthetic pool.
u9h01NvzTL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value practical online selection guided by real-data gradients without external verification or separate validation data.
u9h01NvzTL.main_concern: Unmatched data-drop ratios in ablations confound selection quality with the amount of retained training data.

sQXYZ5XU6t.one_liner: Paired memory interventions reveal decision changes after consolidation despite stable aggregate retrieval and task accuracy.
sQXYZ5XU6t.problem: Retrieval metrics can conceal instance-level decision instability caused by consolidating an agent's stored experiences.
sQXYZ5XU6t.method: The study holds queries and labels fixed while comparing original and consolidated memories. Repeated runs and crossed controls separate ordinary variability, representation changes, and changes in retrieved-experience identity.
sQXYZ5XU6t.key_idea: Compare decisions under paired original and consolidated memories against same-memory repeat variability while controlling retrieved-experience identity.
sQXYZ5XU6t.evidence: The study uses controlled classification experiments, five repeats in the primary configuration, and substitutions of consumer models and retrievers.
sQXYZ5XU6t.claimed_gains: Hit@3 remains 87.06% in both conditions, but excess disagreement is 5.24 percentage points (5.40 pooled), with vulnerability recurring 3.88× and 5.48× above adjusted expectation under consumer and retriever substitution, respectively.
sQXYZ5XU6t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distinction between aggregate retrieval success and instance-level decision stability useful and value the paired, repeat-controlled evaluation.
sQXYZ5XU6t.main_concern: The narrow classification setup and lack of a query-only baseline leave actual memory dependence and generalization to long-horizon agents unclear.

suNcQvUkiN.one_liner: IRIS embeds watermark signals and trains cooperating image editors to suppress velocity predictions on protected inputs.
suNcQvUkiN.problem: Input-only anti-edit perturbations can fail under routine image transformations, while stronger perturbations harm visual quality.
suNcQvUkiN.method: A frozen watermarking model embeds image-dependent protection signals. A target-image-free objective fine-tunes editors to drive protected-input velocity toward zero while preserving clean editing through teacher matching.
suNcQvUkiN.key_idea: Use a watermark as a trigger for selectively suppressing an editor's velocity field so protected-image generation remains noisy.
suNcQvUkiN.evidence: Experiments on FLUX.2 and Qwen-Image-Edit assess protection, perceptual distortion, clean editing, and ablations.
suNcQvUkiN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the simplicity and effectiveness of the training objective and the supporting experiments.
suNcQvUkiN.main_concern: The contribution beyond existing cooperative watermark-triggered defenses appears limited to zero-velocity regression and clean-teacher distillation.

FTGL9stlLf.one_liner: Action-only distillation with empty reasoning blocks and replay KL transfers teacher policies to students that reason at inference.
FTGL9stlLf.problem: Closed teacher models hide chain-of-thought, limiting standard trajectory distillation that imitates both reasoning and actions.
FTGL9stlLf.method: Students imitate teacher actions with an empty reasoning block while replay-based KL regularization limits drift from the initial model. Optional short reasoning summaries appear after that block, and inference enables the student's own reasoning.
FTGL9stlLf.key_idea: Train action imitation with empty reasoning blocks and replay regularization, then enable student-generated reasoning during inference.
FTGL9stlLf.evidence: Experiments use Qwen students on AppWorld and SWE-bench, with open-teacher action traces and closed-teacher visible outputs and summaries.
FTGL9stlLf.claimed_gains: Qwen3.6-27B action distillation raises AppWorld success from 7% to 18% for Qwen3-4B and from 12% to 25% for Qwen3-32B; CoT-proxies raise Qwen3-4B to 35%.
FTGL9stlLf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value transferring agent capabilities without hidden teacher reasoning and recognize substantial benchmark gains.
FTGL9stlLf.main_concern: The mechanism behind cross-format transfer remains unclear because formatting comparisons also alter supervision targets and action-loss weighting.

5B8HQvpax8.one_liner: RecurSE trains rubric judges using a synchronized checker that audits their reasoning through a separately formatted scalar reward.
5B8HQvpax8.problem: Improving language-model judges usually requires costly external supervision, while self-generated rewards can exploit shared output tokens.
5B8HQvpax8.method: A judge evaluates responses against per-rule rubrics, and a synchronized policy copy audits its reasoning against meta-rubrics. Two-pass reinforcement learning separates checker scalar scores from verdict tokens to block token-copying shortcuts.
5B8HQvpax8.key_idea: Decouple checker reward outputs from judge verdict tokens while using recursive meta-rubric audits as reinforcement-learning feedback.
5B8HQvpax8.evidence: Reviews describe multiple models and benchmarks, surface-coupling experiments, CheckEval and ProfBench results, and stopping-monitor analyses.
5B8HQvpax8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers identify surface-coupled reward inflation as a useful finding and view interface decoupling as a simple corrective mechanism.
5B8HQvpax8.main_concern: Missing matched-budget comparisons with closely related meta-judging methods leave the contribution of the recursive training design uncertain.

3Qvz1GP0RC.one_liner: DyaFDB evaluates both participants in full-duplex model conversations to measure partner-dependent turn-taking and task behavior.
3Qvz1GP0RC.problem: Single-sided dialogue evaluations miss behaviors jointly produced by two responsive speakers.
3Qvz1GP0RC.method: Two models converse under assigned cooperative or conflicting roles, and an external judge scores both offline. Self-play and cross-play vary partners, roles, and speaking order to study coupled behavior.
3Qvz1GP0RC.key_idea: Treat both responsive speakers as evaluated participants and vary their pairings to measure model, partner, and interaction effects.
3Qvz1GP0RC.evidence: The benchmark instantiates four tasks in 140 scenarios and records 7,560 conversations across six self- and cross-play pairings.
3Qvz1GP0RC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating both speakers and the evidence that conversational behavior depends on the interaction partner.
3Qvz1GP0RC.main_concern: No human-interaction study establishes whether the behavioral metrics predict coherent, natural, and effective human-model conversation.

TwswjxtT6c.one_liner: Faster-GCG combines distance regularization, temperature-controlled candidate sampling, and duplicate-suffix marking to reduce discrete adversarial prompt evaluations.
TwswjxtT6c.problem: Greedy Coordinate Gradient attacks waste evaluations through inaccurate candidate rankings, uniform sampling, and revisiting suffixes.
TwswjxtT6c.method: Faster-GCG adds embedding-distance regularization to gradient-based ranking, controls sampling temperature, and marks visited suffixes. Faster-GCG++ separately uses a longer suffix configuration.
TwswjxtT6c.key_idea: Regularize gradient-ranked token candidates by embedding distance, bias their sampling, and skip previously evaluated suffixes.
TwswjxtT6c.evidence: Experiments cover multiple open-source language models, JBB-Behaviors and AdvBench, white-box baselines, ranking diagnostics, and component ablations.
TwswjxtT6c.claimed_gains: Faster-GCG reduces evaluations from approximately 256K to 32K for up to 8x sampling efficiency, while the separate 40-token Faster-GCG++ setting reports 78.1% average jailbreak success.
TwswjxtT6c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the systematic diagnosis of GCG inefficiencies and simple modifications supported by experiments.
TwswjxtT6c.main_concern: The method offers limited methodological advances through familiar optimization heuristics, with incomplete justification for the distance penalty.

cXJp4uqpnp.one_liner: TriHAR adaptively selects encoder depths and separately routes modality and EHR-centered interaction predictions for clinical prediction.
cXJp4uqpnp.problem: Fixed encoder outputs and uniform fusion overlook patient-specific representation depths and differing modality and interaction contributions.
cXJp4uqpnp.method: TriHAR integrates EHR, ECG, and chest X-ray data through hierarchical routing. It selects representation depth within each modality, then independently routes modality predictions and EHR-centered cross-modal interaction predictions.
cXJp4uqpnp.key_idea: Select modality-specific encoder depth before independently routing direct modality experts and EHR-centered interaction experts.
cXJp4uqpnp.evidence: ICU length-of-stay experiments cover 27 encoder combinations, trimodal and bimodal baselines, and settings with ECG or CXR unavailable.
cXJp4uqpnp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the multimodal architecture sensible and value evaluation across many encoder combinations.
cXJp4uqpnp.main_concern: Missing fixed-layer and related ablations prevent isolating whether adaptive encoder-depth selection causes the reported gains.

vgJbgsHx68.one_liner: Anchor uses gradient-free historical rules to audit whether irregular time-series benchmarks require specialized neural forecasting models.
vgJbgsHx68.problem: Irregular time-series benchmarks may reward simple historical structure while overstating the need for complex neural representations.
vgJbgsHx68.method: The Anchor family implements persistence, smoothing, sparse repetition, and recurrence controls with non-test empirical rule selection. AutoAnchor and diagnostic perturbations test how these structures explain benchmark performance under matched protocols.
vgJbgsHx68.key_idea: Apply transparent historical forecasting rules directly to asynchronous observations and select them using non-test data.
vgJbgsHx68.evidence: Global irregular multivariate forecasting benchmarks include lookback-horizon sweeps, paired entity tests, perturbation, thinning, bootstrap analyses, and ablations.
vgJbgsHx68.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value questioning neural-model necessity and providing transparent controls for irregular time-series benchmarking.
vgJbgsHx68.main_concern: Missing recent neural baselines and unexplained reversals between reported settings weaken the breadth of the benchmark conclusions.

yTa4gvQUGG.one_liner: KernelAudit checks generated GPU kernels with expert-reference reliability audits and sealed, exclusive-GPU timing.
yTa4gvQUGG.problem: Fixed-tolerance functional checks can accept kernels that exploit measurements or violate requirements, overstating practical speedups.
yTa4gvQUGG.method: KernelAudit assembles expert-written kernels as reliability and speed references and audits generated implementations through five verifier levels. A sealed evaluation environment hides evaluation assets and times expert and generated kernels under one protocol.
yTa4gvQUGG.key_idea: Use expert implementations as paired performance and reliability references while escalating checks through five defect-detection levels.
yTa4gvQUGG.evidence: The benchmark contains 230 tasks across 14 domains from 69 repositories, analyzes 505 functionally passing kernels, and evaluates seven frontier models.
yTa4gvQUGG.claimed_gains: Only 25.3% of generated kernels pass all five audit levels, and no evaluated model exceeds 40.9%.
yTa4gvQUGG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical reliability focus, expert-reference comparisons, and controlled evaluation design.
yTa4gvQUGG.main_concern: Reliability rates mix explicit task obligations with additional expert-interface requirements that may not have been communicated to generation agents.

yEA7jD3qij.one_liner: Centered, truncated-SVD weight updates edit factual associations without storing or precomputing representations of existing knowledge.
yEA7jD3qij.problem: Closed-form factual editing commonly depends on costly corpus-derived proxy representations of pretrained knowledge.
yEA7jD3qij.method: The method formulates edits using only new knowledge and directly updates existing weights. Within-representation centering and truncated singular value decomposition limit ill-conditioning and amplification of updates.
yEA7jD3qij.key_idea: Solve new-knowledge edits with centered representations and a truncated pseudoinverse, omitting stored pretrained-knowledge constraints.
yEA7jD3qij.evidence: Experiments compare editing efficacy and runtime with existing methods and include large-scale editing of 2,000 facts on GPT-J.
yEA7jD3qij.claimed_gains: The abstract reports up to 30× lower amortized editing runtime, from 188 to 6 minutes, zero pretrained-representation storage, and only 0.56% degradation on GPT-J with 2,000 edits.
yEA7jD3qij.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the concrete removal of precomputation and storage dependencies with competitive empirical editing performance.
yEA7jD3qij.main_concern: The paper does not establish why centering and truncated SVD preserve existing knowledge after its explicit constraint is removed.

aYSjWIVjHx.one_liner: Trains a conditional flow matching model on large banks of SVD-canonicalized LoRA adapters to generate task-specific adapters directly from few-shot examples.
aYSjWIVjHx.problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA still requires running a separate gradient-based optimization process for every new downstream task.
aYSjWIVjHx.method: STAGE constructs banks of up to 100,000 independently optimized LoRA adapters paired with small labeled support sets, canonicalizing each adapter via SVD of its effective weight update to remove factor ambiguity. A conditional Flow Matching model then generates task-specific LoRA adapters directly from few-shot support examples without deployment-time gradient updates.
aYSjWIVjHx.key_idea: Canonicalizes pre-fitted LoRA weight updates via SVD and trains a support-set-conditioned flow matching generator over large adapter banks for gradient-free few-shot adaptation.
aYSjWIVjHx.evidence: Evaluated across adapter bank sizes of 1K, 10K, and 100K on six vision dataset-backbone pairs (including CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet) and 14 text generation datasets (including e-SNLI and WikiSQL).
aYSjWIVjHx.claimed_gains: Improves official-split accuracy over the frozen classifier by up to approximately 13.4 and 9.9 percentage points on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet, and achieves gains of 31.7 and 21.9 percentage points on e-SNLI and WikiSQL.
aYSjWIVjHx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the large-scale engineering effort of building 100K-adapter banks and studying how few-shot conditional parameter generation scales with supervision size.
aYSjWIVjHx.main_concern: Reviewers highlight discrepancies and incomplete evaluations between the main text and appendix tables, missing comparisons to HyperTuning and FLoWN, and appendix measurements showing that generating and selecting candidate adapters costs more time and FLOPs than direct LoRA fitting.

GtzE6wTswY.one_liner: Runs extra parallel refinement passes on uncertain draft tokens during speculative decoding and appends the reconsidered guesses to the draft tree.
GtzE6wTswY.problem: Feature-level speculative decoding drafters allocate a single forward pass to every token, causing frequent target rejections on tokens where the drafter is uncertain.
GtzE6wTswY.method: Parallel Reconsideration uses a learned uncertainty gate and bidding strategy to identify hesitant draft tokens and runs extra refinement forward passes on them in parallel with standard one-pass drafting. A co-designed mixed-cache training recipe and serving algorithm append these refined candidates to the draft tree without adding sequential drafting steps.
GtzE6wTswY.key_idea: Executes additional refinement forward passes on uncertain draft nodes in parallel with standard drafting and appends the revised tokens as branches in the verification tree.
GtzE6wTswY.evidence: Evaluated across multiple LLM families (including Qwen3-8B and Llama) and generation benchmarks (including LiveCodeBench) against speculative decoding baselines such as EAGLE-3.1.
GtzE6wTswY.claimed_gains: Improves acceptance length by 5.3% to 10.2% and end-to-end speedup by 3.5% to 9.2% on average across models and benchmarks.
GtzE6wTswY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that spending extra parallel compute to refine uncertain draft features without lengthening the sequential critical path is a practical way to increase speculative acceptance length.
GtzE6wTswY.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the learned routing gate and bidding mechanism are not ablated against simple lowest-confidence threshold rules, and note latency regressions at larger batch sizes (e.g., batch sizes 8 and 16).

QwAZ48DJhW.one_liner: Co-evolves multi-agent workflow generators and executors using trace-derived hierarchical rewards on adaptively hardened multi-agent datasets.
QwAZ48DJhW.problem: Existing multi-agent workflow optimization methods train only the workflow generator while keeping executor agents fixed, and rely on sparse outcome rewards on tasks that single agents can already solve.
QwAZ48DJhW.method: FloWright uses a hierarchical, structure-aware reward paradigm that combines final-answer correctness with role-specific validity checks and execution-trace failure penalties to co-evolve multiple workflow roles via reinforcement learning. It is paired with DataWright, which converts existing benchmarks into harder workflow-level tasks (Shared, Paired, and Decoy).
QwAZ48DJhW.key_idea: Assigns role-localized rewards from workflow execution traces to jointly train workflow generator and executor agents on synthetically hardened multi-part tasks.
QwAZ48DJhW.evidence: Evaluated with small open models across document, slide, chart, code, math, and finance tasks (including MMLongBench-Doc and DocFinQA).
QwAZ48DJhW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending training beyond the workflow planner to executor roles and diagnosing that many workflow benchmarks are solvable by a single agent are well-motivated contributions.
QwAZ48DJhW.main_concern: Reviewers question the credit-assignment claim because execution traces cannot distinguish semantically wrong intermediate outputs without counterfactual runs, and note that DataWright tasks concatenate independent questions without proving that learned coordination is required.

ogu2wTp6nS.one_liner: Evolves multiple populations of natural-language skills from verifier feedback and jointly selects a complementary skill set for frozen LLMs.
ogu2wTp6nS.problem: Frozen language models cannot retain post-deployment task experience in their weights, while evolving a single prompt or natural-language skill trajectory suffers from high variance and overfitting.
ogu2wTp6nS.method: DIVE enables a frozen LLM to self-improve by generating, executing, and revising reusable natural-language skills encoding reasoning procedures, verification strategies, and failure modes using verifier feedback. To avoid local optima, it evolves multiple independent skill populations from bootstrapped experience and jointly selects a complementary ensemble of skills for inference.
ogu2wTp6nS.key_idea: Independently evolves multiple populations of natural-language reasoning skills via self-reflection on verifier feedback and jointly selects a complementary skill subset for test-time aggregation.
ogu2wTp6nS.evidence: Evaluated across six mathematical and logical reasoning benchmarks (including HMMT February 2025) and multiple LLM families (including GPT-5-nano, DeepSeek-v4-flash, and Qwen3.5-27B) against SFT, GRPO, and GEPA.
ogu2wTp6nS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evolving readable, transferable natural-language skills without weight updates or a stronger teacher model yields consistent accuracy gains across reasoning benchmarks.
ogu2wTp6nS.main_concern: Reviewers note that the gain over Multi-GEPA confounds the evolution process with joint complementary ensemble selection at inference, point out discrepancies in reported rollout counts (~40,000 vs. 7,000), and question whether displayed HMMT skills leaked from test problems.

RADqaaSfPw.one_liner: Proves that canonical polyadic tensor gradient flow from vanishing initialization converges to a staircase of greedy bipartite matching events.
RADqaaSfPw.problem: The non-linear learning dynamics and loss trajectories of higher-order canonical polyadic tensor factorization under gradient flow from vanishing initialization lack an exact analytical characterization.
RADqaaSfPw.method: For tensors of order nu >= 3 that are diagonal in mode-wise orthonormal bases, the authors prove that gradient flow from vanishing initialization reduces to a greedy bipartite matching process between model rank-one atoms and target scalar sectors ordered by initialization-dependent activation clocks. Applying Fourier diagonalization, they derive an explicit distribution-free asymptotic loss curve for learning modular addition with complex weights.
RADqaaSfPw.key_idea: Reduces small-initialization CP tensor gradient flow to a greedy bipartite matching sequence governed by pairwise atom-sector activation clocks.
RADqaaSfPw.evidence: Supported by asymptotic convergence theorems for order nu >= 3 diagonal tensors and numerical gradient-flow simulations on modular addition at p = 128.
RADqaaSfPw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the mathematical connection reducing asymmetric CP tensor gradient flow to greedy bipartite matching and its exact application to modular addition loss curves.
RADqaaSfPw.main_concern: Reviewers point out a technical gap in Lemma 7's product-error estimates for quadratic off-sector residuals, note that the diagonal target assumption is highly restrictive, and criticize the jargon-heavy exposition.

RfuxGCsgJY.one_liner: Estimates sample-level adversarial distance and membership inference vulnerability directly from cumulative loss and input-gradient trajectories during training.
RfuxGCsgJY.problem: Measuring sample-level adversarial distance and membership inference risk at scale is computationally expensive because standard methods require iterative attacks, shadow models, or repeated retraining.
RfuxGCsgJY.method: The authors track Cumulative Sample Loss (CSL) and Cumulative Sample Gradient (CSG) during standard training with negligible overhead, deriving two-sided theoretical bounds linking these trajectory statistics to adversarial distance and privacy leakage. They introduce an adversarial-distance proxy for mislabeled/duplicate detection and CSL-Diff for auditing membership vulnerability without auxiliary shadow models.
