Gi3Wmp8rYG.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the theoretical model omits task-prompt information in the generator, relies on worst-case capacity rather than realized query information, and is not directly tested against empirical query counts or iterative tree-search dynamics.

bgJW02fenF.one_liner: Co-evolving target and failure agents generate increasingly plausible hard negatives for preference training.
bgJW02fenF.problem: An agent's obvious failed trajectories provide weak preference negatives and do not teach it to reject plausible attempts with subtle errors.
bgJW02fenF.method: A failure agent learns from both agents' failed trajectories to generate higher-reward failures for target-agent preference training. The improving target supplies new failures to the failure agent, which in turn supplies updated hard negatives during co-evolution.
bgJW02fenF.key_idea: Train a failure policy to prefer higher-reward unsuccessful trajectories and update it alongside the target so negative difficulty co-evolves.
bgJW02fenF.evidence: Experiments on online shopping, scientific reasoning, and interactive SQL querying cover different interactive tasks and model families, with comparisons against frozen failure generation.
bgJW02fenF.claimed_gains: The framework improves average task reward by 5.7 over the baseline.
bgJW02fenF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adaptive hard-negative generation addresses preference-data saturation and that gains span tasks and model families.
bgJW02fenF.main_concern: Comparisons do not match generating policies, rollout diversity, or training cost, and reliance on intermediate rewards limits sparse-feedback settings.

UG830hrcwF.one_liner: Policy document structure and output fields alter LLM-agent authorization decisions despite unchanged requirements.
UG830hrcwF.problem: LLM agents must infer unstated requirement-combination rules, and presentation changes may alter authorization decisions even when policy content stays fixed.
UG830hrcwF.method: The study compares six decision-preserving presentations spanning layout, wording, length, document count, and output format. Matched experiments separate false approvals from false denials and test how suggested combination rules and supporting output fields drive errors.
UG830hrcwF.key_idea: Hold policy requirements and correct decisions fixed while varying document and output presentation to reveal inferred rule-combination behavior.
UG830hrcwF.evidence: Experiments cover 12 open-weight and three Claude model configurations, exhaustive reference answers, an independent Z3 encoding, and four rerun configurations isolating output-effect components.
UG830hrcwF.claimed_gains: Layout, wording, and length change wrongful allowances by at most 5.4 percentage points, whereas splitting policy documents or requesting five output fields raises them by 22 to 32 points, with one sentence carrying 46% of the output effect.
UG830hrcwF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that fixed-content matched comparisons and exhaustive reference checks provide a useful test of authorization consistency.
UG830hrcwF.main_concern: Only 24 synthetic held-out cases support the main experiment, and ambiguous output fields or policy interpretation confound attribution to rule combination.

NeCATATRUB.one_liner: Higher-Order Langevin Dynamics low-pass filters learned diffusion scores to delay memorization.
NeCATATRUB.problem: Diffusion models can reproduce training samples, creating copyright and privacy risks that depend on their generative dynamics.
NeCATATRUB.method: The study introduces auxiliary velocity and acceleration variables through HOLD and derives the resulting time-domain regularization using Laplace and spectral analysis. It shows that the data variable follows a low-pass-filtered learned score and analyzes the optimal empirical score at low noise.
NeCATATRUB.key_idea: Add higher-order dynamical variables so the data trajectory integrates a low-pass-filtered score, with smoothing increasing by model order.
NeCATATRUB.evidence: Theoretical Laplace-transform and spectral analyses are paired with memorization and generation-quality experiments, including Fmem-versus-FID trade-off curves across HOLD orders.
NeCATATRUB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that temporal smoothing provides an interesting account of HOLD and that reduced memorization is a useful property.
NeCATATRUB.main_concern: Higher orders can worsen generation quality without consistently improving the memorization-quality trade-off, and gaps remain between the theory and claimed mechanism.

gmWplWC8G9.one_liner: EdgeDRM routes queries between neighboring federated clients using learned density-based referral potentials.
gmWplWC8G9.problem: Decentralized federated clients develop complementary expertise, but queries are normally evaluated only at their arrival client without global coordination.
gmWplWC8G9.method: EdgeDRM learns one density-based routing potential per client and selects successive referrals from differences between neighboring potentials under a movement budget. Local models along the route generate the aggregated prediction using only neighbor-local training and inference information.
gmWplWC8G9.key_idea: Use neighbor-potential differences for graph-constrained sequential referral and aggregate predictions only from visited clients.
gmWplWC8G9.evidence: Experiments on benchmark and real-world medical data compare graph-matched decentralized baselines across connectivity settings, supported by estimation and referral-gain analysis.
gmWplWC8G9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that budgeted local expert referral is a clear decentralized inference formulation and that per-client potentials respect topology constraints.
gmWplWC8G9.main_concern: Every test query starts at a non-source client, while source-density routing is assumed to identify better predictive experts rather than tested independently.

HRGNcrZi6q.one_liner: Gradient-before-denoising updates treat diffusion denoisers as approximate projections for constrained optimization.
HRGNcrZi6q.problem: External-objective gradient guidance can push diffusion samples away from learned manifolds or feasible-set geometry.
HRGNcrZi6q.method: The update applies an objective gradient inside the denoising step and interprets the Stein denoiser as an approximate projection onto learned geometry. It requires one gradient evaluation and one denoiser call per step without differentiating through the denoiser.
HRGNcrZi6q.key_idea: Interpret Stein denoising after each objective-gradient step as inexact projection back toward the learned feasible geometry.
HRGNcrZi6q.evidence: Theory proves descent and finite-time convergence for linear manifolds, compact convex sets, and compact Riemannian submanifolds, with numerical experiments testing descent and geometry preservation.
HRGNcrZi6q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the one-gradient, one-denoiser update is simple and that the approximate-projection analysis covers several useful geometric settings.
HRGNcrZi6q.main_concern: The update closely resembles plug-and-play proximal-gradient methods, while a disputed manifold lemma and near-manifold assumptions weaken the theory.

3GHBNdICTh.one_liner: Modulates heterogeneous complex spectral recurrence modes using two shared input-dependent scalars for retention and phase control.
3GHBNdICTh.problem: Static spectral recurrences cannot adapt transitions to inputs, while per-mode input-dependent complex transitions incur heavy projection and bandwidth overhead.
3GHBNdICTh.method: SPARC controls a diagonal complex affine recurrence via two input-dependent scalars governing retention and phase, with a retention-coupled clock damping phase drift in persistent modes. The diagonal form supports associative parallel scans for BPTT and linear-memory online RTRL.
3GHBNdICTh.key_idea: Controls high-dimensional heterogeneous complex recurrence modes using only two shared input-dependent scalars and a retention-coupled phase clock.
3GHBNdICTh.evidence: Evaluates on partially observable continuous control, POPGym memory tasks, sequence classification, language modeling, and custom Triton kernel speedups.
3GHBNdICTh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean decoupling of 2-scalar control from state dimension, the phase-damping clock, and the bandwidth-saving Triton kernel.
3GHBNdICTh.main_concern: The key unshared per-mode control baseline was never run, RL baselines use 4-step truncated BPTT, and accuracy is only tested at small width D=64.

oxILJbHE2a.one_liner: Feeds frozen DINO features to a flexible video tokenizer and supervises every token prefix to reconstruct those semantic features.
oxILJbHE2a.problem: Existing flexible-length video tokenizers apply representation alignment only on early decoder states, which the decoder can partially satisfy from noised inputs.
oxILJbHE2a.method: SemanTok feeds frozen DINO features into its encoder and attaches lightweight prediction heads that reconstruct DINO features directly from each retained token prefix alone. This forces early tokens to encode global clip semantics while deferring pixel details to later tokens.
oxILJbHE2a.key_idea: Supervises every retained discrete token prefix directly to reconstruct frozen DINO features instead of aligning noisy decoder hidden states.
oxILJbHE2a.evidence: Evaluates video reconstruction and autoregressive generation across multiple model sizes, noise levels, and datasets including uCO3D and K600.
oxILJbHE2a.claimed_gains: A 201M SemanTok autoregressive model matches or beats a VideoFlexTok AR model 3.4x its size.
oxILJbHE2a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the prefix-level semantic supervision intuitive and appreciate the controlled AR scaling and noise-level probe analyses.
oxILJbHE2a.main_concern: Baseline VideoFlexTok models were retrained for much shorter schedules, component ablations lack quantitative separation, and pixel reconstruction fidelity degrades substantially.

F6hAWEaNYH.one_liner: Uses an LLM actor-critic and three-layer memory to evolve surrogate backward-gradient policies for mixed-integer decision-focused learning.
F6hAWEaNYH.problem: Mixed-integer decision-focused learning relies on fixed, hand-tuned surrogate backward gradients that fail to adapt across problem structures and scales.
F6hAWEaNYH.method: EvoMIDFL pairs a Gradient Actor that proposes surrogate gradient estimators and compositions with a Critic Agent that filters unsafe candidates on validation performance. A Memory Agent stores formulation, mechanism, and skill experiences to guide evolution and target-task refinement.
F6hAWEaNYH.key_idea: Evolves and composes surrogate backward-gradient policies for mixed-integer optimization using an LLM actor-critic loop with three-layer memory.
F6hAWEaNYH.evidence: Evaluates across multiple mixed-integer decision-focused learning problem scales, prediction models, and memory-transfer ablations.
F6hAWEaNYH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the adaptive surrogate-gradient framework well structured and relevant to mixed-integer decision-focused learning.
F6hAWEaNYH.main_concern: The necessity of LLM-driven search over standard non-LLM hyperparameter optimization is unestablished, gains are small without significance tests, and search costs are unreported.

ifJLYMDmUG.one_liner: Parses multi-stage aerial instructions into landmark transitions and proactively adjusts UAV view orientation and lookahead flight paths.
ifJLYMDmUG.problem: Zero-shot aerial vision-and-language navigation methods treat each landmark stage independently, ignoring camera orientation and cross-stage occlusion along UAV paths.
ifJLYMDmUG.method: AheadFly parses instructions into landmark queries and inter-stage transitions, then performs pre-grounding view reorientation so upcoming landmarks enter the field of view and lookahead path adjustment using guiding forces to avoid occlusion and obstacles. The authors also build LandmarkFly for multi-stage evaluation.
ifJLYMDmUG.key_idea: Pre-orients the UAV camera and shapes its flight path toward upcoming inter-stage transitions before grounding each landmark.
ifJLYMDmUG.evidence: Evaluates on OpenFly-AirSim and the newly introduced LandmarkFly benchmark with component-matched modular baselines and ablations.
ifJLYMDmUG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find proactive view and path adjustment intuitive and appreciate component-matched modular baselines.
ifJLYMDmUG.main_concern: The Fly0 baseline reproduces far below its published score on OpenFly, largest gains occur on the authors' auto-generated LandmarkFly benchmark, and stage metrics lack clear definitions.

rpMtZ567Cm.one_liner: Localizes sexually explicit concept channels in diffusion FFN layers and erases them via closed-form weight projection.
rpMtZ567Cm.problem: Existing diffusion concept-erasure defenses and benchmarks target only text-to-image pipelines, leaving image-conditioned and video generation attack surfaces exposed.
rpMtZ567Cm.method: UniErase treats diffusion FFN layers as key-value memories, localizes channels encoding sexually explicit concepts, and removes them via closed-form orthogonal weight projection without retraining. The paper also introduces UniErase-Bench spanning image and video tasks under text and image conditioning.
rpMtZ567Cm.key_idea: Localizes sexually explicit concept channels inside diffusion FFN layers and projects them out in closed form across image and video architectures.
rpMtZ567Cm.evidence: Evaluates on UniErase-Bench across four task categories and text-to-image benchmarks using erasure rate, CLIP score, and FID.
rpMtZ567Cm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the multi-task threat framing across U-Net and transformer diffusion models and the strong erasure-preservation trade-off.
rpMtZ567Cm.main_concern: Technical components combine prior FFN localization and closed-form projection methods, main comparisons use outdated SD-v1.4, and benchmark coverage omits adaptive/joint attacks.

whkdFg9YD5.one_liner: Refines semantic prompts via a 3-agent LLM loop and dynamically routes them into adaptive Transformer layers for few-shot recognition.
whkdFg9YD5.problem: LLM-generated captions for few-shot image recognition are often verbose and redundant, and static prompt injection ignores image-specific visual abstraction levels.
whkdFg9YD5.method: MAD-SP uses Multi-Agent Caption Refinement (generator, critic, refiner) scored by CLIP, Dynamic Prompt Injection (DPI) to select an image-specific Transformer block, and Contrastive Modality Alignment (CMA) via a bottleneck adapter with InfoNCE loss.
whkdFg9YD5.key_idea: Refine class captions offline with a three-agent LLM loop and train a lightweight gating network to inject aligned prompt embeddings into an image-adaptive Transformer layer.
whkdFg9YD5.evidence: Evaluations across 16 few-shot benchmark settings on a Visformer-T backbone and component ablations support the framework.
whkdFg9YD5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing both prompt quality and adaptive layer injection is coherent and shows strong results on the tested benchmarks.
whkdFg9YD5.main_concern: Reviewers note high pipeline complexity, evaluation restricted to a single small Visformer-T (10M) backbone, unanalyzed LLM costs, and no evidence explaining which layers are selected.

TsUqcSpYLb.one_liner: Combines a contextual Transformer cCRE encoder with a neural topic model to link scATAC-seq representations to interpretable regulatory programs.
TsUqcSpYLb.problem: scATAC-seq foundation models lack interpretability, while standard topic models ignore contextual relationships across candidate cis-regulatory elements (cCREs).
TsUqcSpYLb.method: CARMA treats cells as documents, cCREs as words, and regulatory programs as topics; a contextual encoder computes soft cCRE-to-topic assignments while a generative decoder reconstructs cell profiles using shared topic prototypes and cCRE embeddings.
TsUqcSpYLb.key_idea: Tie topic prototypes and cCRE identity embeddings across a contextual Transformer encoder and a generative topic-model decoder for joint cell, topic, and cCRE learning.
TsUqcSpYLb.evidence: Evaluations on seven scATAC-seq datasets, linear-probe annotations on CATlas, SCREEN, and ChromHMM, masked-target tests, and ablations support the model.
TsUqcSpYLb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that CARMA provides a thorough empirical evaluation and coherently links contextual scATAC-seq representations to explicit topic axes.
TsUqcSpYLb.main_concern: Reviewers consider the weight-tying architecture an incremental combination of existing topic and Transformer components and note that context-dependent cCRE assignments lack direct biological validation.

UhsN7VL96W.one_liner: Analyzes stagewise gradient flow of attention experts to explain how in-context learning adapts between sample mean and mid-range estimators.
UhsN7VL96W.problem: How gradient-based pretraining teaches Prior Fitted Networks to adaptively select statistical estimators from context without observing distribution labels is poorly understood.
UhsN7VL96W.method: Observing that scalar softmax attention computes the derivative of the empirical cumulant-generating function, the authors combine attention experts via softmax MoE or GLU gating and analyze stagewise gradient flow on Gaussian versus uniform location estimation.
UhsN7VL96W.key_idea: Use scalar softmax attention both to extract distributional features and to interpolate between sample mean and mid-range estimators under softmax or GLU gating.
UhsN7VL96W.evidence: Theoretical stagewise gradient-flow analysis and synthetic experiments comparing softmax and GLU gating support the findings.
UhsN7VL96W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theoretical insight that scalar softmax attention serves as both estimator and distribution identifier under gradient flow elegant and well checked.
UhsN7VL96W.main_concern: Reviewers note that the architecture is highly specialized with pre-assigned fixed components and restricted to two 1D families, limiting insight into general Transformers.

kJdfDsOXOE.one_liner: Composes radial, spherical-harmonic, and free-form ray rotations on the sphere for camera-agnostic monocular 3D reconstruction.
kJdfDsOXOE.problem: Existing camera-aware monocular 3D models use a single fixed basis to represent both coarse projection geometry and fine local variations.
kJdfDsOXOE.method: OmniRay predicts per-pixel ray directions and up-to-scale radial distances in one feed-forward pass using a hierarchical ray module. It composes a monotone radial base, a spherical-harmonic residual, and a free-form local residual as successive rotations on the sphere without requiring camera parameters at inference.
kJdfDsOXOE.key_idea: Composing monotone radial, spherical-harmonic, and free-form residual components as successive spherical rotations models camera ray fields hierarchically.
kJdfDsOXOE.evidence: Experiments evaluate on seen and held-out camera configurations including catadioptric cameras, PanoCity, ScanNet++ DSLR, panorama benchmarks, and real pinhole images.
kJdfDsOXOE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the hierarchical layered ray representation provides a reasonable geometric inductive bias and improves generalization across diverse camera models.
kJdfDsOXOE.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the gains stem from the hierarchical ray representation itself or from random-lens augmentation and in-distribution vs. out-of-distribution baseline comparisons.

Qcwe9s1q8T.one_liner: Augments strictly proper scoring rules with normalized Bayes value from an action-utility table for medical active learning.
Qcwe9s1q8T.problem: Standard active learning prioritizes predictive probability accuracy rather than the downstream clinical decision costs associated with different prediction errors.
Qcwe9s1q8T.method: Domain-Utility-Sensitive Active Learning (DUSAL) adds normalized Bayes value from a complete action-utility table to a strictly proper base potential, with hard and smooth variants. Under Bayesian updating, its acquisition value decomposes into BEMPS predictive learning and clinical expected value of sample information (EVSI).
Qcwe9s1q8T.key_idea: Adding normalized Bayes value from an action-utility table to a strictly proper potential decomposes acquisition into predictive divergence and decision regret.
Qcwe9s1q8T.evidence: Theoretical convergence and invariance proofs are paired with exact finite-model experiments and evaluations across five public medical tasks.
Qcwe9s1q8T.claimed_gains: DUSAL-Div achieves Holm-controlled reductions in realized-cost AULC on three of four tasks, while additional cost gains from utility augmentation remain unconfirmed under Holm correction.
Qcwe9s1q8T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that incorporating explicit action-utility tables into strictly proper scores for medical active learning is a well-motivated and principled formulation.
Qcwe9s1q8T.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments do not show utility augmentation outperforming matched BEMPS under Holm correction, and dense notation obscures the connection between theory and ensemble retraining.

4sCx8lKSAp.one_liner: Trains an LLM via meta-RL to output textual instructions selecting which Transformer layers to update for continual context consolidation.
4sCx8lKSAp.problem: Streaming long-context workflows require consolidating new information into LLM weights without overwriting previously acquired knowledge.
4sCx8lKSAp.method: SCoL generates textual layer-selection instructions given incoming context and updates only those layers, optimizing the selector with meta-reinforcement learning over the evolving model state using QA or likelihood rewards.
4sCx8lKSAp.key_idea: Uses meta-RL over an evolving model state to train an LLM to emit natural-language layer-routing instructions for sparse continual weight updates.
4sCx8lKSAp.evidence: Evaluated on SQuAD continual knowledge incorporation and LongBench v2 long-context consolidation using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
4sCx8lKSAp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the self-regulated layer-selection mechanism intuitive and note spontaneous alignment with high-Fisher-information layers.
4sCx8lKSAp.main_concern: Reviewers show that a hardcoded Last-10 layer baseline nearly matches SCoL's retention (20.10% vs. 20.46%) despite SCoL's O(T^2) meta-RL cost, and note single-model evaluation.

XbRhpxrxLY.one_liner: Extracts proprietary RAG corpora via response-grounded queries, continuation cues from unused context, and maximin selection.
XbRhpxrxLY.problem: Implicit black-box RAG extraction attacks suffer from semantic drift and localized exploration, limiting systematic corpus coverage.
XbRhpxrxLY.method: GE^3 generates candidate benign queries grounded in prior RAG responses and exploits Echo Knowledge Overflow (EKO) by extracting continuation cues from retrieved context not used in the primary answer. It selects diverse queries from the candidate pool using history-relative maximin distance optimization.
XbRhpxrxLY.key_idea: Combines response-grounded and continuation-cue candidate generation with history-relative maximin distance selection to probe black-box RAG corpora.
XbRhpxrxLY.evidence: Experiments across four datasets, twelve victim LLMs (including commercial models), ablations, and pipeline defenses evaluate corpus extraction.
XbRhpxrxLY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the intuitive black-box framework and solid experiments spanning multiple datasets, victim LLMs, ablations, and defenses.
XbRhpxrxLY.main_concern: Reviewers question whether EKO actually leaks unused retrieved context or improves coverage over answer-only baselines, and note overlap with prior RAG extraction work.

9PACqAXYXu.one_liner: Performs task-free unsupervised continual learning using growing self-organizing maps with per-unit covariance replay.
9PACqAXYXu.problem: Continual learning often relies on storing raw exemplars, task boundaries, or class labels, which limits unsupervised exemplar-free deployment.
9PACqAXYXu.method: The framework augments growing self-organizing maps (GSOMs) with per-unit mean, variance, and covariance statistics and encoder-decoder models. During training without task IDs or labels, units grow dynamically and generate synthetic samples via ancestral sampling for replay.
9PACqAXYXu.key_idea: Stores local distributional statistics in growing self-organizing map units and decodes ancestral samples from those statistics for exemplar-free replay.
9PACqAXYXu.evidence: Evaluations across multiple class-incremental benchmarks, including single-class incremental TinyImageNet and MiniImageNet, plus component ablations.
9PACqAXYXu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unsupervised task-free integration of adaptive GSOM topology with local statistical replay coherent and clearly written.
9PACqAXYXu.main_concern: Reviewers point out that post-training classification assigns majority labels to units using historical labeled training data, undermining the claimed label-free continual setting, and question novelty over prior SOM/GSOM work.

Qb5BUD8nAq.one_liner: Replaces scalar LLM-judge rewards in GRPO with conformally calibrated reward intervals and pairwise interval comparisons.
Qb5BUD8nAq.problem: Scalar pseudo-rewards from LLM-as-a-Judge ignore reward uncertainty, introducing misleading policy-gradient signals in semi-supervised post-training.
Qb5BUD8nAq.method: Range-GRPO constructs conformally calibrated reward intervals from judgment features and computes group-relative advantages by comparing reward intervals pairwise rather than collapsing them to points. This allows interval uncertainty to alter both advantage magnitude and sign, reducing to Dr.GRPO when intervals collapse to zero width.
Qb5BUD8nAq.key_idea: Computes group-relative policy advantages via pairwise comparisons of conformally calibrated reward intervals so uncertainty can flip advantage signs.
Qb5BUD8nAq.evidence: Supported by theoretical reduction to Dr.GRPO and experiments on a synthetic task plus mathematical and multiple-choice reasoning benchmarks.
Qb5BUD8nAq.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest in-distribution and out-of-distribution average performance among evaluated semi-supervised methods using a smaller total response budget.
Qb5BUD8nAq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree pairwise interval comparison is simple, well-motivated, and uniquely enables uncertainty to reverse advantage signs unlike scalar rescaling.
Qb5BUD8nAq.main_concern: Reviewers note real-task experiments confound the pairwise advantage rule with different judges, scorers, and calibration pipelines, and lack empirical/theoretical on-policy coverage validation.

LJmbUpmei7.one_liner: Applies multi-objective gradient conflict resolution locally inside distributed parameter buckets for scalable multilingual LLM fine-tuning.
LJmbUpmei7.problem: Standard multilingual LLM fine-tuning suffers from negative cross-lingual interference, while global multi-objective optimization (MOO) requires materializing full per-language gradient vectors.
LJmbUpmei7.method: Bucket-Level MOO runs gradient-based MOO solvers independently within each parameter bucket of distributed training, eliminating full-gradient materialization. The authors define bucketwise Pareto stationarity and prove descent and convergence for representative variants.
LJmbUpmei7.key_idea: Partitions gradient-based multi-objective conflict resolution into distributed parameter buckets so multilingual updates avoid materializing full per-objective gradients.
LJmbUpmei7.evidence: Evaluated across multiple LLM backbones, three MOO algorithms, and up to 32 languages on two GPUs, including unseen-language transfer and memory benchmarks.
LJmbUpmei7.claimed_gains: Improves multilingual performance over standard fine-tuning by up to 4.3 points while scaling to 32 languages on two GPUs.
LJmbUpmei7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical memory savings (~29% peak memory reduction) that make MOO feasible for distributed multilingual LLM fine-tuning.
LJmbUpmei7.main_concern: Reviewers note limited theoretical/methodological novelty over prior layer-wise/partitioned MOO (e.g., GradVac, Recon) and missing direct empirical comparisons against those methods.

AoAHacnsHt.one_liner: Develops two-level dynamical mean-field theory tracking coupled bulk and outlier weight spectra during neural network training.
AoAHacnsHt.problem: Standard spiked random-matrix analyses assume independence between spike directions and the random bulk, failing to describe weight spectra during SGD training.
AoAHacnsHt.method: The authors formulate a two-level dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for spiked ensembles with bulk-dependent spikes and apply it to infinite-width nonlinear networks and proportional high-dimensional deep linear networks. They also analyze a toy model with extensive output channels to explain spectral bulk restructuring.
AoAHacnsHt.key_idea: Tracks coupled bulk and outlier singular-value dynamics in wide neural networks using a two-level dynamical mean-field theory.
AoAHacnsHt.evidence: Theoretical derivations for mean-field/muP nonlinear and deep linear networks plus a toy model and observations on ImageNet classification and GPT language modeling.
AoAHacnsHt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling dependence between learned spikes and the random bulk via two-level DMFT addresses a hard theoretical problem.
AoAHacnsHt.main_concern: Reviewers criticize poor readability and unclear organization, with one reviewer raising a major attribution issue regarding uncited prior work.

vThENskjCW.one_liner: Trains LoRA ensembles for LLM post-training using an alpha-Renyi variational objective that induces specialist routing.
vThENskjCW.problem: Standard single-point LLM post-training compresses heterogeneous and conflicting supervision into averaged behavior without epistemic uncertainty estimates.
vThENskjCW.method: The authors formulate an alpha-Renyi variational objective interpolating between variational Bayes and predictively oriented posteriors, and apply it to train an ensemble of LoRA adapters over a frozen base model with soft example routing.
vThENskjCW.key_idea: Optimizes a LoRA ensemble under an alpha-Renyi variational objective whose responsibility scores softly route conflicting examples to specialized adapters.
vThENskjCW.evidence: Includes local stability theory (Proposition 3) and pilot LLM post-training experiments on two tasks.
vThENskjCW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the theoretical local stability analysis showing when misspecification favors posterior spread without explicit gating.
vThENskjCW.main_concern: Reviewers find the objective and theory closely follow prior alpha-divergence and PrO work, and note that limited pilot experiments show higher disagreement without demonstrating downstream accuracy or calibration gains.

fXBhoohODi.one_liner: Achieves permutation and positive-rescaling equivariance in LP graph neural networks via smooth energy-based canonicalization.
fXBhoohODi.problem: Exact rescaling-equivariant GNNs for linear programs must discard essential LP coefficients, while existing solvers ignore positive rescaling symmetries.
fXBhoohODi.method: The authors prove every LP admits a canonical representative under positive rescaling, compute it via smooth unconstrained energy optimization, apply a permutation-equivariant GNN, and map predictions back to original coordinates.
fXBhoohODi.key_idea: Maps each LP to a unique canonical representative via smooth unconstrained optimization before applying a permutation-equivariant GNN and inverting the scaling.
fXBhoohODi.evidence: Theoretical proofs of canonicalization existence and equivariance are paired with empirical LP solution prediction experiments using HiGHS labels.
fXBhoohODi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the theoretical analysis of positive rescaling symmetry and LP-specific canonicalization as thorough and well-motivated.
fXBhoohODi.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical significance on small/medium LPs, integration into MILP solvers, and measuring error against a single HiGHS optimal solution when multiple optima exist.

R2h3tLFziY.one_liner: Denoises latent pairwise distances in metric measure spaces via observable neighborhood clustering and cluster-to-cluster averaging.
R2h3tLFziY.problem: Recovering latent pairwise distances from noisy monotone observations without assuming coordinates, curvature, or fixed dimension lacks near-linear-time guarantees.
R2h3tLFziY.method: Under lower volume-growth bounds, the algorithm constructs controlled-radius clusters from internal similarity and estimates distances via independent cluster-to-cluster averaging, alongside a KL folding lower bound.
R2h3tLFziY.key_idea: Builds controlled-radius clusters from noisy similarity observations and averages cluster-to-cluster scores to denoise latent distances.
R2h3tLFziY.evidence: Theoretical runtime and information-theoretic bounds are paired with controlled simulations on 1,200 sampled points on an interval and a branching metric tree.
R2h3tLFziY.claimed_gains: With 1,200 sampled points, simulations reduce normalized mean absolute error from 0.107 to 0.015 on an interval and from 0.112 to 0.025 on a branching metric tree.
R2h3tLFziY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the coordinate-free neighborhood construction under weak lower-mass assumptions theoretically interesting.
R2h3tLFziY.main_concern: One reviewer provides a counterexample falsifying Corollary 3.2(3), while others note exponential dependence on shrinking resolution and unclear practical motivation.

AS1udqfJFu.one_liner: Partitions graphs via degree-normalized neighborhood preservation for SISA-style shard unlearning with training-free entropy-filtered aggregation.
AS1udqfJFu.problem: Applying SISA-style graph partitioning for exact unlearning severs edges and disrupts local node neighborhoods that GNN message passing relies on.
AS1udqfJFu.method: LENS introduces a graph partitioning objective that preserves node neighborhoods relative to node degree, paired with an optimization strategy to form balanced shards. At inference, it combines shard predictions using a training-free aggregation scheme based on entropy filtering and adaptive temperature scaling.
AS1udqfJFu.key_idea: Degree-weighted neighborhood-preserving graph partitioning for shard training combined with training-free entropy-filtered shard aggregation.
AS1udqfJFu.evidence: Evaluated across multiple standard GNN backbones and datasets against retraining-based graph unlearning baselines.
AS1udqfJFu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preserving neighborhoods relative to node degree is well-motivated for GNNs and that LENS is clearly presented with strong empirical results.
AS1udqfJFu.main_concern: Reviewers note missing ablations isolating the partitioning objective from training/aggregation changes, lack of non-retraining approximate unlearning baselines, and limited novelty beyond SISA.

5cE5OuOKoq.one_liner: Audits MoE unlearning via Worst-Route Forget Efficacy over counterfactual expert routes and trains unlearning against those routes.
5cE5OuOKoq.problem: MoE unlearning methods can appear to forget target knowledge under default expert routing while leaving the knowledge recoverable through alternative experts.
5cE5OuOKoq.method: The authors expose off-route recovery via counterfactual routing and propose Worst-Route Forget Efficacy (WRFE), measuring maximum forget-set recovery across an audited family of expert routes. They also introduce RExU to mitigate off-route recovery by optimizing unlearning across those counterfactual routes (abstract truncated).
5cE5OuOKoq.key_idea: Auditing and training MoE unlearning over counterfactual expert-routing configurations to prevent knowledge recovery via unedited experts.
5cE5OuOKoq.evidence: Experiments on MoE unlearning benchmarks including WMDP-Cyber across multiple base unlearning algorithms (GA, NPO, RMU, SEUF).
5cE5OuOKoq.claimed_gains: On WMDP-Cyber, GA+SEUF lowers natural-route FE by 10.22 percentage points (from 36.79% to 26.57%), yet bypassing the edited expert raises FE by 11.33 percentage points to 37.90%.
5cE5OuOKoq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing off-route knowledge recovery in MoEs and introducing the WRFE audit metric are important and convincingly demonstrated.
5cE5OuOKoq.main_concern: Reviewers note tight coupling between RExU's training routes and WRFE's audit family without out-of-family route generalization tests, plus overclaiming knowledge removal versus path suppression.

cEWctQOQL4.one_liner: Iteratively optimizes complementary Text-to-SQL agent skills on residual failures of the existing skill ensemble without fine-tuning.
cEWctQOQL4.problem: Text-to-SQL ensembles using stochastic decoding or heuristic prompt variants suffer from correlated failures that limit Pass@K.
cEWctQOQL4.method: DivSkill-SQL builds a training-free ensemble of agentic Text-to-SQL skills by iteratively optimizing each new skill prompt on the residual failure examples missed by the current ensemble. This directly targets each skill's marginal contribution to Pass@K.
cEWctQOQL4.key_idea: Sequentially optimizing agentic prompt skills on the residual failure examples of prior skills to maximize marginal Pass@K.
cEWctQOQL4.evidence: Evaluated on Spider2-Lite (Snowflake, BigQuery, SQLite) and BIRD-Critic using Opus-4.6 and GPT-5.4.
cEWctQOQL4.claimed_gains: Improves selected accuracy on Spider2-Lite by up to +11.1 points on Snowflake and +8.3 on BigQuery over the strongest ensemble baseline, transfers to BIRD-Critic (+2.6 pts), and reduces hallucinated schema references and function calls by up to 3x.
cEWctQOQL4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizing complementary skills on residual failures is intuitive and yields strong empirical gains on Text-to-SQL benchmarks.
cEWctQOQL4.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental novelty over boosted prompt ensembles, missing ablations isolating residual optimization from other prompt optimizers, and high inference cost from pairwise LLM judges.

bVEhiwv1mQ.one_liner: Projects frozen VAE tokens onto a fixed-radius sphere, lightly finetunes the decoder, and trains spherical flow matching along slerp arcs.
bVEhiwv1mQ.problem: Pretrained VAE latent spaces are optimized for reconstruction rather than generative geometry, where linear flow-matching paths cut through low-density interiors instead of shell-like latent distributions.
bVEhiwv1mQ.method: The authors project each frozen VAE latent token onto a fixed-radius sphere, lightly finetune the decoder to reconstruct from spherical tokens, and train spherical flow matching along geodesic slerp arcs.
bVEhiwv1mQ.key_idea: Normalizing frozen VAE latents onto a sphere with lightweight decoder adaptation and training Riemannian flow matching along slerp trajectories.
bVEhiwv1mQ.evidence: Evaluated on class-conditional ImageNet-256 across three tokenizer families (including FLUX.2 and REPA-E FLUX.1) and SiT-B/XL backbones.
bVEhiwv1mQ.claimed_gains: On ImageNet-256 with FLUX.2 SiT-B/2, reduces FID from 26.35 to 20.55 under a 50-update sampling protocol and reaches FID=30 in ~2.2x fewer flow-training steps.
bVEhiwv1mQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the spherical latent adaptation is simple, architecture-agnostic, and well-supported by ImageNet-256 ablations.
bVEhiwv1mQ.main_concern: Reviewers flag substantial overlap with prior work (Geometry-Aware Image Flow Matching), shrinking gains with scale or longer training, and lack of text-to-image or higher-resolution evaluation.

sEr8vZxUf0.one_liner: Trains adaptive RGB-geometry gating on synthetic texture-swapped 3D scenes with teacher routing distillation and feature invariance.
sEr8vZxUf0.problem: Indoor 3D semantic segmentation models over-rely on RGB color shortcuts and fail when misleading textures contradict valid point-cloud geometry.
sEr8vZxUf0.method: Structured Texture Swapping (STS) constructs paired clean and texture-swapped training scenes by copying donor RGB patches across classes. A Geometry-Texture Interaction Gated Unit (GT-IGU) predicts per-point, per-channel fusion weights regularized by Candidate-Oracle Routing Distillation (CORD) and Structure-Aware Texture-Swapping Invariance (SA-TSI).
sEr8vZxUf0.key_idea: Training per-point RGB-geometry gates on cross-class texture-swapped point clouds with oracle routing distillation and swapped-feature invariance.
sEr8vZxUf0.evidence: Evaluated on S3DIS and ScanNetV2 with PointNeXt and PTv3 under clean, texture-conflict, corruption, and cross-domain settings.
sEr8vZxUf0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing RGB texture shortcuts via synthetic texture-swapped interventions is well-motivated and improves robustness across datasets and backbones.
sEr8vZxUf0.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the method learns genuine adaptive fusion rather than simply suppressing RGB in favor of geometry, and note a missing geometry-only baseline on appearance-corruption tests.

3fAUdr7OXG.one_liner: Extends KBQA logical-form RL with Search_Web and Combine actions and action-aware GRPO credit assignment to recover missing facts.
3fAUdr7OXG.problem: Real-world knowledge graphs are incomplete, causing executable KBQA logical forms to fail even when semantically correct, while retrieved text snippets remain transient and hard to reuse.
3fAUdr7OXG.method: IKBQA-R1 formulates incomplete KBQA as a multi-turn MDP adding Search_Web and Combine actions that ground retrieved evidence into executable logical forms. It initializes the policy via Referenced Rejection Sampling and multi-turn SFT, then trains with GRPO using action-aware token-level credit assignment aligned to gold action anchors.
3fAUdr7OXG.key_idea: Integrating external web evidence directly into executable KBQA logical forms via Search_Web/Combine actions trained with action-aware GRPO credit assignment.
3fAUdr7OXG.evidence: Evaluated on two newly constructed incomplete KBQA benchmarks using Llama-3.1-8B distilled from DeepSeek-V4-Flash trajectories.
3fAUdr7OXG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding external evidence into executable logical-form operations for traceable reasoning is well-motivated and effective on the proposed benchmarks.
3fAUdr7OXG.main_concern: Reviewers note that Search_Web queries a clean offline cache built from hidden-fact annotations without retrieval distractors, and the pipeline heavily inherits from KBQA-R1 and teacher distillation.

kZhUQj0gii.one_liner: Propagates genomic sequence uncertainty into biomedical knowledge-graph phenotype distributions via temperature-conditioned path energies.
kZhUQj0gii.problem: Connecting variant-level genomic foundation model predictions to phenotype hypotheses lacks a way to propagate predictive uncertainty through structured reasoning without patient-level phenotype supervision.
kZhUQj0gii.method: The authors propose an uncertainty-conditioned path-energy framework where a learned energy scores admissible gene-disease-phenotype routes, upstream query uncertainty controls the target temperature, and path probabilities aggregate into phenotype distributions. Exact normalization over enumerable candidates is used to validate a Hastings-corrected learned revision sampler.
kZhUQj0gii.key_idea: Maps genomic sequence predictive uncertainty to the temperature of a learned path-energy distribution over gene-disease-phenotype routes, sampled via a Hastings-corrected revision operator.
kZhUQj0gii.evidence: Evaluations on AlzKB and Hetionet with uncertainty-entropy correlation tests, ablations, exact enumeration checks, and gene-held-out masked-edge recovery across three edge masks.
kZhUQj0gii.claimed_gains: Phenotype-level entropy tracks upstream uncertainty with Spearman correlations of 0.951 on AlzKB and 0.878 on Hetionet; on held-out query genes, mean recall@10 reaches 0.206 across three edge masks, exceeding DistMult by 0.108.
kZhUQj0gii.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear presentation, inspectable path-level attribution, gene-held-out leakage audit, and direct validation of the sampler against exact enumeration.
kZhUQj0gii.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the uncertainty-entropy correlation is largely built into the temperature parameterization rather than proving clinical calibration, and that combining path energies with Metropolis-Hastings offers limited technical novelty.

5K96CWOjm5.one_liner: Decomposes pooled neural conceptors into average pole, mean-separation, and covariance-shape terms to explain contrast-dependent geometry.
5K96CWOjm5.problem: How conceptor representations in neural activation spaces depend on bipolar versus unipolar fitting contrasts and how their geometry affects downstream behavior is poorly understood.
5K96CWOjm5.method: The authors derive an exact decomposition of a centered pooled conceptor into an average pole filter, a mean-separation update, and a covariance-shape update. They evaluate reconstruction, amplification, probe correlation, subspace-removal overlap, and target-expression steering across models and concepts.
5K96CWOjm5.key_idea: Decomposes a centered pooled conceptor into average pole, mean-separation, and covariance-shape updates to analyze how contrast fitting shapes subspace geometry.
5K96CWOjm5.evidence: Exact algebraic decomposition plus experiments across five language models on sentiment, political leaning and stance, and depression expression, including generation steering against three mean-based controls.
5K96CWOjm5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clear, correct mathematical decomposition of pooled conceptors and the systematic evaluation across five model families and three concept types.
5K96CWOjm5.main_concern: Reviewers question whether classifier-margin gains translate to reliable generated text steering, note small or non-public toy datasets, and ask for clearer differentiation from prior conceptor work.

QhB5qsdLPn.one_liner: Probes LLM dialogue state representations and adds a readout-guided controller to edit actions without full belief-state prediction.
QhB5qsdLPn.problem: Instruction-tuned LLMs lack an explicit belief-state object and frequently fail to track and deploy updated constraints in multi-turn task-oriented dialogue.
QhB5qsdLPn.method: The authors probe and causally intervene on internal representations of eight LLMs to show that active structure is linearly readable before action while both current and superseded values remain accessible and causally active at their mentions. They build a lightweight state-action controller that selectively edits base-model actions using structural readouts.
QhB5qsdLPn.key_idea: Uses linear structural readouts from internal activations to selectively edit base-model dialogue actions instead of predicting a full intermediate belief state.
QhB5qsdLPn.evidence: Representation probing and causal interventions on eight instruction-tuned LLMs from four families on MultiWOZ and SGD, plus closed-loop controller evaluation on held-out MultiWOZ across five models.
QhB5qsdLPn.claimed_gains: On held-out MultiWOZ interaction across five models, the controller raises base-model exact-query accuracy from 0.318 to 0.621 and task success from 0.272 to 0.371 at negligible added cost.
QhB5qsdLPn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the broad, carefully controlled representation study across eight models and the clear distinction between readable information, causal influence, and behavioral competence.
QhB5qsdLPn.main_concern: Reviewers note that the benefit of internal activations over a supervised text-based classifier is not isolated, some probe details are missing, and Eq. (1)'s binary contrast is overinterpreted.

vp7AhQ0zGc.one_liner: Steers frozen flow-matching policies at test time by adding magnitude-rescaled critic gradients at estimated clean actions.
vp7AhQ0zGc.problem: Optimizing multi-step flow-matching and diffusion policies with RL is unstable via backpropagation through denoising, forcing distillation or repeated policy fine-tuning.
vp7AhQ0zGc.method: QPILOTS steers each denoising step of a flow policy at inference time without training the policy against the critic. At each step, it maps the noisy intermediate action to a clean-action estimate where the critic is reliable and adds the critic's action gradient rescaled to the base velocity magnitude.
vp7AhQ0zGc.key_idea: Guides every flow-policy denoising step by evaluating the critic gradient at a one-step clean-action estimate and adding it rescaled to the base velocity norm.
vp7AhQ0zGc.evidence: Evaluations on 50 standard offline-to-online RL tasks, steering a frozen pretrained VLA across 11 simulated manipulation tasks and one real-robot task, plus design ablations.
vp7AhQ0zGc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear, simple inference-time steering mechanism and the extensive experiments across 50 RL tasks and simulated/real VLA manipulation.
vp7AhQ0zGc.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty over existing critic-guided flow/clean-action estimation, lack of matched-NFE comparisons (with zero impact at 1-NFE), and gaps between the KL objective and practical implementation.

BLtMieC3Ds.one_liner: Certifies quantized language model generalization and simultaneous weight edits by aggregating PAC-Bayes prior mass over behaviorally equivalent implementations.
BLtMieC3Ds.problem: Weight-code generalization bounds ignore activation and KV-cache quantization effects, charging identical complexity for differently behaving deployments and separate penalties for behaviorally equivalent codes.
BLtMieC3Ds.method: Behavioral Capacity Certificates (BCC) aggregate prior mass over complete quantized implementations (weights, scales, activation and cache rules) sharing a bounded loss, with a break-even law accounting for validation cost. It supports a three-step workflow: forward-only bit-width screening, margin-certified simultaneous weight edits, and nonvacuous population-loss bounds.
BLtMieC3Ds.key_idea: Pools PAC-Bayes prior mass across complete quantized implementations that induce equivalent behavior and uses margin-certified cells to guarantee simultaneous output-head weight edits.
BLtMieC3Ds.evidence: Experiments on small complete decoders, GPT-2, OLMoE-1B-7B, and SmolLM2-1.7B on WikiText evaluating bit-width screening, certified pruning/sign-flip edits, and population-loss bounds.
BLtMieC3Ds.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that certifying shared behavioral equivalence rather than individual parameter codes—while accounting for independent validation—is well motivated and mathematically careful.
BLtMieC3Ds.main_concern: All three reviewers note that full-model nonvacuous bounds are only demonstrated on small decoders, while modern LLM experiments only certify restricted output-head edits on WikiText.

1L93HvqNTj.one_liner: Provides a deterministic, reward-hardened live-commerce benchmark and RL environment where agents run an online apparel store via 29 merchant tools.
1L93HvqNTj.problem: Most agentic benchmarks are static with arbitrary pass bars and terminal verdicts, failing to test long-horizon economic decision-making under asynchronous market shocks and reward hacking.
1L93HvqNTj.method: StoreBench places an agent on a production-grade commerce backend running a mid-size online apparel store through 29 merchant tools under an action-windowed simulated clock so model latency cannot affect time. It calibrates pass thresholds against scripted anchor policies, hardens rewards against known exploits, guarantees deterministic replay, and supports RL post-training.
1L93HvqNTj.key_idea: Couples a deterministic, action-clocked production commerce backend with anchor-calibrated pass bars and exploit-hardened rewards to evaluate and RL-train autonomous store-operator agents.
1L93HvqNTj.evidence: Evaluates seven frontier LLMs, human experts, and a scripted smart-triage heuristic across 11 scenarios (30–45 days) and a full simulated year over three seeds, plus GRPO post-training on Qwen3-27B.
1L93HvqNTj.claimed_gains: The best frontier model (DeepSeek-V4-Pro) passes 49% of task-seed cells versus 97% for the scripted smart-triage heuristic.
1L93HvqNTj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that running agents on a realistic production-grade commerce backend with reward-hacking audits and calibrated anchor policies is a compelling long-horizon setting.
1L93HvqNTj.main_concern: Reviewers highlight reproducibility and openness gaps (benchmark not open-sourced, under-explained construction), confounded full-year settings, and missing comparisons with related commerce benchmarks.

8oR5KqvwGo.one_liner: Benchmarks interactive U.S. tax-filing agents using 55 CPA-reviewed scenarios grounded in a 3,142-rule executable tax-law system.
8oR5KqvwGo.problem: Evaluating tax-filing agents is difficult because existing benchmarks lack measurable coverage of tax rules, reliable ground-truth returns, and fine-grained error attribution.
8oR5KqvwGo.method: The authors build TaxLab-Rule, an executable rule system of 3,142 field-level rules linked to official IRS sources, to generate gold returns, measure rule coverage, and trace agent errors. Using this system, they create 55 CPA-reviewed tax-year-2025 interactive scenarios where agents query a simulated taxpayer, consult offline IRS guidance, and complete tax forms.
8oR5KqvwGo.key_idea: Operationalizes 3,142 source-linked tax rules into an executable engine that generates gold returns, tracks benchmark coverage, and attributes interactive filing errors to specific rules.
8oR5KqvwGo.evidence: Evaluates nine frontier models on 55 CPA-reviewed interactive tax-year-2025 scenarios with rule-level error analysis.
8oR5KqvwGo.claimed_gains: The highest perfect filing accuracy among nine evaluated models, achieved by Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra, is 61.8%.
8oR5KqvwGo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that interactive tax filing grounded in an executable, source-linked rule system with CPA-reviewed scenarios is a practical and well-motivated benchmark.
8oR5KqvwGo.main_concern: Reviewers criticize reporting accuracy only over completed/graded cases (excluding timed-out and failed runs, which alters model rankings), as well as the small 55-scenario size and limited coverage of rule interactions.

FI1xJfiK7E.one_liner: Benchmarks coding agents on building complete installable repositories from scratch across 186 multi-language tasks with behavior-only hidden tests.
FI1xJfiK7E.problem: Evaluating end-to-end repository generation is difficult because tasks must require system-level design while testing externally observable behavior independent of a specific reference implementation.
FI1xJfiK7E.method: E2E-SWE provides 186 whole-repository generation tasks spanning 11 programming languages, where agents receive a natural-language specification and an empty workspace and are graded offline in fresh containers by hidden tests. Engineers and LLMs co-author implementation-independent specs and tests, followed by iterative autonomous agent audits to repair task defects.
FI1xJfiK7E.key_idea: Pairs implementation-independent natural-language specifications with from-scratch hidden behavioral test suites across 186 multi-language repositories, refined via rollout-driven defect audits.
FI1xJfiK7E.evidence: Evaluates 13 frontier models on 186 tasks across 11 languages, supplemented by a 12-gram memorization analysis and a defect audit.
FI1xJfiK7E.claimed_gains: Across 13 frontier models, pass@1 ranges from 11.7% to 67.7%.
FI1xJfiK7E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating whole-repository generation with from-scratch behavioral tests in isolated containers targets an important coding-agent capability.
FI1xJfiK7E.main_concern: Reviewers flag potential contamination/memorization inflation on top models, undocumented rollout-based specification repair and single-judge auditing, and unclear differentiation from existing repo-level benchmarks.

PJttRAc0R9.one_liner: Evaluates clinical LLM agents across multi-stage MIMIC-IV inpatient admissions by querying four role agents and scoring decisions and information gathering.
PJttRAc0R9.problem: Static medical benchmarks cannot evaluate how clinical agents incrementally gather heterogeneous patient information and commit to sequential, irreversible management decisions under uncertainty.
PJttRAc0R9.method: ClinEnv automatically converts real MIMIC-IV inpatient admissions into ordered multi-stage decision sequences under Longitudinal Inpatient Simulation. At each stage, the agent queries four specialized agents (patient, nurse, laboratory, history) before committing to medications, procedures, and diagnoses, scored via deterministic ontology-grounded matching and process metrics.
PJttRAc0R9.key_idea: Simulates multi-stage inpatient care from MIMIC-IV by requiring agents to query four role-specific EHR agents at each stage and scoring both ontology-matched decisions and query behavior.
PJttRAc0R9.evidence: Evaluates seven LLMs on multi-stage inpatient admission cases automatically constructed from MIMIC-IV.
PJttRAc0R9.claimed_gains: The strongest of seven evaluated models reaches 0.31 decision F1, with models recovering discharge diagnoses at 0.51 F1 versus 0.17 F1 for management actions.
PJttRAc0R9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that moving clinical LLM evaluation beyond static snapshots to automated multi-stage interactive EHR simulation is an impactful direction.
PJttRAc0R9.main_concern: Reviewers question clinical realism and transferability—since agents only query LLM-simulated roles over fixed retrospective records and legitimate practice variation may be penalized—and note missing comparisons with existing interactive EHR benchmarks.

Z8vI7QQO0Z.one_liner: Empirically measures minimal Transformer width and depth for exact factual memorization via Bayesian hyperparameter search on synthetic triples.
Z8vI7QQO0Z.problem: Prior studies found linear scaling between memorized facts and model parameters, leaving open whether optimal training and architecture choices yield tighter memorization capacity scaling.
Z8vI7QQO0Z.method: Using extensive Bayesian hyperparameter optimization across 12 synthetic dataset sizes of random independent (subject, relation, object) triples, the authors find the smallest Transformer that achieves exact memorization. They fit functional forms to minimum width and depth and evaluate them with lack-of-fit F-tests.
Z8vI7QQO0Z.key_idea: Uses per-scale Bayesian hyperparameter optimization to identify minimal Transformer widths for exact memorization of random triples, finding logarithmic width growth in fact count.
Z8vI7QQO0Z.evidence: Three-seed experiments across 12 dataset sizes (N = 24 to 49,920 random triples) with lack-of-fit F-tests and parameter accounting separating embedding and non-embedding weights.
Z8vI7QQO0Z.claimed_gains: Across N = 24 to 49,920 facts, minimum width fits d_min = 2.818 log(N + 98.3) - 10.64 without rejection by a lack-of-fit F-test, whereas all other tested forms including power-law are rejected.
Z8vI7QQO0Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the controlled synthetic setup, exhaustive hyperparameter search, statistical testing, and transparent parameter accounting are carefully executed.
Z8vI7QQO0Z.main_concern: Reviewers point out that when embedding parameters—which grow with dataset size—are included, capacity is ~2.04–2.19 bits per total parameter, matching prior linear scaling rather than beating it.

oWhMM8gzUP.one_liner: Forecasts multivariate time series by adaptively calibrating learned periodic templates along temporal and value dimensions before 2D convolutional fusion.
oWhMM8gzUP.problem: Fixed periodic representations in multivariate time-series forecasters fail when the timing (phase) and magnitude of recurring cycles shift across changing contexts.
oWhMM8gzUP.method: PeriCal learns input-conditioned calibration factors to resample and rescale periodic templates along both temporal and value dimensions via cyclic interpolation. It then integrates the calibrated periodic prior with local observations using two-dimensional convolution.
oWhMM8gzUP.key_idea: Applies input-conditioned continuous temporal-offset resampling and value-scaling calibration to learned periodic templates before fusing them with local observations via 2D convolution.
oWhMM8gzUP.evidence: Evaluated on 11 real-world multivariate time-series benchmarks (including PEMS traffic datasets and ETT) with component ablations and calibration visualizations.
oWhMM8gzUP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating temporal and value calibration of periodic priors is intuitive, lightweight, and supported by ablations.
oWhMM8gzUP.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty and a missing comparison to the closely related GTR method, mixed gains over baselines without significance tests, and unverified evidence that learned factors reflect true phase/amplitude shifts.

uRxy4zRR8S.one_liner: Iteratively selects SFT data by combining coarse data-centric filtering with token-probability-partitioned model-aware scoring feedback.
uRxy4zRR8S.problem: Static data-centric SFT selectors ignore a model's evolving learning needs, while dynamic model-centric selectors are computationally expensive over large data pools.
uRxy4zRR8S.method: Dual-perspective Dynamic Data Selection (D²S) performs coarse candidate selection using static data scores, refines candidates with model-perspective scores, and feeds that model feedback back to guide subsequent data-centric selection rounds. For model scoring, Model-aware Scoring (MaS) partitions response tokens into important and unimportant groups by prediction probability and applies distinct criteria before aggregating to sample scores.
uRxy4zRR8S.key_idea: Closes the loop between cheap data-centric coarse filtering and probability-partitioned token-level model scoring (MaS) to dynamically adapt SFT data selection.
uRxy4zRR8S.evidence: Evaluated across three instruction-tuning data pools and two base models (LLaMA and Qwen) with runtime and component ablations.
uRxy4zRR8S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining cheap static filtering with dynamic model feedback is well motivated, reduces runtime over full model-centric selection, and achieves strong reported averages.
uRxy4zRR8S.main_concern: Reviewers flag unfair baseline comparisons (reproducing ADG in a stronger pipeline while copying other baselines' published numbers), unclear checkpoint/hyperparameter validation separation, and limited novelty over hybrid selectors like MoDS, LEAD, and UDS.

uCfM7mNoaG.one_liner: Proves K-frame delay suffices for joint rate-distortion optimality on K-order Markov sources and augments causal video codecs with lookahead modules.
uCfM7mNoaG.problem: Strictly causal neural video codecs ignore future frames, while approaching the joint-coding rate-distortion limit is commonly assumed to require impractical unbounded frame delay.
uCfM7mNoaG.method: Using clique factorization of Markov networks, the authors develop Graph-Factored Sequential Coding (GFSC) and prove that a K-frame delay achieves joint-coding rate-distortion optimality for general K-order Markov sources in a high-resolution regime. They instantiate GFSC as plug-and-play lookahead neural modules augmenting existing causal codecs without altering their core architectures.
uCfM7mNoaG.key_idea: Uses Markov-network clique factorization to show K-frame lookahead attains joint rate-distortion optimality for K-order Markov sources, instantiated via lightweight lookahead modules on causal codecs.
uCfM7mNoaG.evidence: Rate-distortion theoretical proof plus empirical evaluations augmenting three neural video codecs (DCVC, VCT, DHVC) across multiple datasets and delay budgets K=1,2,3.
uCfM7mNoaG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the Markov-network rate-distortion theory for limited-delay coding is solid and the plug-and-play augmentation consistently improves BD-rate across codecs.
uCfM7mNoaG.main_concern: Reviewers note a disconnect between the theoretical clique-wise auxiliary variables and the practical temporal-attention implementation, missing latency/FLOPs overhead measurements, and unclear advantages over simpler future-frame fusion.

KgaVfMC7xq.one_liner: Benchmarks web agents on autonomously reconstructing executable university curriculum rule systems across 735 worlds from 111 institutions.
KgaVfMC7xq.problem: Web agents are rarely evaluated on whether they can synthesize scattered institutional web policies into complete, executable rule systems and accurately judge when reconstruction is complete.
KgaVfMC7xq.method: CurriculumWorldBench collects 735 curriculum worlds from 111 universities across controlled website layouts and frozen institutional sites. It evaluates agents on four decomposed metrics—vocabulary recovery, obligation coverage, executable semantic equivalence (via counterexample search), and calibrated completion claims—supported by mutation and alignment audits of the evaluator.
KgaVfMC7xq.key_idea: Evaluates autonomous web agents on reconstructing executable degree-requirement rule systems across four decomposed metrics—vocabulary, obligation coverage, semantic equivalence, and completion calibration.
KgaVfMC7xq.evidence: Evaluates multiple LLMs and scaffolds across 735 curriculum worlds (including a 63-world confirmatory tier from 18 institutions), with evaluator mutation and alignment audits.
KgaVfMC7xq.claimed_gains: Even with high course recovery, agents omit 63,432 of 84,036 decidable obligations.
KgaVfMC7xq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the four-layer evaluation decomposition (especially calibrated completion claims) and thorough mutation/alignment validation of the evaluator are strong benchmark practices.
KgaVfMC7xq.main_concern: Reviewers note internal inconsistencies in Table 1 (Exec. Recall + Omission exceeding 100%), a small underpowered confirmatory tier (63 worlds across 18 schools), and a narrow domain whose generality beyond existing web/rule benchmarks is unclear.

yFpbjSErt0.one_liner: Combines a dynamic knowledge-graph belief state, reactive fast actions, reflection switching, and twisted SMC slow planning for partially observable agents.
yFpbjSErt0.problem: Conditioning LLM agents on full or summarized histories under partial observability introduces redundant context that misleads belief inference and planning.
yFpbjSErt0.method: NeSyFS maintains a dynamically updated knowledge graph as an explicit belief state shared across all modules. A fast module takes reactive actions checked by a reflection module, which switches to a slow uncertainty-aware planner following twisted sequential Monte Carlo (TSMC) when reactive actions repeatedly fail.
yFpbjSErt0.key_idea: Grounds fast reactive actions, reflection-based escalation, and twisted sequential Monte Carlo slow planning on a shared dynamically updated knowledge-graph belief state.
yFpbjSErt0.evidence: Evaluated across three benchmarks using GPT-5 and Llama model families.
yFpbjSErt0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unified knowledge-graph belief representation and failure-triggered fast-slow deliberation coherent and supported by positive benchmark results.
yFpbjSErt0.main_concern: Reviewers note that the slow TSMC module adds almost no gain on stronger models (GPT-5), the TSMC implementation is unclear, ablations are missing, and components overlap heavily with AriGraph and SwiftSage.

yDqr7huXPs.one_liner: Red-teams diffusion language models across prompt and canvas surfaces, showing multi-turn escalation alone underperforms hybrid infilling attacks.
yDqr7huXPs.problem: Multi-turn jailbreak vulnerability and its underlying mechanism have not been systematically evaluated on diffusion language models (dLLMs).
yDqr7huXPs.method: DRIFT formalizes dLLM red-teaming over two attack surfaces—the conversational prompt surface and the pre-denoising response canvas surface—and evaluates ten attacks (five existing, five constructed hybrids combining multi-turn escalation with canvas infilling such as Crescendo x PAD).
yDqr7huXPs.key_idea: Decomposes dLLM multi-turn jailbreaks into prompt-surface escalation (suppressing refusal opening) and canvas-surface infilling (forcing harmful continuation).
yDqr7huXPs.evidence: Evaluated on four open-weight dLLMs and three autoregressive LLMs across six red-teaming benchmarks.
yDqr7huXPs.claimed_gains: Crescendo x PAD reaches 78.2% ASR, whereas multi-turn escalation alone reaches only 29.7% on dLLMs vs 39.9% on arLLMs and 61.2% for single-turn dLLM attacks (cutting refusal mass from >=0.65 to <=0.05; multi-turn adds 1.4-17 points to infilling).
yDqr7huXPs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize multi-turn safety of diffusion LLMs as a timely problem and appreciate the unified prompt-and-canvas surface framing across multiple models and benchmarks.
yDqr7huXPs.main_concern: Reviewers point out limited novelty because the strongest attacks simply combine existing multi-turn and infilling methods, and note unfair dLLM-vs-arLLM comparisons lacking prefill attacks on arLLMs.

BxfO5mKuLK.one_liner: Penalizes score disagreement across candidate permutations during SFT to stabilize batched LLM scorer decisions without losing ranking quality.
BxfO5mKuLK.problem: Batched LLM scorers with equal ranking quality produce substantially different threshold, reader, or preference-pair decisions when candidates are reordered.
BxfO5mKuLK.method: Order-Consistency SFT (OC-SFT) fine-tunes LLM scorers with an explicit consistency penalty minimizing disagreement between each candidate's scores across different prompt permutations, rather than relying on prompt-time interventions or order-averaged distillation.
BxfO5mKuLK.key_idea: Adds a cross-permutation score-disagreement penalty during SFT so batched LLM scorers assign order-invariant scores across candidate reorderings.
BxfO5mKuLK.evidence: Evaluated across passage reranking, response ranking, and multi-document QA on 12 base models and multiple retrievers with pool-replacement transfer tests.
BxfO5mKuLK.claimed_gains: Five trained scorers within 0.010 nDCG@10 overlap by only 0.66-0.84 when reordered, while a single OC-SFT permutation achieves higher retained-set overlap than ten averaged off-the-shelf permutations.
BxfO5mKuLK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the conceptual reframing highlighting decision stability beyond ranking metrics and the thorough multi-task, multi-model experimental validation.
BxfO5mKuLK.main_concern: Reviewers note that end-to-end downstream impact on RAG or RLHF training is never measured, and that OC-SFT mathematically resembles re-weighted permutation augmentation favored by hyperparameter tuning.

hO44HxFGZI.one_liner: Adapts frozen LLM agents at test time using progress-relative action credits and conditional sequence replay in final budget episodes.
hO44HxFGZI.problem: Experience-based test-time LLM agents keep reinforcing actions that plateau at repeated scores and risk regression when exploring in final budget episodes.
hO44HxFGZI.method: EARN decays action credits for repeatedly attained scores while assigning larger credits to action segments achieving higher scores to reweight LLM-proposed action probabilities. In the final episodes, it conditionally replays stored action sequences whenever contexts match and actions remain valid, bypassing LLM candidate generation.
hO44HxFGZI.key_idea: Decays credits for repeated score plateaus, boosts higher-score segments to reweight frozen-LLM actions, and conditionally replays matched action routes in final episodes.
hO44HxFGZI.evidence: Evaluated across Jericho, ScienceWorld, and Crafter over 33 task-budget settings using final-four-episode average scores and Jericho ablations.
hO44HxFGZI.claimed_gains: Achieves the best final-four-episode average score in 31 of 33 task-budget settings (including ties) and bypasses 78.9-86.3% of candidate-generation calls in the final four Jericho episodes.
hO44HxFGZI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that overcoming score plateaus and consolidating routes without parameter updates is intuitive, well-motivated, and validated across three environments.
hO44HxFGZI.main_concern: Reviewers criticize activating route replay specifically during the final-four-episode evaluation window (tailoring to the metric), missing record-and-replay baselines (e.g., AgentRR), and unclear baseline feedback parity.

fgpKZw2ryE.one_liner: Enables unbiased tree-based speculative decoding for watermarked LLMs by deterministically partitioning the vocabulary across draft branches.
fgpKZw2ryE.problem: Tree-based speculative decoding breaks LLM watermark detection because multiple draft branches draw from different pseudorandom sources.
fgpKZw2ryE.method: The method deterministically partitions the vocabulary into disjoint subsets and samples one draft token per subset to form distinct tree branches. Because an observed token uniquely identifies its subset, only that draft branch and residual sampling remain as possible pseudorandom sources.
fgpKZw2ryE.key_idea: Deterministically partitions the vocabulary into disjoint per-branch subsets so each observed token narrows pseudorandom watermark ambiguity to one draft branch or residual sampling.
fgpKZw2ryE.evidence: Proves output-distribution preservation and acceptance-rate lower bounds, with experiments on Gumbel-max and SynthID watermarks including EAGLE-style draft heads.
fgpKZw2ryE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practical, the presentation clear, and the deterministic vocabulary partitioning a simple way to resolve multi-branch watermark ambiguity.
fgpKZw2ryE.main_concern: Reviewers note that watermark TPR structurally degrades as tree width k increases without practical throughput-detectability guidance, novelty over KGW partitioning and standard tree decoding is incremental, and detection speed is unreported.

BKBpZ7ZhQZ.one_liner: Analyzes sparse linear regression under shuffled differential privacy using non-interactive bounds and a two-round interactive heavy-hitter protocol.
BKBpZ7ZhQZ.problem: Private sparse linear regression exhibits a large accuracy gap between central and local differential privacy, and its limits under shuffled differential privacy are unclear.
BKBpZ7ZhQZ.method: The authors prove an l2-norm lower bound and propose a matching-regime algorithm for non-interactive shuffled DP, then introduce a two-round interactive user-level protocol. The interactive algorithm recovers support via a heavy-hitter step before estimating parameters, complemented by a user-level score-attack lower bound.
BKBpZ7ZhQZ.key_idea: Recovers sparse support in one shuffled heavy-hitter round before estimating parameters in a second round to remove polynomial dimension dependence.
BKBpZ7ZhQZ.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower l2-norm estimation error bounds for non-interactive and interactive user-level shuffled differential privacy protocols.
BKBpZ7ZhQZ.claimed_gains: Proves a non-interactive lower bound of Omega(sqrt(dk)/(n*epsilon)), a non-interactive upper bound of O_tilde(sqrt(k/n) + d*sqrt(k)/(n*epsilon)), and a two-round user-level upper bound of O_tilde(sqrt(k/(nm)) + k/(n*sqrt(m)*epsilon)) without polynomial dependence on d.
BKBpZ7ZhQZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly presented and provides rigorous theory separating single-round sample-level and multi-round user-level shuffled DP.
BKBpZ7ZhQZ.main_concern: Reviewers note restrictive per-user sample size and signal-strength assumptions in the interactive regime, a remaining polynomial gap in the non-interactive bounds, and unclear practical relevance of SDP.

QWTWueRv5S.one_liner: Applies post-training partial linearization to compare fixed-depth and variable-depth networks and isolate residual connections' generalization bias.
QWTWueRv5S.problem: Direct comparisons between residual and feedforward networks confound architectural inductive bias with optimization and trainability differences.
QWTWueRv5S.method: The authors provide a theoretical comparison of ResNet and feedforward function spaces and introduce a post-training partial-linearization setup. This procedure molds an already trained network into either a fixed-depth or variable-depth architecture at comparable nonlinear complexity to isolate generalization effects.
QWTWueRv5S.key_idea: Partially linearizes an already trained network into fixed-depth or variable-depth subgraphs to compare generalization without confounding trainability.
QWTWueRv5S.evidence: A theoretical function-space argument and post-training partial-linearization experiments comparing fixed-depth and variable-depth architectures.
QWTWueRv5S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the research question is important and the variable- versus fixed-depth framing with post-training linearization is a useful approach.
QWTWueRv5S.main_concern: Reviewers criticize weak experimental breadth and misalignment between the post-training linearization test and proving that variable depth drives generalization.

MyuNAxAWyv.one_liner: Introduces BC-Bench and trains MLLMs for sequential brick selection and pose estimation using demonstrations, world feedback, and synthetic data.
MyuNAxAWyv.problem: Current multimodal LLMs struggle with fine-grained part selection and precise 3D pose estimation when assembling objects from diverse building blocks.
MyuNAxAWyv.method: The authors formulate brick assembly as sequential brick selection and 3D pose estimation and create BC-Bench to evaluate it. They propose Brick-Composer, which trains MLLMs using Human Design Sparks demonstrations, visual and physical World Feedback, and Synthetic Experience.
MyuNAxAWyv.key_idea: Trains MLLMs on sequential brick selection and 3D pose estimation by combining human demonstrations, physical world feedback, and synthetic assembly trajectories.
MyuNAxAWyv.evidence: Evaluations on BC-Bench across multiple MLLMs and two trained backbones accounting for interchangeable parts and rotational symmetries.
MyuNAxAWyv.claimed_gains: Brick-Composer improves brick selection accuracy by over three times and substantially reduces pose estimation error.
MyuNAxAWyv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diverse-part assembly task and BC-Bench metrics carefully capture symmetries and expose real MLLM failures.
MyuNAxAWyv.main_concern: Reviewers flag an inconsistent rotation-matrix row/column convention between prompts, unclear test-time ground-truth dependence in World Feedback, and 0% full-object assembly success.

WdW7PX8z5r.one_liner: Aligns variable modality subsets using SCORE, an adaptive weighted resultant-vector length measuring spherical concentration in contrastive learning.
WdW7PX8z5r.problem: Multi-vector similarity methods struggle to support both pairwise and joint retrieval across variable modality subsets within one shared embedding space.
WdW7PX8z5r.method: The authors propose SCORE, a multi-vector similarity based on the norm of a weighted resultant vector over normalized modality embeddings. Instance-pair-adaptive weights modulate each modality's contribution during contrastive training without extra fusion modules.
WdW7PX8z5r.key_idea: Computes multi-modality similarity as the spherical resultant-vector length of normalized embeddings weighted by instance-pair-adaptive weights.
WdW7PX8z5r.evidence: Theoretical geometric analysis and experiments on video-text retrieval (including MSR-VTT), clustering, classification, modality-gap analysis, and ablations.
