WdW7PX8z5r.claimed_gains: On MSR-VTT, SCORE reaches 55.8 R@1 for text-to-video/audio/subtitles retrieval and 54.0 R@1 for text-to-video retrieval.
WdW7PX8z5r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SCORE is geometrically well motivated, avoids extra fusion modules or expensive matrix operations, and supports unified pairwise and joint retrieval.
WdW7PX8z5r.main_concern: Reviewers note SCORE's square reduces to weighted all-pair cosine similarity without an all-pair cosine baseline, and shared-space evaluation details and downstream tasks are limited.

Okq5pCgmFS.one_liner: Distills behavioral traits into reasoning LLMs via trait-conditioned on-policy self-distillation with hard-sample progress guidance and outcome-aware gating.
Okq5pCgmFS.problem: Using reference solutions as privileged supervision is problem-specific, whereas general behavioral dispositions are rarely leveraged as reusable teaching signals for reasoning.
Okq5pCgmFS.method: The authors propose tau-OPSD, where a trait-conditioned self-teacher supplies dense token-level supervision on student trajectories without keeping trait prompts at inference. It adds hard-sample local-progress instructions for budget-exhausted rollouts and an outcome-aware stance gate using reference answers only for verification.
Okq5pCgmFS.key_idea: Conditions a self-teacher on reusable behavioral trait prompts to score student prefixes, gated by task-outcome consistency and hard-sample progress cues.
Okq5pCgmFS.evidence: Experiments on Qwen3 models (1.7B to 8B) across math reasoning benchmarks, abstention tasks, component ablations, and additional traits (planning, exploration).
Okq5pCgmFS.claimed_gains: Across Qwen3 1.7B to 8B, tau-OPSD leads compared methods in average math accuracy and improves abstention under insufficient evidence.
Okq5pCgmFS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree using reusable behavioral traits as privileged self-distillation supervision is a practical idea backed by consistent math and abstention gains across model scales.
Okq5pCgmFS.main_concern: Reviewers question whether gains truly come from behavioral traits rather than generic procedural instructions or outcome-aware gating, and flag test-set checkpoint selection bias.

vVmgGuIRyX.one_liner: Evaluates LLM tutors on misconception repair using learner proxies with compliance and cognitive-load controls across executable coding post-tests.
vVmgGuIRyX.problem: Existing LLM tutoring benchmarks use role-prompted LLM learners that are overly compliant, retain everything, and copy answers from context.
vVmgGuIRyX.method: The authors introduce CogTeachBench with 316 oracle-verified misconception-repair scenarios from post-cutoff LiveCodeBench problems. Simulated learners include an acceptance control (alpha) and a cognitive-load control (beta) calibrated on 557 student-rated segments, scored by four metrics (CBCS, AZS, PSQ, PCE).
vVmgGuIRyX.key_idea: Simulates learners with explicit compliance (alpha) and student-calibrated cognitive-load retention (beta) controls tested via executable post-teaching coding problems.
vVmgGuIRyX.evidence: Evaluation of five LLM tutors across learner model families and a dialogue-replay validation study with 36 undergraduates.
vVmgGuIRyX.claimed_gains: Across five tutors, CogTeachBench rankings match human post-test ordering (Spearman rho = 1.00, exact permutation p = 0.017) and transfer across learner families (rho = 0.90).
vVmgGuIRyX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark artifact is well engineered with post-cutoff executable tests and explicit, controllable tutoring constructs.
vVmgGuIRyX.main_concern: Reviewers note that whether the alpha/beta learner controls actually improve human correlation or model realistic information retention is not directly verified, and diagnostic accuracy is unmeasured.

q4MfqSWooC.one_liner: Retrains only a talking-head model's audio encoder with two-stage optimization and coupling-based layer selection to disrupt harmful-speech lip-sync.
q4MfqSWooC.problem: Existing defenses against harmful talking-head videos rely on per-input perturbations and ignore speech semantics, risking disruption of benign speech containing sensitive keywords.
q4MfqSWooC.method: The authors propose SyncEdit, a model-level defense that edits only the audio encoder while freezing downstream talking-head modules and needing no inference-time classifiers. It resolves gradient conflicts between harmful disruption and benign preservation via two-stage optimization and coupling-based layer selection.
q4MfqSWooC.key_idea: Edits selected audio-encoder layers via two-stage optimization to desynchronize lip motion for harmful speech while preserving benign and keyword-benign speech.
q4MfqSWooC.evidence: Experiments on four heterogeneous talking-head systems, ablations on training design, and a human study measuring perceived mouth match and credibility.
q4MfqSWooC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree distinguishing harmful semantics from keyword-containing benign speech is a meaningful formulation, and video-level plus human evaluations support the effect.
q4MfqSWooC.main_concern: Reviewers note missing quantitative comparisons against practical ASR or audio hate-speech classifiers, unmatched category data distributions, and under-verified ablations and adaptive attacks.

1BC0eYN2uS.one_liner: Replaces doubly stochastic Hyper-Connection mixers with single-marginal softmax matrices (osHC) to preserve depth stability while allowing stream amplification.
1BC0eYN2uS.problem: Enforcing both row and column stochasticity in Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections prevents streams from replicating, aggregating, or amplifying differences.
1BC0eYN2uS.method: The authors analyze one-sided stochastic constraints and propose One-Sided Hyper-Connections (osHC), replacing iterative Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization with a single softmax on either rows or columns. They instantiate four variants—two fixed-marginal and two switching marginals partway through depth—and prove spectral norm bounds.
1BC0eYN2uS.key_idea: Constrains residual stream mixing matrices with a single row- or column-wise softmax instead of doubly stochastic normalization, bounding product spectral norms by sqrt(n).
1BC0eYN2uS.evidence: Spectral-norm stability proofs and language model pretraining experiments across ten routing constructions, two corpora, and three scales (up to 354M parameters, n=4 streams).
1BC0eYN2uS.claimed_gains: osHC achieves the best validation loss in five of six pretraining settings and outperforms every doubly stochastic construction in all six.
1BC0eYN2uS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree osHC is simple to implement with a single softmax, clearly analyzed theoretically, and consistently improves validation loss over doubly stochastic baselines.
1BC0eYN2uS.main_concern: Reviewers note limited theoretical novelty beyond standard stochastic-matrix norms, proofs omitting attention/MLP/input-dependent router effects, and small experimental scale (n=4, up to 354M).

yG1s4ROb7j.one_liner: Predicts per-instance block sizes once after prefill using a learned policy to accelerate diffusion-based speculative decoding.
yG1s4ROb7j.problem: Diffusion-based speculative decoding uses a fixed block size for all inputs, which is suboptimal because optimal block sizes vary across samples.
yG1s4ROb7j.method: The authors observe that optimal block sizes cluster locally around the training block size and formulate block-size choice as a low-dimensional policy learning problem. BlockPilot uses prefill-stage representations to predict an instance-specific block size once per request without modifying the draft or target models.
yG1s4ROb7j.key_idea: Runs a one-shot classifier on prefill representations to pick a per-sample block size within a narrow neighborhood around the training block size.
yG1s4ROb7j.evidence: Experiments across multiple LLMs (including Qwen3-4B) and benchmarks comparing fixed block sizes and temperatures, plus predictor overhead measurements.
yG1s4ROb7j.claimed_gains: Achieves an acceptance length of 5.92 and a 4.20x speedup on Qwen3-4B.
yG1s4ROb7j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree BlockPilot is simple, easy to integrate with minimal online overhead, and beats fixed block sizes across tested models and temperatures.
yG1s4ROb7j.main_concern: Reviewers note modest gains over the best tuned fixed block size (not just the training size), high offline data-collection cost, limited novelty, and unclear end-to-end timing scripts.

n8QuaZwPIm.one_liner: Generates 3D RNA ligands via SE(3)-equivariant diffusion with protein-to-RNA transfer, glycosidic nucleobase correction, and dual-source adaptive sampling.
n8QuaZwPIm.problem: Structure-based small-molecule design for RNA is hindered by scarce RNA-ligand complex data and flexible binding pockets.
n8QuaZwPIm.method: The authors introduce RiboSBDD, an SE(3)-equivariant all-atom diffusion model pretrained on proteins and fine-tuned on RNA, coupled with differentiable glycosidic-bond (chi) nucleobase rotation correction and an adaptive sampler blending frozen protein and RNA proposals. They also curate RiboSBDDBench with 8,006 RNA pocket-ligand instances and grouped structural splits.
n8QuaZwPIm.key_idea: Transfers all-atom protein geometric priors to RNA diffusion while jointly denoising ligands with differentiable glycosidic nucleobase rotations and protein-RNA proposal resampling.
n8QuaZwPIm.evidence: Evaluations on RiboSBDDBench across 713 test pockets spanning protein-free receptors, unseen Murcko scaffolds, and unseen Rfam families, plus four-architecture transfer comparisons.
n8QuaZwPIm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree RiboSBDDBench with grouped structural splits and the unified protein-to-RNA transfer setup are valuable contributions for RNA drug design.
n8QuaZwPIm.main_concern: Reviewers flag excluded failed evaluations biasing cross-method comparisons, synthetic-only nucleobase rotation supervision, and confounded component ablations.

gSU4ogF4WV.one_liner: Deploys industrial ad-recommendation GNNs using LLM-constructed semantic edges, distributed EasyGraph/AngelGraph systems, and hybrid stream-batch serving.
gSU4ogF4WV.problem: Industrial advertising GNNs suffer from cold-start structural sparsity (over 34% of nodes with degree below five), hundred-billion-edge scale, and millisecond latency limits.
gSU4ogF4WV.method: The authors build TGNN, combining LLM-generated semantic edges (via RQ-VAE and Trie lookup) and cross-domain augmentation to densify sparse graphs with EasyGraph (distributed storage/sampling), AngelGraph (GNN training), and a hybrid stream-batch serving pipeline.
gSU4ogF4WV.key_idea: Augments sparse ad graphs with LLM-derived semantic edges and trains/serves 100B-edge GNNs via co-designed distributed graph storage, training, and stream-batch pipelines.
gSU4ogF4WV.evidence: Offline industrial and public (Yelp-2018) evaluations, ablations, and production online A/B tests on Tencent social and short-video advertising feeds (>2B nodes, >100B edges).
gSU4ogF4WV.claimed_gains: Online A/B tests increase overall GMV by 3.43% (4.80% for new ads) in social feeds and 2.77% (3.74% for new ads) in short-video feeds.
gSU4ogF4WV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree TGNN is an impressive end-to-end deployed system with rare production A/B evidence and strong cold-start densification results.
gSU4ogF4WV.main_concern: Reviewers question whether huge offline AUC gaps reflect weak or feature-mismatched baselines rather than GNN architecture gains, and note limited external verifiability and missing LLM cost breakdowns.

IuPwfSDEik.one_liner: Evaluates GUI world models' decision value via controlled interventions and introduces Direct Action Ranking without predicting future screens.
IuPwfSDEik.problem: It is unclear whether GUI world-model lookahead gains come from next-screen prediction itself or from the evaluator scoring candidate actions.
IuPwfSDEik.method: The authors run fixed-prediction evaluator interventions and propose Direct Action Ranking (DAR), a LoRA-tuned VLM that scores candidate actions directly from reference actions without generating future screens. They compare DAR against a prediction-augmented variant under matched supervision.
IuPwfSDEik.key_idea: Separates prediction from evaluation via matched-supervision Direct Action Ranking to measure whether predicted next screens add ranking signal.
IuPwfSDEik.evidence: Controlled offline AUROC comparisons, evaluator-presentation ablations, and online AndroidWorld evaluations across three proposers, two world models, and unseen apps.
IuPwfSDEik.claimed_gains: Without retraining, DAR improves AndroidWorld task success by 5.8-16.4 points across three proposers and outperforms prompted world-model lookahead.
IuPwfSDEik.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree isolating prediction from evaluation is a clean, insightful question and DAR delivers consistent online gains on AndroidWorld.
IuPwfSDEik.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the matched decision-value null result is offline AUROC only (never run online), uses one non-contrastive prediction injection format, and online comparisons pit trained DAR against zero-shot lookahead.

lzzM23NcIO.one_liner: MEMENTO scores KV-cache retention by re-feeding completed context chunks interleaved with decoding for query-agnostic multi-turn eviction.
lzzM23NcIO.problem: Query-dependent KV-cache eviction in multi-turn agentic inference discards context needed by later turns whose queries differ from the current turn.
lzzM23NcIO.method: MEMENTO is a training-free streaming eviction method that re-feeds each completed context chunk and uses the reread attention scores as query-agnostic retention credits. Rereading is interleaved with subsequent decoding in isolated batch rows of the same forward pass, supported by a geometric retrieval-cell error bound.
lzzM23NcIO.key_idea: Re-feeds completed context chunks in interleaved batch rows and uses the resulting self-reread attention to score query-agnostic KV-cache retention.
lzzM23NcIO.evidence: Theoretical geometric error analysis and multi-turn agent benchmarks including SWE-bench Verified on Muse-Glimmer-30B with decoding-speed measurements.
lzzM23NcIO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that query-agnostic KV retention for multi-turn agents is an important problem and that the SWE-bench Verified results (71.5% vs. 65.0% baseline) are strong.
lzzM23NcIO.main_concern: Reviewers identify a mismatch between the max-witness theory and averaged implementation, confounded global-vs-per-head budget comparisons, and missing end-to-end comparisons against query-dependent baselines like H2O, SnapKV, and PyramidKV.

nQwU8tPmKE.one_liner: Restricted Dynamic Hypergraphs represent AI-generated image sources as sparse combinations of reusable fingerprint atoms for open-set attribution.
nQwU8tPmKE.problem: Holistic generator fingerprints fail in open-set AI-generated image attribution because unseen generators often share architectural traces with known lineages.
nQwU8tPmKE.method: The authors propose compositional source fingerprints instantiated via a Restricted Dynamic Hypergraph (RdH), where latent fingerprint atoms induce hyperedges among images. Restricted activation builds compact image-specific atom combinations and degree-aware propagation suppresses broadly shared, low-selectivity atoms.
nQwU8tPmKE.key_idea: Models each generator as a sparse combination of reusable hypergraph fingerprint atoms with degree-aware propagation to suppress non-selective shared traces.
nQwU8tPmKE.evidence: Evaluated across five Cross-Era open-set attribution protocols (GenImage known, AIGI-Holmes unknown) with atom-masking and component ablations.
nQwU8tPmKE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that open-set AI-generated image attribution is timely and that reframing source signatures as combinations of reusable traces is an interesting hypothesis supported by ablations.
nQwU8tPmKE.main_concern: Reviewers point out that Cross-Era gains are confounded because all known sources come from GenImage and all unknown sources from AIGI-Holmes, and that fingerprint atoms lack a precise mathematical definition.

PSHrXIB1Va.one_liner: BeneRAG trains a black-box retrieval router with magnitude-weighted binary cross-entropy on paired no-retrieval versus RAG outcome gains.
PSHrXIB1Va.problem: Correctness-based selective retrieval triggers unnecessary RAG calls when an answer is wrong but retrieval fails to provide evidence that improves it.
PSHrXIB1Va.method: BeneRAG constructs offline benefit labels and magnitude weights by comparing paired closed-book and deployed RAG branch outcomes, then trains a router (DeBERTa) with magnitude-weighted binary cross-entropy. At inference, it routes using only the question, sampled no-retrieval answers, and verbalized confidence.
PSHrXIB1Va.key_idea: Trains a black-box router with magnitude-weighted BCE directly on whether executing the deployed RAG branch improves the answer over closed-book generation.
PSHrXIB1Va.evidence: Controlled 2x2 benefit-vs-correctness experiments across five seeds on TriviaQA, Natural Questions, and MuSiQue-Ans, plus GPT-4.1 semantic evaluation and unseen-generator transfer tests.
PSHrXIB1Va.claimed_gains: At a 50% exact retrieval budget, BeneRAG exceeds the correctness router by 4.06 F1 points (5-seed average); at validation-selected thresholds it reaches 0.4435 mean F1 versus 0.4283 for Always RAG at a 63.1% retrieval rate.
PSHrXIB1Va.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that predicting retrieval benefit rather than answer correctness is well-motivated and cleanly validated by the controlled 2x2 comparison.
PSHrXIB1Va.main_concern: Reviewers note fragile generalization—gains reverse when distractor ratios or retrievers change, fail on 3 of 5 unseen generators, require costly offline paired labeling, and mostly reflect question-only difficulty.

LPIl00WjZG.one_liner: LMBuild evaluates LLM agents generating buildable, functional 3D assemblies in a tool environment across four physical and structural levels.
LPIl00WjZG.problem: Existing 3D generation benchmarks judge visual or geometric appearance while ignoring structural soundness, joints, assembly sequences, and functional realizability.
LPIl00WjZG.method: LMBuild provides an interactive tool environment for retrieving, creating, and placing parts, a 50-object benchmark repurposing CAD datasets augmented with Wikipedia object knowledge, and a four-level evaluation covering structural soundness, functional affordance, design quality, and physical realization.
LPIl00WjZG.key_idea: Represents 3D objects as part-joint-material assembly sequences in a tool environment and scores LLM agents across structural, affordance, design, and physics levels.
LPIl00WjZG.evidence: Evaluates 30 domain-specific models, open-source LLMs, and frontier APIs on the 50-object core benchmark with retrieval-vs-creation analyses.
LPIl00WjZG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating buildability, joints, assembly order, and function beyond visual geometry is an important and substantial benchmark effort.
LPIl00WjZG.main_concern: Reviewers flag confounded model comparisons across different agent harnesses (CLI vs. tool loops), unvalidated affordance/realization proxy metrics (e.g., convex-hull simulation), small 50-object single-run scale, and unclear necessity of the 19-tool restriction.
